**115. `ccdargv.ts`'s mint site now freezes every argv, and the brand's own
disclosure is corrected to match (pre-merge fix round, finding 13S-F1).**
The brand's own comment, task 13S's report §6(3) and deviation 82(c) all
claimed the ONLY way past the `CcdArgv` brand was "a deliberate cast" — not
true as written. Three cast-free shapes launder an arbitrary argv past it:
`Object.assign` onto a minted argv
(`Object.assign(CCD_ARGV.ensure('x'), ['ws-rm','evil'])` types as
`CcdArgv & string[]`, and was RUNTIME-VERIFIED to mutate the real argv in
place); array covariance (`const w: (readonly string[])[] = slots; w[0] =
[...]`); and any `any`-typed value flowing in uncast (e.g.
`JSON.parse(...)`). Two parts: (1) the `Object.assign` shape is now CLOSED —
`argv()` in `ccdargv.ts` wraps its return in `Object.freeze`, so that
assignment throws (`Object.assign`'s own internal `Set(..., throw)` fails
closed on a non-writable index) instead of silently mutating the real argv
in place; (2) the disclosure in all three places (the brand's own comment,
the report, and deviation 82(c) above) is corrected to name the accurate
residual class — a deliberate cast, array covariance, or `any` — rather than
claiming totality. Array covariance and `any` are inherent to TypeScript's
structural and gradual typing and cannot be closed by a stronger brand.
Pinned in `ccdargv-brand.test.ts`: `Object.assign` onto a minted argv now
throws and leaves it unmutated; spreading a frozen argv into a copy (the
shape `lifecycle.ts`'s `ccdRunner` actually uses) remains fully usable.
Mutation swept: reverting `argv()` to the unfrozen cast kills the new throw
assertion; restored and sha256-verified clean. server 939 → 941, all exit 0;
`tsc --noEmit` clean in all three packages.

places, same shape. `notify` is now typed with the real `PushPayload`
(`PushService.notify`'s actual parameter) instead of an untyped zero-arg
callback; the now-redundant `as {...}` cast on the extracted payload is
dropped. Reproduced with a TEMPORARY tsconfig that includes `test/` (never
the real one, and deleted before committing): both errors present with the
brief's original code, gone with the fix; the real server tsconfig and
vitest are unaffected either way (941/941 exit 0 both before and after —

**117. The F3 sensitive-scan refinement — vendored/template noise filtered,
counted, never invisible (pre-merge fix round, the human partner ruled
directly: apply it).** Task 6's F3 guard enumerates inside a collapsed
ignored directory so a secret in a wholly-ignored dir cannot be silently
deleted, but three of `_WS_SENSITIVE_GLOBS` — `credentials*`, `secrets*`,
`*.pem` — reach one directory into a dependency or build tree and catch its
ORDINARY contents: `credentials.d.ts`, `cacert.pem`, `.env.example`
templates, `secretsmanager.generated.js`, `secrets-manager.js.map`. A
secret-shaped name that ALSO ends in a source, compiled or template

**118. `_ws_archive_manifest` records a failed size read as `null`, never a
fabricated `0` (pre-merge fix round, finding 5).** The SEVENTH instance of
the measurement-forgery class in this plan (deviation 10: "a number is a
measurement"). Before this fix, a `du -sb` failure on a `$workdir` that
EXISTS and IS readable wrote a literal `"worktreeBytes":0` — a false claim
of "measured, zero bytes" when the truth was "could not measure it". The
whole-directory-gone case already refuses earlier (the `[[ -d "$workdir"
]]` guard and the `git -C "$workdir" status` read, both before this point
in `_ws_archive_manifest`); this is the narrower window — an ordinary `du`
hiccup, or the directory vanishing between the `-d` check and the `du`
call. Reproduced first: a `du() { return 1; }` shell-function shadow on an
existing, readable worktree (the established technique in this suite)
showed the manifest containing `"worktreeBytes":0` before the fix.
`registry.ts`'s `manifestBytes` already treated anything but a finite JSON
number as unmeasured (Task 19), so the ONLY gap was `ccd` writing the wrong
JSON value in the first place — the fix is one word, `bytes=0` →
`bytes=null`. The identical literal line appears twice more in `ccd`
(`cmd_ws_audit`'s live `WsAudit.worktreeBytes` and `_ws_reap_tail`'s
`ReapResult.bytes`), both typed as plain `number` on the wire, not `number
| null` — changing those would be a wire-shape change touching more
consumers and was out of scope for this finding, which named
`_ws_archive_manifest` specifically; both left untouched. **Correction,
deviation 120: this fix's own reproduction used a `du() { return 1; }`
shell shadow, and the final fix round found that real `du` does not fail
that way on a partial read — it hands back a plausible, wrong NUMBER rather
than nothing, which this fix's regex-only fallback could not catch at all.
`cmd_ws_audit`'s copy is no longer "left untouched" — see 120.
`_ws_reap_tail`'s remains untouched, and 120 states why.** Pinned both
directions in `ccd-archive.test.ts`: a failed `du` now records `null` (was
`0`, shown red against the pristine `ccd`, green after); a genuine `du`
success answering literal `0` still records `0` — the two stay
distinguishable. `fleet.test.ts` gained the one missing shape: an explicit

now emits. Mutation swept: 1 mutant (the `null`/`0` fallback), killed,

**120. `_ws_gc_bytes` fabricates a number on a partial `du` read — null now, at
both named sites (final fix round, finding F).** The NINTH instance of the
measurement-forgery class (deviation 10: "a number is a measurement"), and a
correction to how deviation 118 believed it had already closed this class:
GNU `du` on a tree it can only partly read does not fail the way a
regex-only check over its stdout assumes. It prints the PARTIAL total it
summed on stdout, writes a "cannot read directory" line to stderr, and
exits non-zero — a real, plausible, WRONG number, never an empty or
non-numeric one. Measured: a 100 kB readable + 900 kB unreadable tree
answered `"102400"`, a tenfold understatement that passed
`[[ "$b" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]` clean; a fully unreadable root answered `"0"` the
same way. Both reproduced with a real `chmod 000` subdirectory, never a
`du() { return 1; }` shell shadow — deviation 118's own fix was reproduced
with exactly that stub, and real `du` does not behave like it, which is the
whole lesson.

`_ws_gc_bytes` is the one function every `worktreeBytes` figure in ccd goes
through (`_ws_archive_manifest`, `cmd_ws_audit`, `_ws_reap_tail`), so the
fix lives there rather than at each caller: `du`'s own exit status, via
`set -o pipefail` (file-wide) and the two-statement `local`/assign
CONSTRAINTS.md requires, plus its stderr, both checked in addition to the
pre-existing numeric guard on `$b`. `cmd_ws_audit`'s fallback (ccd:2504)
changes from a fabricated `0` to `null`, matching `_ws_archive_manifest`'s
existing rule (ccd:1190, deviation 118) now that the helper it calls
actually detects the failure. `WsAudit.worktreeBytes` widens to `number |
null` on the wire; `ReapSheet.tsx`'s worktree row and its primary
Remove-and-destroy button — the one figure this whole design exists to
protect — both render "unknown" rather than a number they cannot stand
behind. `_ws_reap_tail`'s own `bytes=…||bytes=0` (ccd:3049, `ReapResult.bytes`,
an epilogue figure reported after the destructive tail, not a confirm a
human reads before it) benefits from the corrected detection but keeps its
existing `0` fallback and non-nullable wire type — outside the two sites
this finding named, and not itself a confirm surface; recorded as a
deliberate scope boundary rather than an oversight.

### The measurement-forgery arc, instances ten to fifteen — read this once, then the entries

Deviation 10 states the rule this branch keeps rediscovering: **a number is a
measurement; `null` means not measured, never 0.** Deviations 118, 120 and 121
are its seventh, ninth and eighth instances. The five fix rounds recorded below
closed instances **ten through fifteen**, plus several more the commits did not
number, and the arc is worth stating once rather than fifteen times.

The mechanism is always the same and it is a TYPE problem, not a discipline
problem. A producer whose wire field is declared `number` has exactly two
options for a read that did not happen, and **one of them compiles.** So the
`0` is written, a consumer sums it, and the figure lands on a confirm button
above an irreversible `rm -rf`. Every durable closure in this arc therefore
widens the wire type as well as fixing the producer — `WsAudit.dirty`,
`.ignored`, `.ignoredCount`, `.ignoredBytes`, `.sensitive`,
`.sensitiveFiltered`, `.stashes`, `.merge.fetchedAt`, `.commitsAheadOfBase`,
`.clips[].bytes` and `ReapResult.bytes` all became `| null` in these rounds
(deviations 167, 178, 179 and 181 — deviation 160 is the one that closed its
forgery by REFUSING instead, because widening there would only have relocated
it into the PWA), and `WsTombstone` was declared for the
first time (183) so the one document that outlives the workspace states the
same thing.

**Three of these instances were made by fix rounds, not found by them**, which
is the part worth remembering:

- the **tenth** (deviation 140) was created by the round that closed the
  ninth — 09ea9ff taught `ws-gc --prune` to list an orphan's ignored set, and
  the tally under that list was a `grep -c` over the rendered text, so a
  filename holding a newline forged rows and was counted;
- `_ws_gc_dirty`'s decline sentence (deviation 159) was made false by the
  round that hardened the read beneath it — b9c4568 correctly taught the
  function to treat an unreadable tree as dirty, and its two callers then
  printed *"has uncommitted changes"* about files nobody had looked at. The
  commit does not give this one a number, so neither does this entry;
- the **fifteenth** (deviation 184) was written by the very rung that fixed a
  destroy-without-confirmation bug: 3578cc2's new detached-HEAD decline
  justified itself with *"nothing else references its commits"*, a reachability
  claim on a code path that reads no refs at all.

A related class runs beside it and is called out where it appears: **a comment
or a report that asserts a fact the code does not establish.** This round
retired a "class guard" that was a hardcoded two-file list (164), a
`tmpHelpers.ts` comment citing a `trap` that exists nowhere in the tree (152), a
route comment claiming a completeness measurement that was a grep for the
opposite thing (151), a test assertion that matched any key set at all (165),
and a coverage referral resting on a claim that was false (166). The entries
below say so in each case, because a document that warns about false claims and
then makes one is the same defect twice.

**123. `_reg_purge`: the registry teardown glob was unanchored, and a second
sweep would have deleted a live session's worktree (the single pre-lane fix —
round 2's four lanes all branched from it — destructive F3; 4e8b689).** `rm -f "$REG/$id".*` at the three registry-teardown call sites
(`cmd_ws_rm`, `_ws_reap_tail` step (i), `_ws_gc_prune_row`'s dead-reg arm)
matches `$id.uuid` — this session's own field — and also `$id.x-y.uuid`, a
field belonging to a DIFFERENT session whose id happens to be `$id.x-y`. Ids
are `<project>-<slug>` and slugs are dot-free (`_ws_slug_valid`), so the extra
dot has to come from a project DIRECTORY name: `demo-quiet-mesa.x` sitting
beside `demo`. Contrived, but dots in project directory names are legal.

What that destroys is not the registry files. The bystander loses its `.uuid`,
the next `_ws_gc_scan` classifies it `orphan`, and `ws-gc --prune`'s orphan arm
runs `git worktree remove` plus `git branch -d` on a live session nobody asked
to reclaim. Measured on the reverted code against the same fixture: sweep one
deletes `demo-quiet-mesa.x-warm-cove.{uuid,workdir,workspace}`, sweep two prints
`reclaimed removed orphan worktree …/demo-quiet-mesa.x/warm-cove` and
`reclaimed deleted merged branch ws/warm-cove`.

Replaced with `_reg_purge <id>`, filtering on the SUFFIX rather than
enumerating field names: no registry field name contains a dot, so
`$id.<field>` has exactly one dot after the id while `$id.x-y.uuid` has two.
That stays correct for any field the file grows later, which a hardcoded
allowlist would not. Pinned across TWO sweeps, because one sweep is not where
the damage shows. Server 960 → 961.

**124. `ws-restore` is serialised against `ws-reap`, on ws-reap's own lock, and
the archived marker is re-read immediately before (a) (fix round 2, destructive
F5; 2afcc84, with its lock-release test made able to fail in 52c37e6).** These
two verbs are the only pair in the design that write the same fact from
opposite directions: `ws-reap` requires `$REG/$id.archived` and `ws-restore`
removes it. Both orders were measured, not argued.

The sequential shape has the teeth. A reap SIGKILLed at (c) leaves a
`reaping=worktree` breadcrumb with the worktree still on disk — the only
interrupted state `ws-restore` can reach. The human restores; the marker goes,
the session is re-spawned and re-supervised, the workspace is live again. The
breadcrumb outlives all of it, so the next `ws-reap` takes the resume fork,
which skips `_ws_reap_eval` entirely and never asks the `not-archived`
question. Measured before the fix:
`{"reaped":"demo-quiet-basin",…,"resumed":"worktree"}` — worktree removed,
branch CAS-deleted, registry purged, on a live restored workspace, with no
human having confirmed anything about its current state.

The concurrent shape is a lost update seconds to a minute wide: Phase A checks
the marker, Phase C then spends up to 12 s in `gh pr list` and up to 60 s in
`git fetch`, and D2 waves the token through because the token was computed in
the same run and `archived` is not one of the fingerprint's thirteen inputs.
The mirror order is worse — a restore landing between the tail's (e) and its
(i) re-spawns and re-supervises a session whose worktree (f) then removes and
whose registry (i) then purges, leaving a `Restart=always` unit pointed at a
deleted directory with no registry row to resurrect from.

`cmd_ws_restore` now takes ws-reap's OWN `$REG/.reap-<id>.lock` with `flock -n`
— the same kernel lock, not a second mechanism, because two locks for one
invariant are two things to get out of step — after the uuid check and before
the archived/workdir reads, so the two facts a concurrent reap can change are
read UNDER the lock. It gives the descriptor back before it answers, since ccd
is sourced and `flock` treats two `open()`s of one path in one process as two
strangers. `_ws_reap_tail` re-reads the marker immediately before (a), refusing
the existing `not-archived` token so no new `SENTENCES` entry is needed, and
writing nothing on the way out; that half is what covers the resume path, which
no lock can span. Four tests in `serialisation with ws-restore`.

The lock-release line shipped unpinned and was caught one round later
(52c37e6): the original test's `lockFree()` ran a NEW bash after the restoring
shell had exited, and the kernel closes what exits, so a leaked descriptor was
unobservable there by construction. The acquire is now attempted in the SAME
shell that ran `cmd_ws_restore`, which is the only place it can be seen; the
cross-process check is kept beside it. Two consequences of this fix are
recorded elsewhere: it added a `die` call site to a verb the house-wide `die`
question already covers (see 146's note and the declines at the end of this
section), and the `not-archived` re-read is what made an interrupted
`_reg_purge` unrecoverable, which is deviation 146.

**125. `ws-gc --prune` scans and lists an orphan's ignored set before removing
it (fix round 2, destructive F4; 09ea9ff).** The orphan arm was the one place
in the whole design where a workspace DIRECTORY is deleted with no
sensitive-ignored scan and no listing of what is inside it. `_ws_gc_dirty`
reads `git status --porcelain`, which does not report gitignored files at all,
so an orphan holding a gitignored `.env` with a real `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`
read CLEAN, `git worktree remove` did not object, and the tree went with the
single line `reclaimed removed orphan worktree <path>`.

`_ws_gc_reclaimable` now runs `_ws_collect_ignored` immediately before the only
step in this command that deletes a directory, and: declines, naming the paths,
when the set holds secret-shaped entries — the same fact `ws-reap` treats as a
§7 no-override refusal, at the same strength, but as "refuse and move on"
rather than "refuse and offer a remedy", because this is an unattended sweep;
declines when the set cannot be READ, unknown counting as dirty, which is the
rule `_ws_gc_dirty`'s own comment states for the tracked half; and lists what
it is about to destroy with sizes and a total, sorted sensitive-first then
bytes-first, capped at ten with the remainder counted. The `  contents` prefix
is deliberately neither `  reclaimed ` nor `  declined `, so the run's tally
stays a count of ACTIONS — which is precisely the invariant this fix then broke
in the other direction (deviation 140). Cost disclosed at the function: the
scan is `_ws_collect_ignored`'s, under its 30 s whole-workspace deadline, and
runs only on an orphan row under `--prune` after the dirty and merged checks
have declined everything they can.

**126. Two mutation survivors on comment-justified lines are pinned rather than
justified (fix round 2, integration docket 7; 1469e39, tests only).** The `^`
anchor in `_ws_ignored_digest`: `git status --porcelain` prefixes each line
with a status and a space, so an untracked file NAMED `a!! b` reports as
`?? "a!! b"` and an unanchored `grep '!! '` admits it to the ignored-entry
preimage. The review's exact digests were reproduced — anchored
`07f8c2c3b4cd2eee…`, unanchored `0ba8517d511c376e…` — and the test asserts the
one-line preimage.

The stash WIP arm is the more interesting one, because the review had recorded
it as *genuinely equivalent* on the reasoning that `grep -F` is a substring
match. It is not: `grep -F` is case sensitive and the two subjects git writes
differ in exactly that character — `git stash push -m msg` gives `On ws/x: msg`
(capital O) and a bare `git stash` gives `WIP on ws/x: 1a2b3c` (lowercase o).
Measured in a repo holding one of each: both arms 2, `-e "On ws/x:"` alone 1.
The unnamed form is the common one and every existing fixture used
`stash push -m`, which is why the mutant survived. What it would cost:
`_ws_reap_eval` gates `stashes-present` on this count, so a workspace whose
only stash was a bare `git stash` reads 0, the §7 no-override guard does not
fire, and the reap CAS-deletes the branch those stashes name. The same test
pins the WIP arm's branch scoping and trailing colon — the docket's fourth
survivor, which the review could not locate. The remaining survivor of the four
(the `sort` in the sensitive-digest preimage) is re-confirmed unpinnable by
construction and left disclosed: `REAP_SENSDIGEST` is computed at ccd:2449,
after Phase B's `sensitive-ignored` refusal at ccd:2303 has already returned for
every non-empty set, so the preimage is always one blank line. (Both line
numbers are as of `1469e39`; the commit body's `ccd:2254` for the refusal was
its own Phase B comment block, not the `_reap_refuse` line.)

**127. The archive path's tree and ignored-set reads check stderr as well as
the exit status (fix round 2, integration docket 5 / new finding 3;
98e027f).** `git status --porcelain` over a PARTIALLY unreadable tree exits
ZERO with EMPTY stdout and the diagnostic on stderr alone. Measured on git
2.43 with `chmod 000` on a TRACKED directory holding a modified file: rc 0,
stdout empty, stderr `tracked/deep/code.txt: Permission denied` plus
`warning: could not open directory 'tracked/'`. `_ws_reap_eval` and
`_ws_collect_ignored` had been hardened against exactly this; two reads in
`_ws_archive_manifest` had not, so the manifest recorded `"dirty":0` for a tree
with uncommitted work in it, and `_ws_ignored_digest` — which checks only
`PIPESTATUS[0]`, also 0 in that state — hashed a SHORT ignored set and reported
success.

Both reads now require rc 0 AND empty stderr, and the manifest's refusal quotes
what git actually said. This is the REFUSED arm of the ladder the function's own
header draws, not an exception to it: the RECORDED arm is for facts that are
merely unexpected, and a partial read is the absence of a fact. Two pre-existing
fixtures were NARROWED rather than weakened — their `chmod 000` subdirectory is
now gitignored, because an unignored one makes the new tree guard refuse first
and the test then asserts the wrong guard. Measured: gitignored,
`status --porcelain` is rc 0 with empty stderr and `--ignored=matching` collapses
the entry without descending, while `du -sb` still walks in, still fails and
still prints the partial total — so deviation 120's pins were re-verified intact
under the narrowed fixtures (102503/102505 vs `null`).

**128. `isExecAllowed` answers `false` for prototype-named commands instead of
throwing (fix round 2, gates 6 / destructive F7; b89499f).** `EXEC_WHITELIST`
is a plain object literal, so `EXEC_WHITELIST[cmd]` returned an INHERITED value
for `constructor`, `__proto__`, `toString`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`,
`isPrototypeOf`, `propertyIsEnumerable` and `toLocaleString`. Those are truthy,
so `if (!prefixes) return false` did not fire and `prefixes.some(...)` threw
`TypeError` — reproduced on 4e8b689 for all eight names.

Today it fails CLOSED: the throw is a rejection that `handleReq(...).catch(...)`
turns into a `fail` frame and no `runExec` happens. The defect is that the only
thing separating "wrong error message on the wire" from "permitted" is that no
caller wraps `isExecAllowed` in a `try`/`catch` treating an exception as benign
— the most natural refactor in the world around a function that unexpectedly
throws. `canonicalize` and `checkPath` were already hardened against this class.
Two independent guards now answer it, `Object.hasOwn` and `Array.isArray`,
either sufficient alone; the new `whitelist-prototype.test.ts` fails 9
assertions on the pre-fix code, including `defaultsToTrueOnThrow` — the
swallowing caller written out, so the pin is against the hole and not merely
against the message. Their respective pinnability is settled in deviation 162.

**129. Granting `gh` becomes a compile error and a boot failure, not one
deletable test (fix round 2, gates 4, MAJOR; 99bb05e).** Reproduced verbatim on
4e8b689: delete `agent/test/whitelist-noghosts.test.ts` (32 tests), add
`gh: [['pr','view']]` above the `ccd` key, and the agent suite reports 99/99
PASS, `server/test/whitelist-subset.test.ts` 35/35, and `tsc --noEmit` clean.
The branch's own stated most dangerous invariant — that any `gh` entry makes
this list the sole control between the PWA and `gh pr merge`, against a host
token carrying the `repo` WRITE scope with no second credential — was pinned by
exactly one test in one file. Position mattered too: the server's layer 3
sliced `whitelist.ts`'s source TEXT from the `ccd` key onward, so a key written
above it was outside the slice and invisible cross-package.

Applying the human partner's standing ruling on this class — STRUCTURAL OVER
TEXTUAL, the same ruling that replaced layer 2b's source scan with the `CcdArgv`
brand — the pin is four mechanisms in three classes. (1) `EXEC_COMMANDS` /
`ExecCommand` close the key set and `EXEC_WHITELIST: Record<ExecCommand, …>`
makes a `gh` key TS2353 at any position (measured above and below the `ccd` key:
identical error). (2) `GRANTABLE_COMMANDS: readonly ProvenGrantable[]` is a
disjointness proof between `ExecCommand` and `FORBIDDEN_COMMANDS`, so widening
the union to satisfy (1) is TS2322 on a different line (measured). (3)
`auditExecWhitelist()` runs at module load and throws, so a widened list makes
the agent REFUSE TO BOOT — the residual class `ccdargv.ts` documents a brand
cannot close (a deliberate cast, an `any`-typed value, array covariance, a
hand-edit of compiled `dist/` JS), because it reads the real object's own keys
after every cast has happened; `EXEC_WHITELIST` is also deep-frozen. (4) Tests:
`whitelist-structural.test.ts` asserts the compile errors of (1) and (2)
actually occur, via `test/types/bypasses/` plus `tsconfig.ok.json` with error
CODES asserted per fixture and a positive control required to compile clean, so
"nothing compiles" cannot satisfy the pins; server layer 3 gains a
position-independent `Object.keys(EXEC_WHITELIST)` assertion in a DIFFERENT
package.

Measured after the fix, same experiments: the review's own (rm noghosts + add
`gh` key) gives agent tsc TS2353, 8 of 9 agent test FILES failing at import, and
`whitelist-subset` failing at import. Worst case — all three coordinated source
edits plus deleting BOTH agent pin files — gives agent tsc clean and agent
99/99, and server layer 3 still fails 2; a fourth deletion, in another package,
is required to go green. Honest limit, stated in the source: nothing in a repo
the editor controls is un-removable; what changed is that it can no longer
happen by one `rm`, by accident, or via a diff that reads as ordinary. This fix
closed the reported instance and left two halves of the class open — the key set
was pinned and the VALUES were not (deviation 149), and the auditor asked a
different question from the lookup (deviation 147).

**130. `server/test/`, `agent/test/`, `server/test-e2e/` and three vitest
configs join a typecheck project, and the gate enumerates directories instead of
naming one (fix round 2, integration 4; 6e04738 — and fix round 6, gates 4;
7a551b7).** `server/tsconfig.json`'s include is `["src/**/*.ts",
"../shared/**/*.ts"]`, so fifty test files and their shared helpers were
compiled by nothing. Verified under a temporary tests-inclusive project: exactly
one live error, `test/fleet.test.ts(178,65) TS2769` — a `PrState` literal
missing the required `retryAt`. Fixed with `retryAt: null`, not `0`: a merged PR
has no scheduled retry, and a number there would be a measurement nobody made.
Deviation 80 had carried that error knowingly, precisely because no gate could
report it. Closed with `test/tsconfig.tests.json` in BOTH server and agent
(agent's was measured clean — the point is that it stays clean), run by
`server/test/typecheck-tests.test.ts` so the controller's existing suite gate
covers it with no new command to forget; a separate project rather than a
widened include, because `npm run build` emits from `tsconfig.json` and must not
emit tests into `dist/`. `test/types/**` is excluded — those are the
deliberately non-compiling bypass fixtures — and the gate asserts via
`tsc --listFiles` that every `.ts` on disk in both test directories is actually
IN the program, so an include that drifted to match nothing cannot report clean
forever.

Four rounds later the same shape was found one directory over, and the guard
written to prevent the recurrence could not see it: `server/test-e2e/`
(helpers.ts and session.e2e.test.ts, 225 lines) was in NO project — measured
with `tsc --listFiles`, `server/tsconfig.json` → 0 files under test-e2e,
`test/tsconfig.tests.json` → 0, because its `./**/*.ts` is relative to `test/`
— and the guard read `readdirSync(here)` with `here` = `server/test/`, so it
checked exhaustively and correctly the one directory that was ALREADY covered. A
gate against "a whole directory is outside the typechecker" that takes the
directory as an input cannot fail for the reason it exists. Both halves fixed:
the include gains `../test-e2e/**/*.ts` (measured clean before the change, so no
verdict moved on the day it landed), and `typecheck-tests.test.ts` now walks the
package root, collects every `.ts` that is not a `.d.ts` and not a
`test*/types/**` fixture, and asserts each is in the union of that package's
programs — with a floor on the walk and a "more than one directory found"
assertion, so a walk that found nothing cannot pass everything.

The enumeration immediately found more than the report did, which is the point
of enumerating: `server/vitest.config.ts`, `server/vitest.e2e.config.ts` and
`agent/vitest.config.ts` were also in no project at all (pwa already covers its
`vite.config.ts`, so this was an asymmetry, not a policy). All three measured
clean, then added via `../*.ts`. `agent/vitest.config.ts` is not inert
configuration here: it carries the `setupFiles`/`globalSetup` wiring whose
absence has killed the live fleet four times (see 175). Measured afterwards by
`find` plus `tsc --listFiles` per project: the only `.ts` outside a program
anywhere in `infra/ccrc` are the `test*/types/**` bypass fixtures, which have
their own projects and are asserted to FAIL. Not covered and reported rather
than implied: `pwa/tsconfig.json`'s own coverage is asserted by nothing (the
file is outside that lane), and the `.mjs` under `pwa/design/` can be checked by
no TS project. Mutations: removing `../test-e2e/**/*.ts` turns 3 red by name; a
new `server/test-int/latent.ts` that nobody listed turns 1 red — the class, not
the instance, since the old gate was green for both. Server 1071 → 1073.

**131. `isPrPhase` replaces the double cast, and then `PR_PHASES` is made
module-private so the double cast cannot be written at all (fix round 2,
integration 3, b167b32; fix round 3, verify2-agent P3, 89a750b).**
`shared/api.ts` states the rule — *"validating an untrusted string against a
`readonly PrPhase[]` needs `raw as PrPhase` on the value being checked, which
asserts the very thing the check is asking. Cast the CONSTANT, never the
input"* — and `registry.ts:80` broke it three lines below:
`PR_PHASES.includes(prPhaseRaw as PrPhase) ? (prPhaseRaw as PrPhase) : null`.
Honest scope, stated in the test file too: NO distinguishing runtime input
exists — both forms do an exact-match `.includes` over the same eight strings,
casts are erased, and `null as PrPhase` is not in the array. The defect is the
shape: an assertion standing where a check belongs reads as validated and
survives the refactor that makes it false. `isPrPhase(v: unknown): v is PrPhase`
removes both casts and rejects non-strings before they can reach `.includes`
wearing a `PrPhase` annotation.

The fix was not pinned against its own reversal, and the verifier proved it:
putting `registry.ts:85` back to the reported defect verbatim, with `isPrPhase`
left exported and unused, gave `tsc -p server` clean, the server suite
1005/1005 and typecheck-tests 7/7. The p1 fixture pinned only that `PR_PHASES`
was cast-HOSTILE, which the reverted expression satisfies BY CASTING. A type was
tried first and MEASURED not to work: branding the registry read
(`string & { readonly [B]: true }`, and a property-brand variant) does NOT make
`raw as PrPhase` an error — TypeScript's comparable relation lets an
intersection be asserted to a constituent's subtype, and all four probe shapes
compiled clean. **No type in this language refuses a cast; what refuses it is
not having the constant.** `PR_PHASES` is now module-private, so the expression
is TS2724 before the casts are even considered, and `isPrPhase` is the only
door. Nothing outside `shared/api.ts` used the list (checked across
`server/src`, `shared`, `pwa/src`, `agent`); the test that needs the eight values
derives them from `Record<PrPhase, true>` and asserts them through the
VALIDATOR. Fixtures: p1 rewritten (TS2345 → TS2724, the stronger error), p2
added replaying the reverted line verbatim, p3 added as a positive control
asserted to draw NO diagnostic. Disclosed and not closed: `isPrPhase`'s own body
losing its `typeof` guard by re-casting the input — no runtime input can
distinguish it, because `Array.prototype.includes` uses SameValueZero and no
non-string is ever equal to a string; that is a proof, and it is why the seven
"rejects a non-string" cases discriminate nothing. Server 1015 → 1024.

**132. Well-safe ink on every well in the light theme (fix round 2, gates 1 —
the branch's only BLOCKER; 11e1d0d).** `--bg-well` is deliberately dark in BOTH
themes (tokens.css:252), so every ink token tuned for paper dies on the glass.
Three rules painted one on a well: `.pr-body-preview` with `--ink-secondary` at
**2.44:1** against a 4.5 floor — the PR sheet's primary content, a real rendered
`<textarea readOnly>`; `.dlg-reply-input` with `--ink-primary` at **1.09:1**,
near-black on near-black, i.e. what you type into the ask sheet is invisible;
and `.msg-attach-gone` with `--ink-tertiary` at **3.17:1**. All three measured
in the light theme; all three read 9.6–17.4 in dark, which is why they survived
every eyeball pass. Fixed with `--ink-on-well` (15.52 / 13.98), the one text
token declared once for both themes, and `--syn-comment` (6.41 / 5.77) for the
placeholder and the degraded-clip line. The gate printed ALL 94 PASS over all
three, because it measured a hand-maintained table of token pairs and none of
these pairs was in it — which is deviation 134.

**133. Archived rows fade with an ink step, not element opacity (fix round 2,
gates 2, MAJOR; a0d7254).** `.proj-archived-body .sess-line { opacity: 0.72 }`
composites over the project card AFTER the token pair has been chosen, so every
already-gated colour in the `SessionLine` subtree silently dropped — fifteen
pairs, measured in both themes: `.sess-meta` 5.06/3.70, its middot 3.60/3.15,
state waiting 5.75/3.30, working 6.05/3.50, exited 5.06/3.70, `.sess-warn`
4.09/3.38, `.sess-acct-away` 5.75/3.30, the four account hues 5.08–6.08 /
3.62–3.89 against a 4.5 floor, and all four lamp dots 3.22–6.07 / 2.18–2.99
against a 3 floor. `chat.css` already carried the rule this broke — *"Never
element opacity, that would push ink below AA"* — on `.task-row--completed`.

Raising the value is not a fix: the light-theme dead dot on its lamp well needs
opacity 0.962 before it clears 3:1, and at 0.962 nothing reads as faded. So the
past-tense signal moves to the row's identity — the label steps `--ink-primary`
→ `--ink-secondary` (15.68 → 8.67 dark, 16.58 → 7.41 light, both pairs the gate
already measures) and drops its medium weight. Two channels, no compositing.
`:not(.sess-line--active)` is load-bearing, not decorative: the selected row
reverses out and fills with `--ink-primary` as a BACKGROUND, `--ink-secondary`
on that slab is 1.81 dark / 2.24 light, this rule sits after
`.sess-line--active .sess-label` at equal specificity, and
`project-card.test.tsx:337` renders exactly an archived selected row.

**134. The contrast gate stops being a hand-maintained token table and becomes
a stylesheet parser — one auditor, called by the gate and by the suite (fix
round 2, the systemic finding behind gates 1 and 2, ee3ac42; fix round 3, the
finding no lane owned plus verify2-css P1/P2/P3/P6, 5e18079, 9c398d5, e997e79,
6b61800, and the file's first landing inside a4f3a42).** This is the largest
single change in these rounds and it replaces the mechanism, not the data.

`design/contrast-check.mjs` — the command the plan and all three whole-branch
reviews quote by name — measured a hand-typed table of token hexes against a
hand-typed list of 94 pairs. Every defect of gates 1 and 2 is a consequence of
that shape: a rule that pairs two tokens nobody wrote down is invisible to it,
and `opacity` is invisible to it in principle, so a live 2.44:1 WCAG failure and
a fade that pushed fifteen gated pairs below their floors both shipped under
`ALL 94 PASS`. Deviations 86 and 87 were both "the table and the stylesheet
disagree", the same class one directory away.

The first attempt (ee3ac42) built the parser inside `test/contrast.test.ts`,
because `design/` was outside that lane's file ownership. It did the three
things the review sketched — parse tokens.css for both theme blocks, resolving
`var()` chains, `rgb(a)` and `color-mix(in srgb, A p%, B)`, stripping comments
FIRST because `:root` and `[data-theme='light']` both appear in the file's own
prose; measure every rule that sets both a `color` and a `background` (51 of
them) against the ground the rule names itself; and require every static
`opacity` strictly between 0 and 1 to be registered with either the composited
pairs it fades or a reason it fades no coloured content. On its first run it
found three further pre-existing failures, all fixed in the same commit:
`.chat-banner--dead` and `.fleet-host-banner` painting `--status-dead-tint` (12%
alpha, priced over a CARD) on `--bg-page` at 4.44 light; the caution callout,
the one alpha tint of the five, reading 4.44 light where its siblings read
4.94–5.73; and the reduced-motion pin on `.dot--busy`/`.dot--attention` at
opacity 0.8, which put the light attention dot at 2.88 against a 3 floor (0.85
clears all four grounds, tightest 3.10). Verified by 14 mutants, each applied
with a `count==1` anchor, run, restored and sha256-checked.

**But that answer was itself the class it was closing.** It left the NAMED gate
still measuring 94 token pairs from hardcoded tables, and it carried its own
`DECLARED_PAIRS` list — a fresh unbound copy of the stylesheet, ten of whose
fifteen entries were markdown callouts written out as literals with no scrape
pin, so the exact blocker shape could be reintroduced in a callout variant with
the whole suite green. So the next round put ONE auditor in `design/audit.mjs`
(the file lands in a4f3a42 and is wired up in 5e18079), called by the gate and
by the suite, with nothing typed twice: the D/Lt hex tables are gone and with
them the drift test that existed only to police them; `color-mix()` is now
computed in PREMULTIPLIED alpha per CSS Color 5, the previous implementation
having interpolated raw channels, which turns a 12% wash into a colour 88% of
the way to black; the stylesheets are DISCOVERED from disk rather than listed
(`src/styles/base.css` was absent from the hardcoded list and therefore exempt
from BOTH audits while the list looked complete — a list of files is the same
drift class as a list of colours); VARIANTS are followed, so a rule that only
rebinds the custom properties a base rule paints with re-measures the base rule,
and all five markdown callouts with their `::before` labels are read off the
stylesheet instead of being declared; pseudo-element children inherit their
host's background through each of the host's variants; `72%`, `.72` and
`0.72 !important` all normalise to 0.72, where they used to hit `Number(v)` →
`NaN` and be FILTERED OUT of the fade set, falsifying the report's central
claim; and a structural problem — unregistered fade, unparsed colour, registry
entry naming a rule that no longer exists — is a FAIL row and a non-zero exit,
never a silent pass. **94 token pairs → 234 measured pairs, all green, gate
exits 0.** `test/contrast.test.ts` keeps only what a test can do and a gate
cannot: seven hand-computed arithmetic controls, structural assertions, and 12
mutation proofs that copy the tree, mutate one file and run the real gate binary
against it, one per escape route that has actually been used to get a failure
past this gate.

Two more pieces landed with it. `@keyframes` troughs (9c398d5): the previous
round had disclosed the trough set BY HAND as "working-glyph .35, working-dot
.25, tool-breathe .55, task-breathe .55" and shipped that as complete, and it
was already wrong — `dot-breathe` 0.55, the status lamps, the most visible
animation in the app and the one whose steady state the reduced-motion block had
to be measured for, was missing. `audit.mjs` now discovers every `@keyframes`
block and the lowest opacity any of its stops sets, and requires each to appear
in `KEYFRAME_TROUGHS` with the elements it animates and their reduced-motion
steady state; ten blocks discovered, ten registered, and an unregistered trough,
a stale entry or a non-static stop is a gate failure. The RULING on the troughs
themselves is documented follow-up, not pre-merge: WCAG 2.1 states no per-frame
contrast requirement for an animating element, every loop here reduces to a
steady state under `prefers-reduced-motion` that IS registered and measured, and
flooring a trough means retuning the "glow means life" motion language
DIRECTION.md sets out — a design decision with no standards mandate behind it.
What changed is that the disclosure is now enforced rather than asserted, and the
follow-up has an accurate inventory. And the 12% dead wash (6b61800) got a token,
`--status-dead-tint-solid`, instead of three copies of a `color-mix` written out
in full at each site plus five in the test: change tokens.css:63 to 0.15 and the
gate stayed green while all three surfaces kept the old 12%. Declared once in
`:root` only, since both `--status-dead-tint` and `--bg-surface` are re-declared
for the light theme so `var()` resolves it per theme exactly as the browser does;
verified byte-equal to the old value in both themes (44.48,32.96,28.68 dark and
245.76,232.08,229.68 light); and the binding is a per-theme test asserting the
composite EQUALS the token, so retuning either alone fails.

Finally the prose (e997e79): tokens.css's header, `design/DIRECTION.md` and
`design/QA-CHECKLIST.md` all said the checker verifies "74 pairs"; it had
measured 94 for some time and measured 234 by then. A hand-typed number
describing a machine-counted thing is a copy, so the number is deleted rather
than re-synced and the three files describe the MECHANISM instead. DIRECTION.md
also gains the standing rule that falls out of this round — **a quiet, stale or
disabled treatment belongs in the chrome or in an ink step, never in
`opacity`** — and states the open motion question the keyframe troughs leave.
The auditor's own escapes are deviations 165, 172 and 173.

**135. `contrast.test.ts` stops leaking a `/tmp` directory on every run (fix
round 2, gates 3, MAJOR; 32f3ac0).** `test/contrast.test.ts:54` called
`mkdtempSync` directly to hold the deliberately-broken copy of
`design/contrast-check.mjs`, and the file had no `afterAll`, no `afterEach`, no
`rmSync` and no `unlink`. Every run left the directory behind: measured 688 →
689 across one run of the pwa suite, oldest dated 2026-07-27, the day this
branch's work started. `server/test/tmpHelpers.ts` is the repo's answer and
`server/` is clean across 77 call sites; `pwa/` had no equivalent, so the same
two pieces — a registry of what was made and a file-scoped cleanup — land in the
one file that needed them, with the injection test removing its own directory in
a `finally` so the leak is observable: an `afterAll` cannot be asserted from
inside the file it runs for, so the new test reads the path the previous test
recorded. Without it, a mutation sweep (50–120 suite runs) adds 50–120
directories to a `/tmp` that already holds 47k entries, on the box whose
OOM/disk incident history is why this project exists. The same class in
`agent/test` is deviation 150, its guard is 164, and the harness leak that
survived all of them is 175. The ~680 stale `contrast-*` directories already on
the host were DECLINED as too risky pre-merge (sibling lanes were running the
pwa suite from their own worktrees and a prefix sweep would delete a live
fixture); that remains a controller action item.

**136. `ReapSheet` refuses to describe one workspace while naming another (fix
round 2, destructive F2, 41c5b10; fix round 3, verify2-tsx P1/P2, 9b22d62;
fixture correction c120938).** There was no guard on the in-flight audit fetch,
so two audits could be in flight at once — sheet open on alpha, target switches
to bravo — and whichever RESOLVED LAST won. When that was alpha's, the sheet
rendered the header, title and primary button from the `session` prop
("Remove bravo · …") over rows, paths, clip names and a TOKEN measured on alpha.
Task 17's F1 `setAudit(null)` fixed only the synchronous half. Nothing is
destroyed by the resulting tap — `id=$1` is the first line of `_ws_fingerprint`,
so ccd recomputes a different token and refuses `state-changed` — but this
branch's whole safety model is that the human sees what would be destroyed
before authorising it, and a confirmation that names one workspace while
describing another is that model failing.

Two independent gates, because this is the destructive-confirmation surface: a
generation counter, where every `load()` claims a generation and a response is
accepted only while its generation is current (the audit-failure toast guarded
the same way); and `audit.id === session.id`, ccd's own first field and the
first line of the fingerprint the token hashes — the response's own statement of
what was measured. The second needs no reasoning about order and covers the one
window a generation guard structurally cannot: `session` is
`sessions.find(...) ?? null` at both call sites, so the fleet can drop the target
to null and bring a DIFFERENT one back, and that render commits before the effect
that would clear the old audit. A mismatch renders "Checking…" — refusing to
describe — never the wrong facts.

The generation bump shipped inside `load()` only, and the cleanup bump was
declined as an equivalent mutant on the reasoning that unmount and `id → null`
are unobservable. `toast()` is the counter-example: it is a global host that
outlives this sheet's render, so a failed audit belonging to a sheet the reader
has left still puts a red banner on their screen. Three distinguishing inputs
are now pinned, all three failing with the one line removed — the sheet
dismissed while an audit is in flight, the fleet sweep dropping the target so
`session` goes null, and the screen unmounting with the app-shell ToastHost still
mounted. The shipped comment had already asserted the cleanup bump, so the
invariant was implemented rather than the claim weakened.

One fixture note was itself false and is corrected in c120938: it called
`id: 'demo'` "a response ccd cannot produce" while substituting
`claude:OpenClawHetzner`, which ccd cannot produce either — `cmd_ws_audit`
validates the id against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` before doing anything (ccd:2512),
so a colon dies at the verb and the route 502s. Both reap tests now use
`OpenClawHetzner-quiet-basin`, the `$project-$slug` form ccd actually builds
(ccd:712); no assertion changed and reverting the fixture id to a mismatch still
fails both.

**137. One copy of the PR phase words (fix round 2, integration finding 5,
83f9567; and the tooltip rendered as plain text, verify2-tsx P6, 599a162).**
`PrKeycap.tsx` exports `prSentence`, `prLegend` and `UNCHECKED_PR` precisely so
the cap and the sheet can never disagree about what a phase means, and
`UNCHECKED_PR`'s own docstring says a second copy would drift. `PrSheet.tsx` had
made one anyway, one layer down — three phase-keyed fragments re-declared — and
one had already drifted: the sheet's `.pr-checkline` said "no checks configured"
where the cap's aria-label said "No checks configured." Re-syncing the words
would only reset the clock, so each copy is removed rather than corrected:
`checkText`'s four strings move into a `CHECK_PHRASE` record behind a new
exported `checkPhrase(pr)`; the `no-commits` disabled button's tooltip reads the
`lede` variable that already rendered it; and the `closed` phase's `.pr-note`,
which repeated the second sentence of the lede verbatim so the same words
appeared TWICE on one screen, is deleted. The failing-check NAMES stay out of
`checkPhrase` by design — the sheet has a dedicated inert block for them, since
they are attacker-controllable on fork PRs. The four new tests pin the PROPERTY
rather than the strings: for every CI state the sheet's line must be a clause of
the sentence the cap speaks, the tooltip must be the lede, and the closed
sentence must appear exactly once. Seven tests fail on the pre-fix components.

De-duplicating the tooltip against the lede was right; reusing the lede string
byte-for-byte was not. A `title` attribute is plain text, so the markdown ticks
meant for the lede's own presentation showed as literal backticks, and the
tooltip repeated the "Pull request: " opener plus the whole visible sentence
sitting one line above it. `tooltipSentence` derives the plain form from the same
string — still one sentence, still no second copy — and keeps a numbered opener
("Pull request #42: "), since the number is information the tooltip does not
otherwise carry.

shared, formatting-insensitive reader (`test/cssRule.ts`), whose header carries

The report of that fix claimed "all three". There were five files carrying a
hand-rolled reader, and an enumeration for the wider shape — any assertion
matched against raw stylesheet TEXT — found more on top of those. The verifier

**142. Off-branch stashes are counted, so a detached `git stash` cannot read 0
(fix round 3, integration docket 6, "THE headline gap"; 2e65bb5).** A stash
taken with a bare `git stash` from a worktree on a DETACHED HEAD carries the
literal `(no branch)` in place of a name, so neither `-e "On <branch>:"` nor
`-e "WIP on <branch>:"` matched it and `_ws_stash_count` answered an
honest-looking 0. §7's no-override `stashes-present` guard could not fire and the
reap CAS-deleted the branch the stash was taken from. The finding had been
declined out-of-lane in the previous round with "whoever owns ccd should decide";
ccd is this lane's.

Attributed by BASE COMMIT — the stash commit's first parent — because the message
has no name to match: an off-branch entry belongs to this branch exactly when
that commit is reachable from it. Deliberately NOT "any `(no branch)` stash
blocks every workspace", which ccd:2505 already rejects with a measurement
(the commit body's `ccd:2392` is the `foreign-worktree` refusal, not the stash
one; 2505 is where *"what the guard must NOT do is read `refs/stash exists` as
`this branch has stashes`"* is measured, as of `2e65bb5`). An
entry whose parent cannot be read counts. The over-attribution cost is measured
and disclosed in source rather than estimated: an off-branch stash based on
SHARED history counts against every branch in the repository (fixture: one stash
at the root commit, both `ws/x` and `master` read 1). Taken anyway —
`stashes-present` has a local remedy, and the narrowing that would remove it is a
second inference in front of a no-override guard. The same count feeds the
archive manifest's `stashes` field. The apparent contradiction with ccd's own
fleet-wide rule is reconciled in deviation 161.

**143. `prnumber` is cleared before `prphase` moves, so no kill can leave
`{none, 42}` (fix round 3, integration new finding 9; 7ba9f04).**
`put('prphase')` ran nineteen lines ahead of the number write, so an
interruption between them persisted `{phase:'none', number:42}` — the one pair
docket 1 proved otherwise unconstructible, and the reason its
"unconstructible" claim was only conditional. Two files cannot be written
atomically, so the fix is WHICH half-written pairs are reachable:
`clear('prnumber')` now runs first and the number is re-put last, so every
intermediate is `{some phase, absent}`, which is what a workspace that never had
a PR looks like and what every reader already treats as null. A degraded reading,
never a false one. Pinned by injecting the interruption where a test can see it —
a DIRECTORY at the prnumber path makes `clear`'s `os.remove` raise
`IsADirectoryError` — with the assertion on the ordering property.

**145. `ccclip` stops orphaning its incoming `/tmp` file, and validates the
session id before it reaches the remote shell (fix round 3, gates
"cannot-verify 5" — the finding no lane's ownership list contained; 36dbfee and
65f05d9, with the harness note d064c37).** Two independent defects on one
production path.

The leak: `ccd clip` only ever MOVES `/tmp/ccclip-incoming-<pid>.png`, and it
dies before the move for three ordinary reasons (path is not a file, no cc
session attached, session not alive). Each left the file on the box for ever,
with no owner and no sweep, on a host that hit 95% disk the day this was
written. The cleanup now travels with the ssh command rather than living in
`ccd clip`'s exit paths, so it runs after a success (no-op, already moved), after
every die, and after any other non-zero exit, with the verb's own status
preserved and re-raised. The remote name gains a `$RANDOM` component: `$$` alone
is a recycled pid and a collision would have one run overwrite another's unfiled
image.

The injection, found on the line the leak fix touches and reported as a new
finding rather than folded into it: `ssh "$BOX" "$CCD clip '$remote' '$1'"` is
ONE string the box re-parses with `sh`, so a single quote in the id closes the
quoting and everything after it runs there as the operator. ccd validates the id
with exactly this regex — but INSIDE the verb, i.e. after the shell that would
already have run the injection. The same `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` now runs before
`scp`, so an id ccd would accept is an id this sends, pinned in both directions.

The new `ccd-ccclip.test.ts` runs the REAL script with `pngpaste`/`mktemp`/`scp`/
`ssh` shadowed as exported bash functions — because line 8 replaces PATH outright
and a stub directory would be discarded — then executes the command it transmits
against a stubbed verb. Nothing touches the real `/tmp` or the network. It was
then routed through `ghContainedEnv` (d064c37) even though `ccclip` could not
reach a poisoned `gh` if it tried, because the structural half of the no-real-gh
boundary is "every bash call site in every ccd test file goes through it", and a
file that argued its way out of the gate would be the precedent that ends the
invariant.

**146. The state markers are purged last, and a partially purged id can no
longer be reused as a clean slug (fix round 3, verify2-bash P4, 74c3e8f; fix
round 4, round-3 verification P1, b0decea).** `_reg_purge` unlinked one file at
a time in GLOB order, so `archived` went several files before `reaping`. A
SIGKILL or an OOM between them — the failure model the reap lock exists for, and
this project's speciality — left `<id>.reaping=clips` beside a MISSING
`<id>.archived`. That used to be resumable; since deviation 124's archived
re-read landed in `_ws_reap_tail` it answers `not-archived` for ever, and
`ws-archive` cannot be re-run on a half-purged registry. The invariant is one
line — **`reaping` must never outlive `archived`** — so the two state markers are
removed last, in that order, after every ordinary field, and the marker's removal
is CONDITIONAL on the breadcrumb's having actually gone, which makes it a
mechanism rather than an assumption and makes the order observable to a test.
The residue of the last window (a lone zero-byte `.archived`) is disclosed in
source. Second half: the tail's refusal detail no longer asserts "ws-restore
brought it back" — a missing marker is the observable fact, who removed it is an
inference, and until this commit it was not even the only cause.

That fix then created its own hazard, which the next round's verification caught.
Removing the markers last makes both of them outlive `.uuid` BY CONSTRUCTION,
and `_ws_slug_free` asked only `[[ ! -f "$REG/$1-$2.uuid" ]]`. So a kill in the
~4 syscalls after the `.uuid` unlink freed the slug while leaving the state
markers on disk, and `cmd_ws_add` purges nothing for the id it creates. The next
workspace to draw that slug inherited them: `ws-archive --session <id>` answers
`already archived` at exit 0 having stopped no session and written no manifest;
`_ws_reap_eval` Phase A and `_ws_reap_tail` both pass the archived gate on a
workspace nobody archived; and with `.reaping` present `_ws_reap_locked` takes
the resume fork, where the token is not checked and Phase C — the merged-PR
proof — is deliberately not re-run. Pre-fix that residue was unconstructible and
the failure was a safe-direction wedge; post-fix it is unsafe-direction and on
the destructive path. `_ws_slug_free` is now an ANY-FIELD check over
`$REG/<id>.*`, carrying `_reg_purge`'s two-dot skip for `_reg_purge`'s reason
(deviation 123). The property is not that these two markers in particular are
noticed, but that a partially purged id is never reused as a clean one — wherever
the interruption landed, whichever function was interrupted, and including any
field added later. The residual leak changes direction rather than disappearing:
an interrupted purge now costs a SLUG rather than costing the next workspace its
archive and reap gates, it is visible (`ws-add` prints the field names still on
disk, which is also the reclaim instruction), and refusing to build is the safe
direction. Pinned by four tests that construct the residue directly, the first by
shadowing `rm` with a budget so EVERY interruption point of the purge is
enumerated rather than the one the previous round disclosed; the uuid-only form
kills 3 of the 4 and dropping the two-dot skip kills the fourth.

`Object.defineProperty(EXEC_WHITELIST, 'gh', { value: [['pr','merge']],

**148. The agent refuses to boot for OVER-permission and never for under (fix
round 3, critic2 "still unverified" / verify2-agent item 3; 23ff1a9).**
`whitelist.ts` threw at module load if its key set was wrong AT ALL. The
disclosure — "a widened list must stop the agent from starting" — was right about
the dangerous half and wrong about the other one: it also converted a
harmless-looking mistake into a dead agent on a fleet host running 11 live

message, fatal or not, now carries the `ccrc-agent:` prefix the rest of the agent
logs with, names the offending key, and ends "Refusing to start."; the throw
happens while the ESM module is evaluated, before `index.ts`'s body runs, so the
`unhandledRejection` backstop there cannot swallow it, and the residual (a future
dynamic `await import()` inside a `try`) is disclosed in source. Agent 172 → 174.

**150. Agent test fixtures are removed in a hook, not after the assertion (fix
round 3, critic2 "gates 3, related sub-item"; b685ab2).**

**151. The `verbSupported` gate reaches every route that needs it, and the claim
that it already did is retracted (fix round 3, integration new finding 10,
db45adb; fix round 4, round-3 P1, c44d29b).** `GET /api/sessions/:id/workspace/
audit` was the one ccd route with no `verbSupported` gate: against a fleet host
running a ccd without `ws-audit`, the call went out anyway, ccd answered on
stderr, `parseAudit` returned null and the route 502'd, so version skew rendered
as a failure of the workspace rather than as the "unsupported" answer the rest of
the branch gives — on the route that feeds the destructive confirm sheet. Status
and body match the reap route exactly (501 `{ok:false, error:'unsupported'}`),
because the sheet drives audit and reap from one flow and must be able to tell
"this ccd is too old" from "ccd tried and could not". Two tests, the second being
the one that stops "501 always" from passing: a fleet that advertised `ws-audit`
and a fleet that advertised NOTHING (`ccdVerbs: null` = no evidence, e.g. local
mode or an older agent) must both still audit.

That fix then wrote into `server.ts` that the audit route had been "the ONE ccd
route with no `verbSupported` gate (measured: server.ts:434, :456, :499 had it,
the audit route did not)". **The measurement was a grep for the routes that
ALREADY HAD a gate, not for the routes that NEEDED one, so the sentence was false
when it was written** — the same damage class this branch removed from
`tmpHelpers.ts` three commits later (deviation 152). Three sites were missing the
gate, all the same verb generation and all added by this branch:
`POST /api/sessions/:id/archive`, `POST /api/sessions/:id/restore`, and
`FleetWatcher.archiveMerged` in `watch.ts` — the level-triggered auto-archive
lane, which on a skewed host did not fail once but re-fired for every merged
session on every sweep, for ever. All three now answer skew the way every sibling
does: 501 for the routes, a silent skip that leaves the merged level intact for
the sweep. The false comment is replaced by a dated retraction that says what was
wrong with the measurement.

**The completeness claim is no longer made in prose at all.**
`server/test/verb-gate.test.ts` parses every `.ts` under `server/src` for
`CCD_ARGV.<name>(` call sites, resolves each one's enclosing handler by brace
depth over comment- and string-blanked source, and requires a `verbSupported(` in
that scope unless the VERB is in an explicit `UNGATED_BY_DECISION` set (the six
pre-branch verbs). It asserts both directions, so the exemption list cannot rot
into folklore, and it self-tests the scanner against known-answer fixtures so "no
offenders" cannot mean "matched nothing". Proof: reverting the `/archive` gate →
pr-routes 1 failed, verb-gate 2 failed; `/restore` the same; the `watch.ts` gate →
pr-sweep 1 failed, verb-gate 2 failed; adding `'ws-archive'` to
`UNGATED_BY_DECISION` → verb-gate 1 failed (the rot check); breaking the scanner
regex → verb-gate 6 failed. Server 1024 → 1037. Two judgements are recorded
rather than proved: the six exempt verbs are exempt because they predate the
fleet handshake carrying a verb list, and the `watch.ts` change moves a skewed
host from "try and fail every sweep" to "skip" — no state is written either way
and the level stays `merged`, so the archive still happens on the first sweep
after an upgrade, but it is a behaviour change in the auto-archive lane and the
lane flagged it as the one edit in its diff a reviewer should look at hardest.
The toast this gate then produced is deviation 170.

rendered "Archived · 3 · 0 B" — a confident total for three workspaces nobody

`archivedSummary` now returns `bytes: number | null` plus `unmeasured`, and one

(`.map(...).filter((b): b is number => b !== null)`) and no `?? 0` remains in the

where both fields are `number | null` and null means the window was not read.

(`server/src/limits.ts`) and `fleet.ts` passes it through as a non-null `limits`

The branch's own numbering has two claimants for the **eleventh** instance of the
