**158. The filtered-secret count is legible against the list it counts, and the
expand choice resets per target (fix round 3, critic2 uncovered, 785a7cd; fix
round 4, controller item 2, 67284c2).** `ReapSheet` capped the ignored list at
three entries while rendering the count of secret-shaped matches the noise filter
had dropped. A filtered entry is exactly the one that sorts last — ccd orders
`ignored` sensitive-first then bytes-descending (ccd:2561) and a noise-filtered
match leaves the entry non-sensitive (ccd:1996-2000) — so its NAME sat below the
cap while the NUMBER claiming it sat above. "Excluded must never mean invisible"
held for the count and failed for the name, which is the only thing a human can
judge a wrong filter by. ccd caps nothing on the wire, so showing it is enough:
when anything was filtered the entries are expanded by default, the collapsed
toggle states how many entries it hides ("show all 5"), and the note tracks the
list's actual state rather than promising what is not on screen. **The FILTER
POLICY itself is deliberately untouched** — that question is open with the human
partner and is not recorded here.

The one line carrying that behaviour across a target change was a mutation
survivor: the round claimed the reset in prose and shipped no test, so
`setShowAll(null)` could be deleted from `load()` with all 768 pwa tests green.
The new test walks the verifier's scenario — session A filtered one match so its
list opens expanded, the reader taps "show fewer", the target changes to session
B which filtered three, and B's own facts must not be outvoted by the previous
session's tap. Measured: deleting `setShowAll(null)` → 1 failed | 50 passed;
`setShowAll(false)`, the equally silent wrong default → 3 failed | 48 passed. The
class was then swept by grep rather than memory — per-target state on a sheet
REUSED across targets rather than remounted, since `app.tsx:59` renders
`<SessionScreen key={sessionId}>` so everything below it remounts — which found
one survivor, `SwapSheet`'s `target`, reported rather than taken because its
trigger is different. That is deviation 171.

**159. `ws-gc` reports a failed read as a failed read, not as a measurement (fix
round 4, round-3 verification P2; e0fbead).** Deviation 141's stderr rung makes
`_ws_gc_dirty` refuse a partially unreadable tree, which is right and stays. But
the function is a boolean and its two callers put a SENTENCE in front of a human:
a tree with ZERO uncommitted changes that git could only partially read was
printed `declined  <path> has uncommitted changes` and listed with STATE `dirty`.
Measured on git 2.43: a committed-clean worktree with one `chmod 000` tracked
directory gives rc 0, empty stdout, and the diagnostic on stderr. So the report
asserted something about files nobody looked at — the class this branch spent
eleven rounds closing — while the same file already owned the honest vocabulary
two functions away (`_ws_gc_reclaimable`: "refusing to remove a tree it cannot
describe") and `_ws_reap_eval`'s `tree-unreadable` verdict.

`_ws_gc_dirty` now carries its reason in `GC_DIRTY_STATE`
(`dirty | tree-unreadable | clean`) and `GC_DIRTY_WHY` (git's own first line of
stderr). Globals rather than a third exit status, deliberately:
`if _ws_gc_dirty …; then refuse` is the shape both callers use and the shape the
next caller will copy, and a third status would make it silently stop refusing on
the unreadable branch — "do not touch" stays exit 0 for every reason there is.
Swept as a class rather than as the reported instance: every `_gc_declined` in the
file was read, and one other producer had the same shape — `_ws_gc_merged` returns
1 for "not an ancestor", for "no origin/HEAD" and for `merge-base` exiting 128,
and the caller printed `$p is on unmerged branch $branch` for all three. It now
says "could not tell whether branch X is merged … refusing to remove $p on an
unproved merge" when nothing was compared. Two existing tests pinned the old
wording and were corrected rather than left; five mutants, all killed.

**160. The TWELFTH measurement forgery: `_ws_collect_ignored` refuses instead of
forging a size, and the reap sheet states no size it was not given (fix round 4,
round-3 item 3 routed from the ui-tsx verifier — 638fc29 for the producer and
5406103 for the display).** `_ws_collect_ignored`'s rung was
`[[ "$b" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || b=0`, and it forged in BOTH of `du`'s failure modes:
hard failure (du absent or stubbed, entry gone) recorded 0, and a PARTIAL read —
measured, GNU coreutils 9.4 — exits 1, writes `du: cannot read directory …:
Permission denied` to stderr, and STILL prints `5000` for a tree holding 14000,
which `^[0-9]+$` accepted. **0 looks like a bug; an under-count looks like an
answer.** Both land in `ignoredBytes`, which `ReapSheet.tsx:161` prints as a
stated total immediately above the Remove button.

The fix is NOT a null in the record. `ignoredBytes` is `number` on the wire
(`shared/api.ts:155`) and `humanBytes(null)` renders `0 B`, so a null would
relocate the forgery into the PWA rather than close it. It is the refusal this
function already owns — `return 1` plus `REAP_IGNREASON`, the same channel its
git-status and inside-walk rungs use, which every caller already handles
(`_ws_reap_eval` refuses `tree-unreadable`, `_ws_reap_tail` refuses rather than
finishing "on a guess", `_ws_gc_reclaimable` declines "refusing to remove a tree
it cannot describe"). A size ccd could not take is a tree ccd cannot describe.
**The test that pinned the 0 is fixed, not deleted:** `records 0 bytes rather than
an empty field when the size read fails` asserted `bytes: 0` and
`ignoredBytes: 0`; it is now `refuses the collection when an entry's size read
FAILS, and records no 0`, keeping the half it legitimately defended — an empty
`b` yields `"bytes":`, which is not JSON. A per-site `du` sweep over the whole
file found one other unguarded site, closed here: `cmd_ws_gc`'s grand total ran
`du -scb` with rc and stderr both discarded and `_ws_gc_human` only answers `-`
for a NON-numeric input, so a partial sum rendered as a figure under the sentence
"what removing all of them would free"; it now prints "total unmeasured … du
could not read all of them, so there is no figure to give."

The display half landed first on purpose, in the other lane: **the screen must
already be honest on the day the 0 stops being fabricated, and must not print
`NaN B` in the meanwhile.** One `sizeText(bytes: number | null | undefined)`
answers every size on the sheet, deliberately wider than `WsAudit` declares, so an
absent field degrades to the honest word rather than to arithmetic on `undefined`
— the not-in-git total, the worktree row (which already refused `null`, now one
spelling instead of two) and the confirm button, which was a THIRD copy of that
ternary. A `grep -rn humanBytes src/` class check found the sheet's fourth figure,
the only one that is a SUM and therefore the one that can be wrong with every
individual input intact: `clips.reduce((n, c) => n + c.bytes, 0)` silently
under-counts an unmeasured clip (`3 + null === 3`) and NaNs a missing one — a
PARTIAL TOTAL, which the house rule bans by name alongside `0`. It now states
what was measured and discloses the rest, in `ArchiveScreen`'s existing words.
Eight ReapSheet mutants were run — the commit's own prose says seven and its
table lists eight — and every branch of both helpers has a test that
dies with it; the three new fixtures go past the compile-time type on purpose and
say so, because `ignoredBytes: null`, the field absent entirely, and
`clips[].bytes: null` are what the RUNTIME can hand this component. Its producer,
`_ws_clip_manifest`, is deviation 167.

**161. The off-branch stash arm is reconciled with the fleet-wide rule it appeared
to contradict, and the refusal gets an exit (fix round 4, round-3 verification P3,
MINOR; f5ab9d5).** Deviation 142's arm attributes an anonymous `(no branch)` stash
by its base commit, so one taken on SHARED history is reachable from every branch
in the repository and every workspace of that project answers `stashes-present` —
a guard §7 gives no override. `_ws_reap_eval` rejects a fleet-wide no-override
stash refusal 2200 lines earlier, with a measurement; the arm's own comment then
cited that rejection as though this arm avoided the cost, and admitted three lines
later that it does not. The two could not both be read as written.

Reconciled in one place with the distinction stated rather than implied: what
`_ws_reap_eval` rejects is attribution by EXISTENCE ("refs/stash resolves ⇒
refuse"), which fires on a NAMED stash on another branch — main's own parked work
— that the operator has a standing reason to keep, so the wedge has no end date;
what this arm does is attribution by BASE COMMIT, firing only on an ANONYMOUS
entry that nothing in this design can associate with anything and that nobody
keeps on purpose. Different rules that SHARE the fleet-wide reach, now said once
at both sites and cross-referenced instead of denied at one and conceded at the
other.

**The narrowing stays rejected, for a stronger reason than the old comment gave:**
a reap only runs behind a MERGED PR, so after a true merge every commit of the
branch is already an ancestor of `origin/HEAD` and the narrowed arm would count
nothing at all — it would survive only for squash merges. A guard whose coverage
depends on which merge button a reviewer pressed is an argument about PR shape,
not a fact about stashes. What changes in behaviour is the REFUSAL: this file's own
test for accepting a no-override guard is whether the operator can get out of it,
the standard it states for `stash-unreadable`, and `stashes-present` carried no
remedy. It now says the entry counts against every workspace of the project and
hands over both commands, the keep one and the discard one, because only the
operator may choose. Pinned by a test whose fixture IS the fleet-wide case, so the
reach is recorded as chosen and not discovered.

**162. `isExecAllowed`'s declared-set gate is declared UNPINNABLE and its premise
pinned instead, and its two siblings are enumerated (fix round 4, round-3 P3;
8d982b5 and 3af6a14).** Deviation 147 was "two changes so both ask the same
question" and the report offered ONE measurement for it — a non-enumerable key
planted on a fixture. That measurement is produced entirely by the AUDITOR half
(`Reflect.ownKeys`). The lookup half, `GRANTABLE_COMMANDS.includes(cmd)`, was
covered by nothing, and the existing test that appeared to cover it passes either
way. Re-measured: delete that line and the agent suite is 193 passed / 12 files,
`tsc --noEmit -p agent` rc 0, and the cross-package subset test 39/39. Nothing
fails.

It is not pinnable, and that is a property of the design rather than a gap anyone
can close: a distinguishing input needs an OWN key of `EXEC_WHITELIST` outside
`GRANTABLE_COMMANDS`, and the literal is typed `Record<ExecCommand,…>`,
`auditExecWhitelist()` runs at module load over `Reflect.ownKeys` and refuses to
boot on one, and the object is frozen before any test runs. **Making it pinnable
was considered and REJECTED**: it would mean giving `isExecAllowed` an injectable
table the way `auditExecWhitelist` has one, and injection into the audit can only
cause a false THROW while injection into the lookup would create an allow-path
that does not exist today. A pin is not worth a bypass primitive in the one
function between the PWA and `exec`. So the line keeps its defence-in-depth role
and both the source comment and the test now SAY it is unpinned rather than
implying coverage; the misleading test is replaced by three that pin the PREMISE
— the table is frozen, its `Reflect.ownKeys` set IS the declared set, and an
undeclared key cannot survive module load. If any of those ever fails, the
declared-set line stops being redundant and starts holding the door, which is when
someone needs to read it. The class sweep then enumerated the two siblings in the
same function rather than assuming: deleting `Object.hasOwn(EXEC_WHITELIST, cmd)`
leaves agent 194/12 passing and tsc clean (unpinned, same reason), while deleting
`Array.isArray(entry)` is TS2322 at whitelist.ts:583 plus one failing test
(pinned). Recorded at the site so the next reader does not re-run it. Agent
191 → 193.

**163. The g1/g2/g4 bypass fixtures replay the construct the file actually ships
(fix round 4, round-3 P4; da83516).** `EXEC_WHITELIST` became
`} as const satisfies ExecWhitelist;` at whitelist.ts:309, but g1, g2 and g4 still
declared `const x: ExecWhitelist = { … }`, and so did the positive control's
`good`. Their stated purpose is to fail "against the same type the real site is
checked against", and they no longer did — a compile-failure pin in a construct the
shipped file does not use proves nothing about the shipped file, and
excess-property checking under `satisfies` has moved across TS releases before.
All four converted, with codes measured before and after and unchanged (g1 TS2353
at 13,3; g2 TS2353 at 11,3; g4 TS2741 at 14,12; `tsconfig.ok.json` still rc 0 with
empty output). The class is scanned rather than listed: a new test walks both
fixture directories and fails on any `: ExecWhitelist = {` literal, so a ninth
fixture written in the old form is caught too, while
`export const live: ExecWhitelist = EXEC_WHITELIST` is deliberately not matched —
checking the real value against the type is a different and still-wanted question.
Agent 193 → 194.

**164. The temp-dir class guard becomes a directory scan, and the second registry
is folded into the one registry (fix round 4, round-3 P2; 7eed9ec).** Deviation
150's guard read `const files = ['whitelist.test.ts', 'helpers.ts'];` — a
hardcoded two-file list — and its report claimed on the strength of it that the
pin "fails if any agent test file goes back to a bare `mkdtempSync`" and that "the
registry is now one per package". **Both claims were false when written.**
`agent/test/exec.test.ts` was in the same directory with its own `stubDirs` array,
its own `afterAll` and a bare `mkdtempSync` — precisely the pattern the class check
said had been resisted — and the verifier defeated the guard by dropping a new
file next to it (4 passed / 4).

Two changes. `exec.test.ts` routes its stub-binary directory through `mkTmp`; it
never leaked, since its hook was a hook, so this is not a leak fix but the
difference between importing the discipline and re-deriving it, which is what
decides whether the NEXT file gets it right. And the guard reads the directory
(`readdirSync(here)`) instead of naming two files, with the only hardcoded thing
left being a two-entry exemption map carrying a per-entry reason: `tmpHelpers.ts`
(IS the registry) and `contain-path.setup.ts` (a `setupFiles` module, not a test
module, already hook-cleaned, and forbidden to rewire). Both directions are
asserted so a stale exemption fails too; a second test checks that
`contain-path.setup.ts` still EARNS its exemption; the marker is assembled at
runtime and comments are stripped first, so the guard is neither its own first
offender nor fooled by prose about the pattern; and a final assertion confirms the
matcher still recognises the registry's own call, so "no offenders" cannot mean
"the matcher is broken". Proof: dropping the verifier's `zz-scratch-leak.test.ts`
in → tmpfixtures 1 failed (the exact mutation that gave 4 passed / 4);
reverting `exec.test.ts` → 1 failed; turning contain-path's `afterAll` into a
trailing `rmSync` → 1 failed. The rest of the class was enumerated by grep across
all four packages, with `pwa/test/contrast.test.ts`'s third local registry listed
as out-of-lane and left. Agent 190 → 191.

**165. The auditor's own escapes, closed four ways (fix round 4, verify3-ui-css
P1/P2/P3/P4; e77a8f5, ccbee8b, 6b2a610, a3e1daa).** Deviation 134's auditor
shipped the claim "this is what makes the callouts unforgeable", and the verifier
forged it. Four defects, each of which let the reported 2.44:1 blocker shape — or
an unregistered fade — walk through the real gate binary with `ALL 234 PASS` and
exit 0.

*Variants were matched on the whole selector STRING* (P1, MAJOR). `contextsFor`
compared `sel.startsWith(base)` with the remainder rejected if it contained a
space, plus a same-file filter, so three spellings escaped: a grouped rule (stored
whole by `rulesOf`, so its remainder contains a space), an added ancestor
(`.msg-assist .md-body .callout[…]`), and an added qualifier on an ancestor
(`.msg-assist[data-md] .callout[…]`). `variantSuffix(sel, base)` now splits both
selectors into a selector LIST at bracket/paren depth zero, takes each side's
SUBJECT COMPOUND — the rightmost compound, the element the rule paints — and asks
whether the candidate's subject is the base's subject plus compound qualifiers.
Ancestor chains and the file are no longer part of the comparison. This
OVER-approximates, which is the safe direction for a gate, and it costs nothing
today: the measured-row set on the live tree is byte-identical to the old
matcher's, 140 rows, ADDED [] REMOVED []. The same string comparison one function
down (the `::before` host looked up by exact `file selector` key) falls back to the
same subject match. The unforgeability claim is replaced with one that is true,
plus the disclosure of what is still not covered (`:is(.callout)[data-x]`,
`[class~='callout'][data-x]` — restatements that are not textually
base-subject-plus-qualifiers; closing those needs a selector engine).

*The auditor read the FIRST declaration; CSS applies the LAST* (P2, MAJOR). Any
rule with a duplicated `color`, `background` or `opacity` was audited against a
value nothing paints, and `background: <fallback>; background: var(--x)` is the
standard progressive-enhancement idiom, so this was one ordinary rule away from a
real mismeasurement. `declOf` now keeps the last match. The fourth escape was a
second bug of the same species: `bgOf` was
`declOf('background') ?? declOf('background-color')`, treating the longhand as a
FALLBACK for the shorthand when they write the SAME cascaded value and the answer
is source order; `bgOf` now takes the last of either, which also gets the reverse
right. Class check by parse, not memory: all 589 live rules scanned for a property
declared more than once → 0, and for rules declaring both `background` and
`background-color` → 0, so this was latent, and the measured-row set is
byte-identical before and after. Every other declaration read in `audit.mjs` was
checked for the same shape and neither `localVars`/`customProps` (built through
`Object.fromEntries`, where a later duplicate already wins) nor `keyframeTroughs`
(`Math.min` over all stops) needed changing.

*The auditor's failure branches were untested* (P3, MINOR). Four "could not measure
something" branches could each be replaced with a bare `continue` with all 145
tests green, and two of them were exactly the claims the lane's own report made in
prose. **A gate whose failure branches are untested is not a gate — the
unmeasurable direction is where a defect becomes a silence.** Swept by mutant
rather than by memory: every `problems.push` in `audit.mjs` (12 sites) neutered in
turn and each of the five `stale` directions set to `[]`, which found the four the
review named plus five more of the identical species (a pseudo-element painting an
unresolvable colour; an `INHERITED_GROUNDS` entry whose rule was renamed, or that
stopped setting a colour, or whose colour is unresolvable; an `OPACITY_REGISTRY`
pair with an unresolvable colour; and three stale-registry directions). All eleven
are pinned by mutation proofs against the real gate binary, and re-running the whole
sweep afterwards kills at least one test at 12/12 `problems.push` sites and 5/5
stale directions. The remaining SILENT skips are enumerated and NOT closed: they
are the ~230 colour-without-background rules whose ground is DOM knowledge, already
disclosed in the file header.

*The `knownBelowFloor` hatch survived in the gate under an assertion that could not
fail* (P4, MINOR). `contrast.test.ts:783` (the commit body says `:531`; the
assertion is at 783 in the file it was measured against) was
`expect(Object.keys(entry).sort()).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining([]))`, which
matches ANY key set — measured directly: `['knownBelowFloor','whatever']` passes,
`[]` passes, `['literally','anything','at','all']` passes. It sat directly above
the only real guard and read as a second one. Replaced with the check it was
pretending to be (an entry's key set must be exactly `['pairs']` or exactly
`['noText']`), and proved load-bearing with a hatch spelled `knownBelowFloorX`,
which the explicit guard does not name: the dead assertion passes and the new one
fails. And `audit.mjs`'s `if (!('pairs' in entry)) continue;` meant the GATE
silently skipped an `OPACITY_REGISTRY` entry carrying neither key — measured:
replacing the `.tool-dot--run` entry with `{ knownBelowFloor: … }` gives
`node design/contrast-check.mjs` → ALL 232 PASS, exit 0, while the suite threw.
**Gate and suite disagreeing about whether the hatch exists IS the hatch.** It is
now a `problems` entry. The two other shaped registries were class-checked the
same way and neither has a key its consumers ignore. pwa 768 → 817 across the four
commits, gate `ALL 234 PASS` exit 0 throughout.

**166. The `.offline-banner` referral is withdrawn, because the coverage claim
behind it was false (fix round 4, verify3-ui-css P5, MINOR; 1292717).** The css
lane's one out-of-lane item routed a render assertion for `.offline-banner` to
another lane on the grounds that "Nothing tests it". Both states were already
pinned — `fleet-screen.test.tsx`'s "shows a persistent offline banner when conn is
'down'" asserts `getByText('Reconnecting…')`, and `offline.test.ts` asserts
`getByText('Last known state — connecting…')` and then its absence once the socket
opens. Measured rather than read: four mutants on `FleetScreen.tsx` — each banner
deleted, and each banner's condition narrowed — every one failed exactly one of
those two tests. The item is withdrawn so no phantom work travels to another lane.
What WAS missing is the pointer, so the fleet.css comment that justifies removing
the fade (deviation 153) and the contrast.test.ts case that restates it now name
the two tests. Comment-only.

**167. The THIRTEENTH measurement forgery: clip sizes stop being invented, and the
type stops forcing it (cross-lane seam pass; e53c774).** `_ws_clip_manifest` sized
a directory entry with `b=$(du -sb …); [[ "$b" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || b=0` and a file
entry with `stat -c %s … || echo 0`. Both answered a FAILED READ with a number, on

**172. The contrast auditor reads CSS case-insensitively, as browsers do (fix round
6, final2-gates F2, MINOR; de2daa7).** `COLOR:` / `BACKGROUND:` / `OPACITY:` are
valid declarations a browser paints, and every one of them was invisible to
`declOf`, `bgOf`, the fade sweep and the keyframe sweep — so the reported 2.44:1
blocker shape forged the whole gate to `ALL 234 PASS` just by being written in
uppercase, and an uppercase stop inside an ALREADY-registered animation deepened its
trough without changing the registry key. Property names are ASCII
case-insensitive (CSS Syntax 3 §3.1) and so are function names and at-rule
keywords; CUSTOM property names are not (CSS Variables 1 §2). So the fold is applied
everywhere except there, and `declOf` switches on the `--` prefix rather than taking
a flag a caller can forget. `resolveColor` (`VAR()`, `RGB()`,
`COLOR-MIX(IN SRGB, …)`), `blockBody` (`:ROOT`, `[DATA-THEME='light']`, searched by
regex rather than `indexOf`) and `keyframeTroughs` follow, the last taking its block
body from the MATCH POSITION rather than re-finding it by string, because a
case-insensitive find plus a case-sensitive re-find is how this kind of fold goes
wrong. Enumerated rather than remembered: a sweep over every declaration in all six
stylesheets found ZERO non-lowercase paint property names today, so this is an
adversarial hole rather than a shipped defect — but it is the textual-matching class
the file's own header condemns.

**173. The gate measures the variant SHAPE rather than its spelling, a live 3.03:1
AA failure is fixed, and the gate publishes what it CANNOT measure (fix round 6,
final2-gates F1 MAJOR and F3 MINOR, committed together because F3's `paintOf` is
the primitive F1's variant route needs; 18fa23d).**

The live defect: `.code-block-copy:hover, .code-block-copy[data-copied]` painted
11px uppercase mono text (`--text-2xs`, so the floor is 4.5, not 3) in
`var(--accent)` on the code block bar — **3.37:1 on the well the GROUNDS entry named,
3.03:1 on the bar it is actually in**. `[data-copied]` is not hover-only:
`MessageBubble.tsx` holds it 1600 ms after every copy and it is the state that
renders "Copied". Fixed with a new token `--accent-on-well` (#45D67E, the dark
accent) in the CODE WELLS block of tokens.css that is deliberately never overridden
in light — because wells ARE dark in both themes and the light `--accent` (#0E7B3F)
is tuned for paper — giving 9.91 dark / 8.62 light, with the focus ring on the same
element moving with it (3.37 → 9.9 against a 3 floor). Two neighbours corrected while
in there: the GROUNDS entry for `.code-block-copy` said `--bg-well` when the button
is inside `.code-block-bar` (`--well-bar-bg`, 5% ink over the well), which flattered
every ratio on that bar by ~1.4; and `.code-block-lang`, its sibling on the same bar,
was in the uncovered census with nothing grounding it and now measures 5.95 / 5.18.

The shape, not the spelling: `contextsFor` returned only the base unless the base
declared custom properties, and then admitted only variants that REBOUND one of
them. Enumerated with the auditor's own exports rather than from memory — **20 rules
in the tree are variants of a self-grounded rule that change paint, and only 5 were
measured.** The predicate is now "does this rule change one of the three inputs to
the pair" (ink, ground, or a property the base resolves against), and four routes
ground a colour rule instead of two: VARIANTS now include `color`-only,
`background`-only, and a second rule with the very same selector (where
`variantSuffix` answers null by design, so that case is handled explicitly), with
same-qualifier rules MERGED so that splitting the ink across one rule and the ground
across another is not a hiding place — merged contexts are ADDITIONAL to the
per-rule ones, never a replacement, because an earlier draft replaced them and
silently re-opened the three spellings deviation 165 closed, specificity not being
source order. DESCENDANTS are new: a colour rule with no ground of its own whose
selector NAMES a self-grounded ancestor is measured on that ancestor's ground,
through every variant context of it, with no DOM knowledge involved because the
selector says it. And a rule with a `SELF_GROUNDED_EXEMPT` reason is now exempt
wherever it is reached, which surfaced `.btn-ghost:disabled` (`--ink-disabled`, 2.85
/ 2.63) for the first time; it takes the same WCAG 1.4.3 inactive-control exemption
its three siblings already had.

F3: `background-image` was not read at all, so a rule painting its own opaque ground
with a gradient and putting unreadable text on it was skipped SILENTLY,
contradicting the header's own "an unparsed paint is a FAIL, never a skip". Both
spellings are read now and a non-null answer is a loud `problems` entry naming the
two honest ways out. Zero live instances (grep-verified), so this is the hole the
next gradient walks through.

**The census is the part that generalises.** Rather than keep adding shapes it can
measure, the audit now computes what it CANNOT: `report.uncovered` is every colour
rule no route could ground, `counts.uncovered` is the number, the gate PRINTS it,
and `--uncovered` lists it. **196 before, 186 after.** The header's old claim that
all of them "inherit from an arbitrary ancestor, which a stylesheet parser cannot
recover" was false for 20 of them; it is true of what is left, and the suite
re-derives that independently instead of taking the sentence's word for it. Proved
by running the real gate command against a mutated copy of the tree — twelve
escapes, every one `exit=0 :: ALL 234 PASS` before and `exit 1` after, including
both review mutants from the finding. pwa 844 → 889 at this commit; gate
`ALL 272 PASS`, exit 0.

**174. Every hand-typed copy of a tokens.css colour is bound to it (fix round 6,

**175. The containment harness stops leaking `/tmp` on a module-load throw (fix
round 6, final review tests finding 1, MAJOR; 5508f1a).**
`contain-path.setup.ts` made its stub directory at MODULE SCOPE of a `setupFiles`
entry and removed it in an `afterAll`. A setup file's body runs BEFORE the test
module is imported, so a test module that THROWS AT IMPORT left the directory behind
with no vitest hook to remove it: one leaked directory per failed-to-import file.

**That failure is this project's own security design working as intended.**
`auditExecWhitelist()` runs at module load and `refuseToBoot` THROWS (deviations 129
and 148), so every over-permission mutant turns most of this suite into import
failures — the harness leaked WORST on exactly the event it exists to cause, and
mutation sweeps are this project's whole method. The host hit 95% disk the day this
was found, with `/tmp` at 55 GB and 697 entries from this leak class. Measured
before: one throwing test file → `1 failed | 12 passed`, and
`ls -d /tmp/ccrc-agent-containpath-*` went 98 → 99; the reviewer's real mutant
(`--expect` dropped from the ws-reap grant) leaked 10, twice.

**The first fix was tried and rejected on measurement**: `process.on('exit')` in the
setup file is present, readable, and skipped, because vitest's default pool is
`forks` and tinypool destroys worker processes — the new pin still failed 2 runs in
12. An 80% fix on a leak that has cost this host twice is not a fix. What shipped is
a run-scoped root: `test/contain-path.globalsetup.ts` runs in vitest's MAIN process
before any worker forks, makes one root, hands it to the workers through the
environment they inherit, and removes it in the teardown it returns, which the pool
cannot skip. The setup file makes its per-file directory inside that root and still
removes it in `afterAll`, and falls back to `os.tmpdir()` if the global setup is ever
unwired, so **containment itself never depends on the janitor** — the stub `tmux`
and `gh` are still made and still put earliest on PATH.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, and this is the decline worth keeping: sweeping the other
~100 `ccrc-agent-containpath-*` directories. Deleting one a CONCURRENT agent run is
using takes the stub `tmux` off its PATH and makes `exec.test.ts`'s
`tmux kill-server` resolve to the real binary — the mechanism that has killed the
live fleet four times — and sibling lanes were running this suite on this box at the
time. Stale dirs cost disk; a wrong sweep costs eleven sessions. Pinned
behaviourally rather than by introspection: `contain-path.test.ts` spawns a real
vitest whose test module throws at import, with `TMPDIR` pointed at a directory of
its own and `setupFiles`/`globalSetup` DERIVED from the real `vitest.config.ts`, then
counts what is left, with two positive controls guarding the "zero" reading and the
inherited run root stripped from the child env so the count cannot read zero for the
wrong reason. Deviation 164's exemption for this file was conditional on "cleanup is
a hook" — a condition that was true and insufficient — and now requires the root
too. Three mutants killed (globalSetup unwired; the setup ignoring the root;
the teardown dropping its `rmSync`). Agent 194 → 195, 15 consecutive full runs green,
and the leak measured closed: 5 full runs with a module-load throw injected,
`ccrc-agent-containpath-*` 100 → 100.

**176. `deploy.sh` verifies the agent restart, and fails loudly when it loops (fix
round 6, final review gates finding 5, MINOR; a501b12).** `deploy/deploy.sh:47` ends
the SERVER path with `sleep 1 && curl -fsS "$HEALTH_URL"`. The AGENT path ended at
`systemctl --user restart ccrc-agent.service`, which returns success the moment
systemd forks and says nothing about whether what it forked stayed up. The asymmetry
lands exactly where the agent's own security design puts its last line of defence:
every over-permission a TYPE can see is already caught by the `npm run build` earlier
in the same chain, so the only states that reach `refuseToBoot` on a host are the
ones no type can see — a hand-edited `dist/whitelist.js`, a non-array prefix, a
symbol key — and with `Restart=always` and `RestartSec=3` those produced an agent
crash-looping every three seconds behind a deploy that exited 0. **The one residual
class the throw exists for was the one class the deploy would not notice**, on the
eve of this branch's deployment.

`deploy/verify-service.sh` is appended as the LAST link of the agent remote command's
`&&` chain, so its exit status is the ssh exit status and `set -e` aborts on it. Not
a health curl, because the agent has no HTTP routes — its `createServer()` exists to
carry a WebSocket upgrade, bound to 127.0.0.1 behind a bearer token. MainPID
stability rather than `is-active`, because a crash-looping unit spends most of a 3 s
cycle in `activating (auto-restart)`, which `is-active` rejects, but not all of it: a
single sample can land in the up window, and two samples either side of an
observation window LONGER than `RestartSec` cannot. `NRestarts` was deliberately not
used — its reset semantics across a manual restart are a systemd version detail,
while a PID that did not change is a PID that did not change on every version.
Read-only throughout. Verified end to end against real systemd on the LIVE fleet host
with no unit created, started, stopped or reset: a healthy unit → rc 0 "MainPID …
stable across 2s"; an inactive unit → rc 1 with banner and journal tail; and a
session unit genuinely sitting in `activating` → rc 1 with banner, a real restart loop
caught by the real script rather than a stub. **Stated rather than implied:** no
transient probe unit was created to force a loop end to end, because the fleet is live
on this host and a scratch unit is the wrong risk for a case the stub covers exactly.
Also here: `systemctl` joins `tmux` and `gh` in `contain-path.setup.ts`, because it is
in `FORBIDDEN_COMMANDS` and `systemctl --user stop ccrc.service` is the same blast
radius as `tmux kill-server`; the list's admission bar is now written down —
mutates state outside the fixture, or spends a host credential — with `journalctl`
excluded under it and `bash`/`node`/`git` excluded because stubbing them would break
the runner. Four mutations verified, including that the verify call is pinned by chain
POSITION rather than by grep, and that the observation window is asserted to exceed
the unit file's `RestartSec` across two files. Agent 195 → 204. NOT fixed and
reported rather than improved: the server path's failure output is a bare `curl`
error with no journal tail — that is the finding's own baseline standard, and the eve
of a deploy is the wrong time to widen it.

**177. `ws-gc --prune`'s orphan gate was INVERTED for a detached HEAD (fix round 6,
final review destructive F1; 3578cc2).** The one counter-example on this branch to
"no sequence of actions destroys a workspace without a human first seeing an accurate
description of what would be destroyed". `rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` answers the
literal string `HEAD` for a detached worktree, so

    if [[ -n "$branch" && "$branch" != HEAD ]] && ! _ws_gc_merged …

ran the mergedness proof ONLY when a branch survives the removal — the case where
nothing is lost either way — and SKIPPED it for the case where `git worktree remove`
deletes `$main/.git/worktrees/<slug>/` with its HEAD reflog and leaves the commit
referenced by nothing at all. **The guard existed for the case where a ref survives
and was absent for the case where none does.** Three rungs now, in `_ws_gc_merged`'s
own `unprovable` polarity: HEAD unread → decline; detached → decline, naming the
short sha; on a branch → the existing merged proof. The now-provably-dead
`[[ -n "$branch" && "$branch" != HEAD ]]` conjunct in front of `git branch -d` is
removed rather than kept, so nothing in the arm reads as though the detached case can
reach it. Second half, independent of the first: `_ws_gc_reclaimable`'s
`has nothing ignored — everything in it is in git` is printed on the line above
`reclaimed removed orphan worktree …` and is the reassurance a reader uses to
authorise it, while that function measures the ignored set and nothing else; it now
says only that. Pinned by four new cases — `grep -n detach` over that file returned
nothing before them, so the FALSE arm of the old conjunct had never been exercised by
any test. Mutation: disabling both new rungs fails 3; restoring the old sentence
fails 1. Server 1071 → 1075. This fix wrote the fifteenth measurement forgery on its
way past; see deviation 184.

**178. The FOURTEENTH measurement forgery, and the first to land on the
delete-confirmation surface itself: a refusal is now distinguishable from a clean
scan at every layer (fix round 6, final review tests F3; 69a779d).** `cmd_ws_audit`
printed `_ws_reap_reset`'s defaults on EVERY verdict: `"dirty":[]`, `"ignored":[]`,
`"ignoredCount":0`, `"ignoredBytes":0`, `"sensitive":[]`, `"sensitiveFiltered":0`,
`"stashes":0`, `"fetchedAt":0`. `ReapSheet` renders those rows unconditionally and the
refusal paragraph comes AFTER them, so a workspace refused in Phase A — before
`_ws_collect_ignored`, before the stash read, before the PR fetch — was described to
the human as *"uncommitted: none / not in git: 0 entries, 0 B / stashes: none"*, and
*"merged in #? (proof: none), 20669 days ago"*. Every PWA-reachable Phase-A refusal
(`registry-branch-drift`, `foreign-worktree`, `no-worktree-record`, `detached-head`,
`incomplete-registry`) leaves the worktree ON DISK, holding whatever those rows deny.

Reachability is stated because it decides the severity: the Remove button is NOT
reachable in this state — it renders on `verdict === 'reapable'` alone, and ccd
converts the one reapable-without-measurement path to `reap-interrupted`. The harm is
a false description above a refusal, not a delete.

Closed at all three layers, because any one alone leaves it standing. In **ccd**,
`REAP_IGNSCANNED` is the proof the scan ran, set on `_ws_collect_ignored`'s single
success path, and the ignored/sensitive/filtered block is skipped without it; `dirty`
is read with rc AND stderr into a temp file (Phase B's own rule — a partial read exits
0 with the diagnostic on stderr) and is `null` for no-directory or a read that did not
finish; `REAP_STASHES` and `REAP_FETCHED` reset to `""` rather than 0 and print
through the `null` guard `REAP_PRNUM` has carried since deviation 10. On the **wire**,
EIGHT fields widen to `| null` in `WsAudit` — `dirty`, `ignored`, `ignoredCount`,
`ignoredBytes`, `sensitive`, `sensitiveFiltered`, `stashes` and `merge.fetchedAt`
— with the reason written where the next producer will read it. (The commit body
and the type's own docstring both say "six", counting the six in one block and
naming `stashes` and `merge.fetchedAt` separately; the diff widens eight.) On the **screen**, one shared `NOT_SCANNED` constant,
deliberately worded apart from `sizeText`'s "unknown" (attempted and failed) — which
the seam pass's own residual asked for by name — with the unrecoverable-content note
and the filtered-secrets note suppressed alongside the list they describe. `dirty` is
nulled on a narrower condition than the rest, deliberately: `cmd_ws_audit` reads the
tree itself, so a refusal with a readable worktree still carries a real list, and that
is pinned in both directions. 11 new tests; mutation — an unconditional ignored block
fails 1, `dirty_json="[]"` fails 3, stashes and fetchedAt fabricating 0 fail 1 each,
and `ReapSheet` rendering `?? 0` / `?? []` fails 4.

**179. The completed-reap RECEIPT stops reporting `bytes:0` for a tree nobody sized
(fix round 6, final review tests F2; 86452c7).** `_ws_reap_tail` held the last of the
three identical `bytes=$(_ws_gc_bytes "$workdir"); … || bytes=0` lines — the archive
manifest and the audit's `worktreeBytes` were closed in earlier rounds (deviations 118
and 120) — and it is the one printed AFTER the irreversible delete, so
`{"reaped":…,"bytes":0}` states "this deletion reclaimed nothing" from a `du` that
never completed. `ReapResult.bytes` becomes `number | null` on the wire for the reason
the class keeps recurring. Mutation G4 had survived the whole 58-test file in BOTH
directions because nothing read the field, and pinning it corrected the review as
well: `_ws_reap_tail` sizes the worktree at its TOP, before (f) removes it, so a
resume whose kill landed at (d) still has a tree to measure and reports a real figure
— it is only a resume re-entering PAST (f) that has nothing to size. Both resume
shapes are now asserted in opposite directions so neither can drift into the other.
`grep -nE '\|\| *[A-Za-z_]+=0\b'` over ccd then returned one live site, which is
deviation 181.

**180. The reap sheet's "kept" row stops overstating what survives the delete (fix
round 6, final review tests F5; 014a464).** The row read
`${result?.attic ?? shown.commitsAheadOfBase} commits pinned in the attic`, so
BEFORE the reap the figure was `commitsAheadOfBase` —
`git rev-list --count "$base..refs/heads/$branch"` — which is a different quantity
from what `_ws_attic_pin` pins: one ref per DISTINCT REFLOG SHA, `sort -u | head -200`,
plus the tip. Unequal in both directions, since amends and rebases push the reflog
above the commit count while past 200 the cap truncates, so on the sheet that describes
an irreversible delete the row could promise MORE retention than the attic provides.
**Overstating what survives is the dangerous direction on this surface.** Before the
reap the row now states the RULE, which is exact and needs no measurement; after it,
`result.attic` is the count `_ws_attic_pin` itself returned. `commitsAheadOfBase` is
deliberately left unrendered — it is a real figure in `ccd ws-audit`'s own output and
was only ever wrong as an answer to "how much of this survives". The existing
zero-attic test's rationale is updated rather than left stale: the distinguishing
mutant moved from `??` → `||` to `!== undefined` → truthiness, the same falsy 0.

**181. `commitsAheadOfBase` answers `null` for a comparison that did not run, and a
test that was holding the 0 in place is inverted (fix round 6, final review
destructive F2; 9962273).** The last surviving `|| x=0` in ccd; `grep -nE
'\|\| *[A-Za-z_]+=0\b'` over the file now returns only comments. Both arms were
fabricating and both are reachable: the initialiser `ahead=0` stands when the `if` is
skipped entirely (`$base` does not resolve, or `$branch` is empty), and the fallback
`|| ahead=0` stands when the `rev-list --count` inside it fails. ccd had already
litigated this exact value 1,340 lines earlier — `_pr_state_one` (ccd:1650) writes
`ahead=""` under *"`""` is UNMEASURED, not zero. `ahead=0` is the claim 'this branch is
level with base' … a ref that does not resolve has not been measured against
anything"* — so the file disagreed with itself. `WsAudit.commitsAheadOfBase` is
`number | null` on the wire. **And a test was holding it in place:** `publishes a
NUMBER for commitsAheadOfBase even when the count fails` asserted the 0. It is
inverted rather than deleted, because the half it legitimately defended is real — an
EMPTY `$ahead` interpolates as `"commitsAheadOfBase":`, which is not JSON, and an
unparseable manifest takes the refusal down with it; `null` satisfies that and states
the truth, 0 satisfies it and states a falsehood.

**182. The "records no 0" case asserts an invariant that is now true, in a form that
can tell (fix round 6, final review tests F4; 9ff65cd, tests only).**
`ccd-ws-audit.test.ts`'s comment claimed *"the forged figures are ABSENT, not zero: a
refusal document carries no ignored manifest at all"*, and its assertions were
`expect(a.ignored ?? [], …).toEqual([])`, `expect(a.ignoredBytes ?? 0).toBe(0)` and
`expect(a.ignoredCount ?? 0).toBe(0)`. **Two independent defects.** The premise was
FALSE of the ccd it described — `cmd_ws_audit` emitted `"ignoredCount":0,
"ignoredBytes":0` on every verdict, which is deviation 178 — and `x ?? 0` then
`.toBe(0)` is the ONE form that cannot distinguish absence from a literal 0, i.e.
exactly the discrimination the test's own title claims to make. A comment and a test
can be wrong together and neither notices. Both are now true of what ships: the fields
are PRESENT and NULL, asserted with `toBeNull()`, with `hasOwnProperty` for
present-ness and a `JSON.stringify` regex for the "no 0 anywhere" claim the old form
could not make. Null rather than absent is deliberate and the comment says why — a
dropped field reads as an older server at every consumer, while null is ccd positively
stating that nothing was measured. Class sweep, mechanical: the `?? 0`-then-`toBe`
grep over `server/test`, `pwa/test` and `agent/test` now returns only two
`Object.keys(s ?? {})` shape checks and one collision-index message, none of them a
measurement, and the per-field grep returns four assertions on genuinely measured
reapable documents plus `ccd-archive`'s `still records a genuine ZERO-byte measurement
as 0` — the other half of the rule, which must stay.

**183. The three INFO residuals on the destructive path, and the tombstone gets a
declared type (fix round 6; 304ce71).** Four small things, closed together.

(a) **F4** — `ws-gc --prune`'s dead-reg arm printed a `reclaimed` for work it did not
do. `_ws_gc_scan` refuses to reconstruct an id when the registry disagrees with itself
("a prune keyed off a wrong reconstruction would delete a different session's entry")
and reported that as `dead-reg <id> ?`; the prune arm then recomposed
`"$project-$slug"` — the literal `<id>-?` — purged nothing with it, and printed an
unconditional `reclaimed dead registry entry <id>-?` plus a footer increment, on every
run for ever. The `?` could not glob (quoted expansion), so nothing was ever at risk;
the defect is the fabricated success line. The row now has its own state, `reg-broken`,
and its own arm, which DECLINES and names the inconsistency. **A sentinel inside a
field the consumer recomposes was the bug; a state it can recognise is the fix.**

(b) **F5a** — `_ws_gc_reclaimable` justified "the bytes are numeric" by citing the
collector's `[[ … ]] || b=0`, which deviation 160 replaced with a refusal. The
conclusion survived and the reason did not, which is the shape of stale comment that
later licenses putting the coercion back "because the sum needs it".

(c) **F5b** — `_ws_reap_eval`'s `unpushed-commits` detail printed
" commit(s) are not on the remote" for a `rev-list` that failed: a count with the
number missing, about a comparison that never ran. Direction unchanged, sentence
fixed, both arms pinned.

(d) **the seam pass's residual #1** — the TOMBSTONE, the record that outlives the
workspace, had no declared type at all, so `clips[].bytes: null` (deviation 167)
existed there purely as ccd behaviour. `WsTombstone` is declared in `shared/api.ts`
with the same `number | null` as `WsAudit.clips`, and a new test asserts a null
survives BOTH hops: `_ws_tombstone`'s write and `_ws_tombstone_reclip`'s
`python3 json` round-trip — the hop where a null would most plausibly be coerced —
while every other field is byte-identical across the reclip.

**184. The FIFTEENTH measurement forgery, written by the rung that fixed a
destroy-without-confirmation bug (final ship-blocker; f983cdc).** Deviation 177's new
detached-HEAD decline said *"nothing else references its commits"*. That is a
reachability claim, and `_ws_gc_prune_row` never looks at a single ref: it printed the
identical sentence for a commit with three refs pointing at it and for one with none.
The comment four lines above already conceded the point — "this arm cannot tell that
from a lost hour's work" — while the sentence below asserted the opposite. **The
honest statement and the false one shipped in the same commit, which is why review did
not catch it.** Safe-direction: it is a DECLINE either way and nothing is destroyed.
Fixed anyway, because "a number is a measurement" (deviation 10) governs prose as well
as JSON, and a refusal justified by a fact nobody established teaches the operator to
discount the next refusal — on a command whose other refusals are the last thing
between a sweep and someone's committed work. It now says only what the rung knows:
there is no branch naming the commits, so ccd cannot prove anything else reaches them,
so it stops. Two tests, both proved load-bearing; the second is the one the old
sentence got flatly backwards — a tag is planted on the detached commit so it
demonstrably IS referenced, and the message must be unchanged, because this arm still
has not looked.

**185. The SIXTEENTH measurement forgery: an unreadable clips directory issued a consent
token to destroy it (post-final round; `ccrc/r5-clips`).** `_ws_clip_manifest` answered
`[]` for a clips directory that EXISTS but cannot be enumerated, and `ReapSheet` renders
`clips.length === 0` as **"clips: none"** on a sheet whose Remove button is reachable.
`clipsDigest` is built from the same manifest, so both sides agreed on an emptiness
neither measured and the fingerprint could not catch it — the shape deviation 121 closed
for dotfiles, reappearing for the whole directory. Reproduced by execution under an
isolated `$HOME`: `verdict = reapable`, `clips = []`, **token issued** — and then
`rm -rf` on that directory returns 1 and it survives, so the reap it authorised would
have stranded the workspace half-deleted. After: `verdict = clips-unreadable`,
`clips = null`, no token.

Two things the fix got right that the brief for it got wrong. **First**, the brief said to
keep the `[]` on stdout and merely return non-zero; that leaves the forgery fully formed
for the two consumers that *cannot see a status they were never handed* — `| sha256sum`
reports the pipe's, and a `$( )` inside a `printf` argument list swallows it. It now
prints nothing, so a status-blind future consumer writes `"clips":` and fails to parse:
loudly wrong beats quietly reassuring, and empty-stdout-plus-non-zero is this file's own
precedent (`cmd_ws_audit`'s `_json_str` probe). **Second**, `find`'s exit status alone is
not a usable predicate. Measured, GNU findutils 4.9.0: mode `000` exits 1 with EMPTY
stdout (opendir failed); mode `400` **also** exits 1 but with the COMPLETE list of names
(readdir fine, every per-entry `stat` failed). Identical status, opposite facts — and the
mode-`400` case is already answered honestly by deviation 167's per-entry `null`s and
pinned by an existing test. So the guard is `rc != 0 AND no records came back`, and the
mutant that drops the second conjunct kills that pinned honest answer.

Each consumer answers for itself, deliberately differently: the **audit** emits `null` and
a third verdict branch withholds the token (covering the window between the eval's read
and the wire's); the **fingerprint** refuses, which is what makes a stale token fail
instead of matching a digest over unread emptiness; the **tombstone** records `null`,
never refuses, because it is the record that outlives the workspace and the resume arm
runs with the worktree already gone — refusing there converts one unreadable directory
into a workspace stranded forever. `WsAudit.clips` and `WsTombstone.clips` are
`{name,bytes}[] | null`. Ten mutants, all killed; `[[ -d "$dir" ]]`, a disclosed mutation
survivor since deviation 121, now takes 41 tests with it.

**186. Destructive finding F8 — RULED by the human partner, and already implemented
(`785a7cd`).** Deviation 117's F3 noise filter drops genuine secrets from the one guard
with no override: a gitignored `secrets.py` holding a real AWS key returns
`sensitive: []`, `sensitiveFiltered: 2`, verdict `reapable`. Honestly surfaced — both
files appear by name in `audit.ignored` and the sheet states the filtered count — but the
sheet capped the ignored list at three entries. Put to the human partner three times with
three options; ruled **keep the filtering policy, fix the display**.

The lane that implemented it found the sharper form of the residual than the one put to
the human partner: a filtered entry is not merely *able* to fall outside the cap, it is
**reliably** outside it. ccd emits `ignored` sorted sensitive-first then bytes-descending
(ccd:2561) and a noise-filtered match leaves `sensitive` at 0 (ccd:1996-2000), so the
filtered entry always sorts last — the NUMBER above the cap, the NAME below it. It also
implemented it better than the controller specified: "render filtered entries, cap the
rest" is unbuildable, because the wire cannot distinguish a filtered match from an
ordinary non-sensitive file — both arrive `sensitive: 0`. Expanding the whole list
whenever anything was filtered is the only correct form. `ReapSheet.tsx:213`:
`const expanded = showAll ?? (shown !== null && (shown.sensitiveFiltered ?? 0) > 0)`,
with a `null` count meaning the filter never ran and so has hidden nothing. The reader may
still collapse it, and the collapsed toggle always says how many entries it is hiding.

### What these rounds DECLINED, and why

Recorded because the reasoning is the durable part, and because a decline that is not
written down is indistinguishable from an oversight next time.

- **The house-wide `die` refactor (integration docket 9).** `die()` exits a sourced
  shell mid-batch. Declined by the lane that owns ccd as the house-wide refactor the
  brief rules out, and the decline held on scope: production reaches every verb
  through the `BASH_SOURCE` dispatcher as a subprocess and `runCcdOr502` turns the
  non-zero exit into a 502, so the exposure is the sourcing test harness and
  hand-written batch loops, not a product path. The final destructive review re-raised
  it against `cmd_ws_restore` and reached the same verdict — "test-harness fragility,
  not a product path". The caveat the lane disclosed and this document carries:
  deviation 124's lock refusal ADDS a `die` call site, so the exposure grew by one
  during a round that declined to shrink it.
- **The `stashes-present` fleet-wide reach (deviation 161).** An anonymous
  `(no branch)` stash based on shared history counts against every workspace of the
  project, behind a §7 guard with no override. The narrowing that would remove it was
  rejected on measurement: after a true merge every commit of the branch is already an
  ancestor of `origin/HEAD`, so the narrowed arm would count nothing at all and would
  survive only for squash merges. A guard whose coverage depends on which merge button
  a reviewer pressed is not a fact about stashes. The trade is paid for with a remedy
  in the refusal detail instead.
- **Making `isExecAllowed`'s declared-set gate pinnable (deviation 162).** Rejected
  because the only way to pin it is an injectable table, and injection into the lookup
  would create an allow-path that does not exist today. A pin is not worth a bypass
  primitive in the one function between the PWA and `exec`.
- **`prstate.ts:157`'s `ahead: line.ahead ?? 0`** — raised by verify3 as an eleventh
  measurement-forgery candidate, in lane, and deliberately not taken: INFO,
  pre-existing, outside the round's four items, and a close-out round is the wrong
  place for it. Still a fabricated `0`, and still read by no pwa consumer
  (`grep '\.ahead\b'` over `pwa/src` returns zero) — the null-preserving form already
  exists next door at `prstate.ts:236`.
- **Sweeping the ~100 stale `/tmp/ccrc-agent-containpath-*` and ~680
  `/tmp/contrast-*` directories** (deviations 175 and 135). Declined twice, both times
  because sibling lanes were running these suites on this box from their own
  worktrees and deleting a live fixture takes the stub `tmux` off a running suite's
  PATH — the mechanism that has killed the live fleet four times. Disk cost against
  outage risk, decided the same way both times. Controller action item, outstanding.
- **Flooring the `@keyframes` opacity troughs (deviation 134).** Documented follow-up,
  not pre-merge: WCAG 2.1 states no per-frame contrast requirement for an animating
  element, every loop reduces to a registered and measured reduced-motion steady
  state, and flooring a trough means retuning the motion language DIRECTION.md sets
  out — a design decision with no standards mandate behind it. What changed is that
  the inventory is now discovered and enforced rather than hand-typed and wrong.
- **`deploy.sh`'s server path failure output** (deviation 176) — a bare `curl` error
  with no journal tail. That is the finding's own baseline standard, and widening it
  on the eve of a deploy is the wrong trade; reported, not fixed.
- **`server/test/ccd-ws-gc.test.ts:402`'s flake under concurrent load**, and the
  unnamed server-suite flake the seam pass and fix round 6 both recorded without being
  able to reproduce or name. Both are disclosed rather than chased; neither has a
  captured test name, so absence of recurrence is weak evidence and is stated as such.

### A note on the counts quoted in these entries

Every figure above is taken from the commit body or the lane report that measured it,
never inferred. FOUR of the destroy lane's seven commit messages in fix round 6 quote a
per-commit suite total predicted rather than measured, and the lane corrected them in
its own report rather than by rewriting history: server 1086 → actually 1085 (`9962273`
and `9ff65cd`), server 1091 → actually 1089 (`304ce71`), pwa 852 → actually 851
(`014a464`). `fix6-destroy.md` says "three" while listing four, which is why the count
is restated here. No entry above quotes any of the four; the only fix-round-6 totals
quoted are ones nothing has contradicted.
The last THREE lanes ran in PARALLEL off `f9b3852`, so their end-state totals are
per-lane and not additive — destroy measured server 55 files / 1089 and pwa 851,
contrast measured pwa 895, infra measured agent 204 and server 1073. When this section
was drafted no whole-tree count at the merged tip was in evidence on disk, and the draft
declined to add four numbers that were never added — correctly, on what it could see.

The merged figures below were measured by the controller directly, on the merged tree,
with the LOCAL `./node_modules/.bin` binaries from inside each package. They are recorded
here because an absence in a document is read as an absence in fact:

| merge point | server | pwa | agent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `e876817` — the four ship-blocker lanes merged | 1091 (55 files) | 902 (40 files) | 204 (13 files) |
| `a2e5228` — **the shipping tip**, with `r5-clips` | **1099** (55 files) | **903** (40 files) | **204** (13 files) |

`tsc --noEmit` clean in all three packages at both points, `bash -n` clean for `ccd`,
`ccclip`, `deploy.sh`, `notify.sh` and `verify-service.sh`. The baseline these rounds
started from, before deviation 123, was server 960 / pwa 623 / agent 99.

One caution about `npx` for whoever re-measures this: `npx vitest` resolves to a global
cache copy with no `jsdom` and reports **"no tests" with 39 errors**, which reads exactly
like a code failure and is not. Every count in this document came from the local binary.

- [ ] **Step 3: Add the PR types to `shared/api.ts`**

Insert immediately after the `TaskProgress` interface (`api.ts:38-43`):

```ts
/** Where a workspace's pull request is, as ccrc last managed to find out.
 *
 *  `unchecked` is a FIRST-CLASS state, not a synonym for "no PR": keying the
 *  header control's visibility on `pr !== null` would make its absence an
 *  affirmative claim ("this session cannot have a PR") rendered identically to
 *  "we have not looked", and would put the retry affordance behind a control
 *  that is not on screen. */
export type PrPhase =
  | 'unchecked' | 'none' | 'no-commits' | 'open' | 'draft' | 'merged' | 'closed' | 'unknown';

/** CI rollup. `null` means NO CHECKS ARE CONFIGURED — distinct from 'pending',
 *  and rendered with different words. */
export type PrChecks = 'pass' | 'fail' | 'pending' | null;

export interface PrState {
  phase: PrPhase;
  number: number | null;
  url: string | null;
  title: string | null;
  checks: PrChecks;
  /** Names of the FAILING checks. GitHub-sourced and attacker-controllable on
   *  any repo that accepts fork PRs, so this is inert text everywhere it is
   *  rendered: never a prompt, never an argv, never a shell word. */
  checkNames: string[] | null;
  ahead: number;                 // commits past base
  /** Why `phase` is `unknown`. Every member but `merge-unproven` is a FAILED
   *  READ; `merge-unproven` is the opposite — GitHub answered fine and said
   *  MERGED, and a conjunct of the merge predicate did not hold, so ccrc
   *  declines to call it merged. It exists because `error` renders as "GitHub
   *  could not be read", which in that case is simply untrue. */
  reason:
    | 'timeout' | 'offline' | 'unauthenticated' | 'rate-limit'
    | 'no-remote' | 'unsupported' | 'agent-down' | 'error'
    | 'merge-unproven' | null;
  checkedAt: number | null;      // epoch ms of the gh read that produced this
  mergedAt: number | null;
  /** Epoch ms the sweep will next try this project, or null when nothing is
   *  scheduled. §6's rate-limit row promises the UI shows the reason AND the
   *  retry time, and `prBackoff` is the only thing that knows it — 15 minutes
   *  of a greyed cap with no explanation reads as broken rather than as
   *  waiting. Null on a ROUTE read failure, which backs nothing off and must
   *  not borrow the lane's clock. */
  retryAt: number | null;
}

/** The eight phases as a runtime value, so a string read off disk (written by
 *  ccd, possibly a version behind) can be validated rather than trusted. */
export const PR_PHASES: readonly PrPhase[] =
  ['unchecked', 'none', 'no-commits', 'open', 'draft', 'merged', 'closed', 'unknown'];
```

Then add two fields to `FleetSession`, after `tasks` (`api.ts:21`):

```ts
  /** This workspace's pull request, or null for a main checkout — which is the
   *  ONLY thing that suppresses the header control. */
  pr: PrState | null;
  /** Epoch SECONDS this workspace was archived (ccd writes `$REG/<id>.archived`
   *  as an epoch), or null. Every piece of archive copy in the UI derives from
   *  THIS, never from `pr.phase`: a merged PR whose archive was deferred
   *  because the session was busy must not claim it was archived. */
  archivedAt: number | null;
```


with one helper above `readRegistry`:

```ts
/** A registry field as a finite number, or null. `parseInt` alone yields NaN
 *  for a truncated write, and NaN on the wire renders as `null` in JSON while
 *  typing as `number` — a silent lie. */
function numOrNull(raw: string | null): number | null {
  if (raw === null || raw.trim() === '') return null;
  const n = Number(raw.trim());
  return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : null;
}
```

```ts
/** The PR state a session has WITHOUT a live sweep: whatever `ccd pr-state`

    checkedAt: r.prCheckedAt, mergedAt: null,
    // The registry stores no backoff: it is per-process, per-project, in-memory.
    retryAt: null,
  };
}
```

### Task 2: `ccd caps`, `ws-archive`, `ws-restore`, `ws-attic` — the lossless half

**Files:**
- Modify: `infra/<server-host>-portability/ccd` — new helpers after `_ws_unsupervise`
  (`ccd:109`); new `cmd_*` after `cmd_ws_rename`'s closing brace, above the
  `# ── reclamation ──` banner (`ccd:468`); new dispatch arms
  in the `case` block (`ccd:1306-1324`)
- Test: **Create** `infra/ccrc/server/test/ccd-archive.test.ts`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `$REG/<id>.prnumber` (Task 1's field, written by Task 3).
- Produces, on the box:
  - `ccd caps` → one verb name per line, exit 0
  - `ccd ws-archive --session <id>` → `archived <id> …` / `already archived <id>`, exit 0
  - `ccd ws-restore --session <id>` → `restored <id> — <workdir>`, exit 0
  - `ccd ws-attic --session <id>` → `<refname> <sha>` per line; `ccd ws-attic --drop <id>` releases them
  - registry writes: `<id>.archived` (epoch seconds), `<id>.archivedreason`, `<id>.archivemanifest`
  - the manifest's keys, since Tasks 5, 6 and 19 read this record and not the
    worktree: `id`, `branch` (the registry's name), `worktreeHead` (git's record
    for that path; `""` for a detached HEAD), `base`, `tip` (**`null`** when
    `refs/heads/<branch>` does not resolve), `dirty`, `ignoredDigest`, `stashes`,
    `worktreeBytes`, `pr`, `transcript`

**Context.** Archive destroys nothing: no `git worktree remove`, no
`git branch -d`, no `rm -f "$REG/$id".*`. Branch, worktree, every gitignored
file, stashes and the per-worktree HEAD reflog are byte-identical afterwards.
Its one real cost is the tmux pane — scrollback and any in-flight turn — which
is why it requires an affirmative idle. `ws-restore` runs `_spawn "$id" resume`
and Claude Code resumes from the on-disk transcript, so *context* survives;
only the pane does not. **Archiving is allowed on a dirty tree** — it destroys
nothing, and refusing would strand merged-but-dirty workspaces in the live
fleet permanently. The dirty refusal belongs in reap.

The same rule decides every other awkward state this verb can meet, and it is
worth stating as a rule rather than re-deciding per field, because the first
implementation got it wrong in both directions at once (deviations 6 and 7):

> **Archive refuses only what it cannot DESCRIBE.** A question git cannot answer
> — no worktree record for this path, a directory belonging to another
> repository, an unreadable tree or ignored set, no `python3` to quote with — has
> no truthful record and must refuse, because a manifest that reads pristine is
> what authorises a later deletion. A fact that is merely not the expected one —
> the worktree is on another branch, on a detached HEAD, or the branch the
> registry names no longer resolves — is **recorded**, because `ws-archive` runs
> unattended (Task 14, every 120 s, exit code discarded) and a refusal it cannot
> converge out of strands the workspace in the live fleet forever with nothing on
> screen to explain it. Each of those recorded states is one `ws-reap` refuses in
> its own right (`registry-branch-drift`, `detached-head`, `branch-missing`), at
> the instant of deletion, where refusing costs a deferred cleanup and nothing
> else. The lossless verb must never be stricter than the destructive one.

The one apparent exception is the missing worktree directory, which stays a
refusal: with the directory gone `dirty`, `ignoredDigest` and `worktreeBytes` are
unmeasurable at the same time, so the record would not describe a drifted
workspace — it would describe nothing, in the pristine-reading shape deviation 6
closed. `ws-rename`, `ws-restore` and reap's `worktree-missing` all refuse the
same shape, and unlike drift it is visible outside ccd's stderr: `ws-gc` reports
it as `dead-reg`. Task 14 will nonetheless re-fire on it every 120 s and discard
the refusal, which is a Task 14 concern (skip it, or surface it) and is recorded
here so it is not rediscovered as a Task 2 bug.

`ccd ensure` does **not** re-supervise (ccd:1081-1088), so `ws-restore` must call
`_ws_supervise` explicitly or boot persistence is silently lost.

```ts
// of this reaching a real repository.

  _ws_supervise() { echo "supervise $1" >> "$HOME/ccd-calls"; };
  _spawn() { echo "spawn $1 $2" >> "$HOME/ccd-calls"; };
  tmux() { echo "tmux $*" >> "$HOME/ccd-calls"; return 1; };
  _alive() { return 1; };`;

const shFail = (snippet: string): { code: number; stdout: string; stderr: string } => {
  try { return { code: 0, stdout: h.sh(snippet), stderr: '' }; }
  catch (e) {
    const err = e as { status?: number; stdout?: string; stderr?: string };
    return { code: err.status ?? 1, stdout: String(err.stdout ?? ''), stderr: String(err.stderr ?? '') };
  }
};

const workspace = (project: string, slug: string): string => {

    // is worse than none, because the server would trust it.
    const src = fs.readFileSync(CCD, 'utf8');
    const block = src.slice(src.indexOf('case "${1:-}" in'));
    const dispatched = [...block.matchAll(/^ {2}([a-z][a-z|-]*)\)/gm)]

    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(wt, 'README.md'), 'edited\n');
    expect(h.sh(`${ARCH} cmd_ws_archive --session demo-quiet-basin`)).toMatch(/^archived/);
    expect(h.reg('demo-quiet-basin', 'archived')).toMatch(/^\d+$/);
  });

  it('is idempotent — a second call says so and exits 0', () => {
    workspace('demo', 'quiet-basin');
    h.sh(`${ARCH} cmd_ws_archive --session demo-quiet-basin`);
    // Level-triggering depends on this: the sweep retries every 120 s until it
    // succeeds, and a second success must not be an error.
    const r = shFail(`${ARCH} cmd_ws_archive --session demo-quiet-basin`);
    expect(r.code).toBe(0);
    expect(r.stdout).toBe('already archived demo-quiet-basin');
  });

  it('refuses when the wrapper status cannot be read while the pane IS alive', () => {
    workspace('demo', 'quiet-basin');
    const BUSY = ARCH.replace('_alive() { return 1; };', '_alive() { return 0; };');
    expect(shFail(`${BUSY} cmd_ws_archive --session demo-quiet-basin`).stderr)
      .toMatch(/status-unknown/);
  });

  it('refuses a busy session', () => {
    workspace('demo', 'quiet-basin');
    const cfg = path.join(h.home, '.claude', 'sessions');
    fs.mkdirSync(cfg, { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(cfg, '4242.json'), '{"status":"busy","statusUpdatedAt":1}');
    const BUSY = ARCH
      .replace('_alive() { return 1; };', '_alive() { return 0; };')
      .replace('tmux() { echo "tmux $*" >> "$HOME/ccd-calls"; return 1; };',
               'tmux() { case "$1" in list-panes) echo 4242 ;; *) echo "tmux $*" >> "$HOME/ccd-calls" ;; esac; };');
    expect(shFail(`${BUSY} cmd_ws_archive --session demo-quiet-basin`).stderr).toMatch(/session-busy/);
  });

  it('names the PR in archivedreason when the registry knows one', () => {
    workspace('demo', 'quiet-basin');
    h.sh('_reg_set demo-quiet-basin prnumber 42');
    h.sh(`${ARCH} cmd_ws_archive --session demo-quiet-basin`);
    expect(h.reg('demo-quiet-basin', 'archivedreason')).toBe('merged:#42');
  });

  it('writes the manifest into the REGISTRY, never into the worktree', () => {
    const wt = workspace('demo', 'quiet-basin');
    h.sh(`${ARCH} cmd_ws_archive --session demo-quiet-basin`);
    const m = JSON.parse(h.reg('demo-quiet-basin', 'archivemanifest')!) as Record<string, unknown>;
    expect(m.branch).toBe('ws/quiet-basin');
    expect(m.base).toBe('origin/main');
    expect(m.tip).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/);
    expect(m.dirty).toBe(0);
    expect(m.stashes).toBe(0);
    expect(typeof m.worktreeBytes).toBe('number');
    // git's own record for this path, beside the registry's claim — equal here,
    // and the pair that makes the drifted cases describable (deviation 7).
    expect(m.worktreeHead).toBe('ws/quiet-basin');
    // NOT `toContain('.claude/projects/')`, which passes for any munge at all:
    // the exact path `mungePath` computes, because the reap has to find the
    // transcript after the registry is gone. `tr './_' '---'` has to agree with
    // munge.ts on all three characters, so assert the whole path.
    expect(m.transcript).toBe(path.join(
      h.home, '.claude', 'projects', mungePath(wt), `${h.reg('demo-quiet-basin', 'uuid')}.jsonl`));
    // The manifest describes the thing that may later be deleted, so it cannot
    // live inside it.
    expect(fs.existsSync(path.join(wt, '.archivemanifest'))).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe('ws-restore', () => {
  it('undoes an archive completely and re-supervises', () => {
    workspace('demo', 'quiet-basin');
    h.sh(`${ARCH} cmd_ws_archive --session demo-quiet-basin`);
    const out = h.sh(`${ARCH} cmd_ws_restore --session demo-quiet-basin`);
    expect(out).toMatch(/^restored demo-quiet-basin/);
    expect(h.reg('demo-quiet-basin', 'archived')).toBeNull();
    expect(h.reg('demo-quiet-basin', 'archivedreason')).toBeNull();
    expect(h.reg('demo-quiet-basin', 'archivemanifest')).toBeNull();
    expect(h.reg('demo-quiet-basin', 'started')).toBe('1');
    // `ccd ensure` does NOT re-supervise, so restore must do it explicitly or
    // boot persistence is silently lost.
    expect(h.calls()).toContain('spawn demo-quiet-basin resume');
    expect(h.calls()).toContain('supervise demo-quiet-basin');
  });

  it('refuses a session that is not archived', () => {
    workspace('demo', 'quiet-basin');
    expect(shFail(`${ARCH} cmd_ws_restore --session demo-quiet-basin`).stderr).toMatch(/not archived/);
  });

  it('points at the attic when the worktree is gone', () => {
    const wt = workspace('demo', 'quiet-basin');
    h.sh(`${ARCH} cmd_ws_archive --session demo-quiet-basin`);
    fs.rmSync(wt, { recursive: true, force: true });
    expect(shFail(`${ARCH} cmd_ws_restore --session demo-quiet-basin`).stderr)
      .toMatch(/ccd ws-attic --session demo-quiet-basin/);
  });
});

describe('ws-attic', () => {
  it('lists the refs pinned under this session, and drops them on demand', () => {
    workspace('demo', 'quiet-basin');
    const main = path.join(h.home, 'projects', 'demo');
    const tip = h.git(main, 'rev-parse', 'refs/heads/ws/quiet-basin');
    h.git(main, 'update-ref', `refs/ccrc/attic/demo-quiet-basin/${tip}`, tip);
    expect(h.sh('cmd_ws_attic --session demo-quiet-basin')).toContain(tip);
    expect(h.sh('cmd_ws_attic --drop demo-quiet-basin')).toMatch(/dropped 1 attic ref/);
    expect(h.sh('cmd_ws_attic --session demo-quiet-basin')).toBe('');
  });

  it('rejects any mode word other than --session or --drop', () => {
    // The session has to EXIST for the mode word to be what is under test.
    // Without it `_attic_project` fails and the command dies at `no such session`
    // before the case is reached, so `expect(code).toBe(1)` passes whether or not
    // the `*)` arm exists: measured, deleting that arm left the whole suite green
    // while `ccd ws-attic --frobnicate <real id>` exited 0 with no output.
    workspace('demo', 'quiet-basin');
    const r = shFail('cmd_ws_attic --frobnicate demo-quiet-basin');
    expect(r.code).toBe(1);
    expect(r.stderr).toMatch(/usage: ccd ws-attic/);
    expect(r.stderr).not.toMatch(/no such session/);
  });
});
```
