- [ ] **Step 3: Add the shared helpers to `ccd`**

Insert immediately after `_ws_unsupervise` (`ccd:109`):

```bash
# ── PR / archive lifecycle helpers ─────────────────────────────────
# `local x=$(cmd)` returns local's status, never cmd's — so anything whose exit
# code is read below declares first and assigns second, deliberately.

_json_str() {   # value -> a JSON string literal (quote/backslash/control safe)
  # THE ENCODING POLICY IS PINNED HERE, because the value may be RAW BYTES and a
  # filename is not text. `_ws_collect_ignored` reads paths with `-z`
  # (deliberately — see there), so `ignored[].path`, `sensitive[]` and the
  # `sensitive-ignored` detail carry whatever the filesystem holds, and a Linux
  # path is any byte string without NUL or `/`.
  #
  # The previous form read stdin through python's LOCALE codec. On this box
  # (`LANG=en_US.UTF-8`) that is utf-8 STRICT, so one 0xff byte raised
  # UnicodeDecodeError, stdout was EMPTY, `$(…)` swallowed the status and
  # `cmd_ws_audit` printed `"ignored":[{"path":,"bytes":600,…}]` — a document
  # JSON.parse rejects, at exit 0, over a workspace whose verdict was
  # `sensitive-ignored` and whose `sensitive` array had silently degraded to
  # `[]`. Under `LC_ALL=C` the same input was fine (python falls back to
  # surrogateescape), so it was locale-dependent as well as wrong.
  #
  # So the bytes are read as BYTES — `sys.stdin.buffer`, which no locale can
  # reach — and decoded utf-8 with errors='replace'. LOSSY, deliberately, and it
  # cannot weaken a guard: every decision over these bytes has already been taken
  # in bash on the RAW bytes (`_ws_sensitive_match`'s `case` globs, `du`'s size,
  # `_ws_ignored_digest`'s hash) before anything is serialised. What is left is
  # the HUMAN's copy, and U+FFFD renders as a visible "this is not text" where a
  # `\udcff` surrogate escape — the round-tripping alternative — is valid JSON
  # that most consumers mangle or refuse to re-encode. `json.dumps` defaults to
  # ensure_ascii, so stdout is pure ASCII whatever the writer's locale; `LC_ALL`
  # is pinned anyway rather than inherited, so nothing here depends on the box.
  #
  # NON-ZERO now means one thing only: python3 could not be RUN. Callers must
  # check it — a bare `$(_json_str …)` inside a printf argument list swallows the
  # status by construction, which is how the hole above got printed — and both
  # callers that build a whole record (`_ws_manifest`, `cmd_ws_audit`) probe once
  # up front and refuse rather than checking nineteen substitutions.
  #
  # MUTATION SURVIVOR, disclosed and measured: `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8` can be deleted
  # with the suite green, and always will be on a box whose LANG is already a
  # UTF-8 one — `sys.stdin.buffer` bypasses the stdin codec and `ensure_ascii`
  # makes stdout pure ASCII, so between them the call is already locale-proof and
  # no fixture on THIS box can tell the two apart. It is written because the
  # defect it guards against is precisely a difference between boxes: the old
  # form was correct under `LC_ALL=C` and broken under `en_US.UTF-8`, so "it
  # works here" was exactly the evidence that was worthless. Pinning it means a
  # future rewrite that goes back to a text-mode read fails on every box rather
  # than on someone else's.
  printf '%s' "${1-}" | LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 python3 -c 'import json,sys
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(sys.stdin.buffer.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")))'
}

_ws_status() {   # id -> busy|idle on stdout; NON-ZERO when it cannot be read.
  # Fails closed twice over, and both halves are load-bearing.
  #
  # UNREADABLE -> non-zero. A socket hiccup or an unreadable status file must
  # not read as "not working" and let an archive kill a live turn.
  #
  # UNRECOGNISED -> busy. `idle` is an ALLOWLIST; every other value is busy.
  # Claude Code writes at least `idle`, `busy` (a model turn is in flight) and
  # `shell` (a Bash tool command is running) — server/src/livestate.ts:14-30 is
  # this repo's own record of that vocabulary, and of what matching `busy` and
  # calling the rest idle cost when the server side did it. Here the price is
  # steeper than a wrong badge: `ws-reap` gates `git worktree remove` on this
  # answer, so `shell` reading idle deletes the tree out from under a running
  # `npm test`. A status we do not recognise is far likelier to be new work than
  # new rest, and an allowlist is the only polarity that survives the wrapper
  # growing a fourth word. Same polarity as _auto_swap_check's gate
  # (ccd:1261), which is likewise `[[ "$st" == "idle" ]]` and stops on anything
  # else.
  local id="$1" wrapper cfg pid sf st
  wrapper=$(_reg_get "$id" wrapper); [[ -n "$wrapper" ]] || return 1
  cfg=$(_cfg_dir "$wrapper");        [[ -n "$cfg" ]]     || return 1
  _alive "$id" || { echo idle; return 0; }      # no pane at all: nothing is running
  pid=$(tmux list-panes -t "$(_tmux "$id")" -F '#{pane_pid}' 2>/dev/null | head -1)
  [[ "$pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
  sf="$cfg/sessions/$pid.json"
  st=$(grep -oE '"status":"[a-z_-]+"' "$sf" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | cut -d'"' -f4)
  [[ -n "$st" ]] || return 1
  [[ "$st" == idle ]] || { echo busy; return 0; }
  echo idle
}

_transcript_path() {   # id -> the Claude Code transcript for its CURRENT uuid
  # <cfg>/projects/<workdir with / . _ all mapped to ->/<uuid>.jsonl — the same
  # munge server/src/munge.ts applies. Recorded so a reap never has to be
  # reconstructed from an escaped path after the registry is gone.
  local id="$1" wrapper cfg workdir uuid munged
  wrapper=$(_reg_get "$id" wrapper); workdir=$(_reg_get "$id" workdir); uuid=$(_reg_get "$id" uuid)
  cfg=$(_cfg_dir "$wrapper")
  [[ -n "$cfg" && -n "$workdir" && -n "$uuid" ]] || return 1
  munged=$(printf '%s' "$workdir" | tr './_' '---')
  printf '%s/projects/%s/%s.jsonl\n' "$cfg" "$munged" "$uuid"
}

_ws_stash_count() {   # main branch -> stash entries belonging to that branch
  # -F on both patterns: a branch name carrying a '.' would otherwise be a
  # wildcard and over-count, which here means refusing a legitimate reap.
  git -C "$1" stash list 2>/dev/null | grep -cF -e "On $2:" -e "WIP on $2:" || true
}

_ws_ignored_digest() {   # workdir -> sha256 of the ignored-entry set
  # NON-ZERO when the set could not be read at all.
  #
  # --ignored=matching, NEVER `ls-files --others --ignored`: the latter
  # enumerates per file (measured 210,070 entries / 24.6 MB in custom-tools,
  # against an 8 MB agent EXEC_MAX_BUFFER), while this collapses each ignored
  # directory to one entry.
  #
  # A failed read must not be indistinguishable from an empty one, and by
  # construction the digests are: a nonexistent directory, a corrupt repo and an
  # index.lock contention all hash sha256("") = e3b0c442…b855, exactly like a
  # workspace with nothing ignored. Harmless while the digest is only recorded;
  # a forgery the moment ws-reap compares a stored digest against a live one to
  # prove gitignored content is unchanged, because a failure on EITHER side then
  # manufactures the match that authorises the delete. So the difference is
  # carried by the exit code.
  #
  # It has to come from PIPESTATUS[0] — git's own status — and not from the
  # pipeline: `grep '^!! '` exits 1 on a legitimately empty ignored set, so the
  # pipeline already returned non-zero for the HEALTHY case (measured: rc=1 for a
  # clean workspace, rc=1 for /no/such/dir). Two statements, because
  # `local d=$(...)` would return local's status.
  local d
  d=$(git -C "$1" status --porcelain --ignored=matching 2>/dev/null \
        | grep '^!! ' | sort | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1; exit "${PIPESTATUS[0]}") || return 1
  [[ "$d" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "$d"
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Add `cmd_caps`**

Insert after `cmd_ws_rename`'s closing brace — find it by the line above it,
`echo "renamed $id: $old -> $new"`, and put the new verbs before the
`# ── reclamation ──` banner (`ccd:468`):

```bash
cmd_caps() {   # one verb name per line — what THIS copy of ccd implements.
  # ~/.local/bin/ccd is a COPY, not a symlink to the repo, so a verb can pass
  # the agent's whitelist and still not exist on the box. The agent reads this
  # at start and reports it in its ready frame; the server refuses to emit a
  # verb the agent did not advertise. NOT whitelisted — the agent runs it
  # directly, and it is a pure read.
  #
  # It takes no argv, and says so rather than ignoring it. This whole verb exists
  # so a caller can find out what this copy of ccd supports; answering `ccd caps
  # --json` with the plain list — which is what silently discarding argv did —
  # hands that caller a shape it did not ask for and no way to tell. Every other
  # verb here asserts its argv exactly; this one is the one whose whole job is
  # honesty about capability.
  [[ $# -eq 0 ]] || die "usage: ccd caps"
  cat <<'EOF'
attach
caps
clip
enable
ensure
list
menu
pick
prefer
start
stop
supervise
swap
swap-self
ws-add
ws-archive
ws-attic
ws-gc
ws-rename
ws-restore
ws-rm
ls
EOF
}
```

The parity test in Step 1 sorts both sides, so the order above is irrelevant —
but every arm of the dispatcher's `case` must appear, and nothing else. As
Tasks 3–6 add `pr-state`, `pr-open`, `ws-audit` and `ws-reap`, each adds its
verb HERE as well; the parity test is what forces it.

- [ ] **Step 5: Add `cmd_ws_archive`**

Insert after `cmd_caps`:

```bash
cmd_ws_archive() {   # ccd ws-archive --session <id> — fold a merged workspace
  # out of the live fleet. DESTROYS NOTHING: no worktree remove, no branch -d,
  # no rm of the registry. Its one cost is the tmux pane (scrollback and any
  # in-flight turn), which is why it demands an affirmative idle.
  [[ $# -eq 2 && $1 == --session ]] || die "usage: ccd ws-archive --session <id>"
  local id=$2
  [[ $id =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || die "bad session id"
  [[ -f "$REG/$id.uuid" ]]       || die "no such session: $id"
  [[ -n "$(_reg_get "$id" workspace)" ]] \
    || die "not a workspace — refusing to archive a main checkout"
  # `return`, not `exit`: ccd is sourceable (the BASH_SOURCE guard below), so an
  # `exit` here would terminate an in-process batch caller at its first
  # already-archived workspace and skip the rest with a success code.
  [[ -f "$REG/$id.archived" ]] && { echo "already archived $id"; return 0; }

  local workdir; workdir=$(_reg_get "$id" workdir)
  [[ -n "$workdir" ]] || die "incomplete registry for '$id'"
  # The same refusal ws-restore makes, for a stronger reason: with the directory
  # gone every tree field in the manifest reads PRISTINE — dirty 0 because the
  # status read failed, worktreeBytes 0 from _ws_gc_bytes's '-' fallback,
  # ignoredDigest = sha256("") — and the output still said "nothing deleted".
  [[ -d "$workdir" ]] \
    || die "worktree is gone: $workdir — cannot describe it for the archive record; see: ccd ws-attic --session $id"

  local st
  st=$(_ws_status "$id") || die "status-unknown"
  [[ "$st" != busy ]] || die "session-busy"

  # Build the manifest BEFORE anything is torn down, and refuse if it cannot be
  # told truthfully. Its exit status used to be discarded and every field inside
  # it 2>/dev/null-swallowed, with no [[ -s ]], no parse and no guard before the
  # `archived` marker went down — so a workspace whose worktree had moved away
  # archived at exit 0 with a manifest asserting a clean, empty tree, and a box
  # without python3 persisted syntactically invalid JSON as the archive record.
  # This is what Task 5's audit ladder and ws-reap compare against: a manifest
  # that lies pristine is a manifest that authorises a deletion. The helper says
  # on stderr which rung refused.
  local manifest
  manifest=$(_ws_archive_manifest "$id") \
    || die "cannot describe $id truthfully — nothing was touched"
  [[ -n "$manifest" ]] || die "empty archive manifest for $id — nothing was touched"
  # Parsed, not merely non-empty: the fields are individually guarded above, and
  # this is what keeps a future unquoted or non-numeric field from becoming a
  # record that only LOOKS like JSON.
  printf '%s' "$manifest" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; json.loads(sys.stdin.read())' 2>/dev/null \
    || die "archive manifest for $id is not valid JSON — nothing was touched"

  # Into the REGISTRY, never into the worktree — the worktree is the thing that
  # may later be deleted, and a manifest inside it would die with it.
  printf '%s\n' "$manifest" > "$REG/$id.archivemanifest"

  _ws_unsupervise "$id"                                   # clears Restart=always
  tmux kill-session -t "$(_tmux "$id")" 2>/dev/null || true

  local pr; pr=$(_reg_get "$id" prnumber)
  _reg_set "$id" archived "$(date +%s)"
  if [[ "$pr" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then _reg_set "$id" archivedreason "merged:#$pr"
  else                             _reg_set "$id" archivedreason "merged"; fi

  local note=""; [[ "$pr" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && note=" (merged in #$pr)"
  echo "archived $id$note — worktree kept at $workdir, nothing deleted"
}

_ws_archive_manifest() {   # id -> one JSON object on stdout
  # NON-ZERO, with the reason on stderr, when the workspace cannot be described
  # truthfully. Every field used to be swallowed individually, which made the
  # unreadable cases indistinguishable from a clean, empty, unstashed tree.
  #
  # The line between the two halves of that sentence is the whole design, and it
  # is NOT "anything unexpected refuses":
  #   REFUSED — a question git cannot answer at all: no worktree record for this
  #     path, a directory belonging to another repository, an unreadable tree or
  #     ignored set, no python3 to quote with. There is nothing truthful to write.
  #   RECORDED — a fact about the world that happens not to be the expected one:
  #     the worktree is on another branch, or on a detached HEAD, or the branch
  #     the registry names no longer resolves. Those are describable, so they are
  #     described, and the DESTRUCTIVE verb refuses on them at the instant of
  #     deletion (Task 5/6: `registry-branch-drift`, `detached-head`,
  #     `branch-missing`) where a refusal costs nothing but a deferred cleanup.
  # Archive is lossless and runs unattended — Task 14 fires it every 120 s and
  # discards the exit code — so a refusal it cannot converge out of strands the
  # workspace in the live fleet forever with nothing on screen to say why. Same
  # argument Task 2's Context already makes for a dirty tree ("refusing would
  # strand merged-but-dirty workspaces in the live fleet permanently"), and the
  # same division `cmd_ws_rm` draws for this very divergence: the registry is a
  # witness, never the decider (ccd:465-471).
  local id="$1" project workdir branch base main tip dirty ignored stashes bytes pr transcript
  project=$(_reg_get "$id" project); workdir=$(_reg_get "$id" workdir)
  branch=$(_reg_get "$id" branch);   base=$(_reg_get "$id" base)
  [[ -n "$project" && -n "$workdir" && -n "$branch" ]] \
    || { echo "manifest: incomplete registry for '$id'" >&2; return 1; }
  main="$PROJECTS_ROOT/$project"

  # Every string field is quoted by python3, so without it NONE of them are and
  # the record is not JSON. Probed once, up front, rather than six times inside
  # the printf. ccd's other python3 call site (ccd:1447) warns and continues,
  # which is right for a best-effort transcript sanitize and wrong for a record
  # that authorises deletions.
  _json_str probe >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || { echo "manifest: python3 unavailable — cannot quote JSON safely" >&2; return 1; }

  # ccrc asks $main; $workdir is only ever a path git is asked ABOUT. The tree
  # reads below are the one class that must be `-C "$workdir"` — they are
  # questions about that directory's contents — so they run only after git's own
  # record AND the directory itself have both said $main, which is the pair
  # cmd_ws_rm requires before it touches anything (ccd:432-435). `registered` is
  # read from $? on its own line: `local x=$(...)` returns local's status.
  local wthead registered wd_common main_common rc
  wthead=$(_ws_wt_branch "$main" "$workdir"); registered=$?
  (( registered == 0 )) \
    || { echo "manifest: $main has no worktree record for $workdir" >&2; return 1; }
  # DRIFT IS A FIELD, NOT A REFUSAL. `_ws_wt_branch` follows a rename whether ccd
  # or the user did it (ccd:377-383), so `$wthead` is git's own answer for this
  # path and `$branch` is the registry's claim: recorded side by side as `branch`
  # and `worktreeHead`, which is the pair Task 5 fingerprints (`worktreeHead=`)
  # and puts on the wire as `headMatchesRegistry`. "" is git's answer for a
  # recorded detached HEAD, and the same "" Task 5 compares against `$branch`.
  # Three ordinary states used to refuse here, permanently and identically on
  # retry: a `git branch -m` inside the worktree, a `git checkout other-branch`
  # to compare something, a `git bisect`. None of them makes the workspace
  # undescribable, and refusing left the sweep logging the same line every two
  # minutes forever.
  #
  # The record alone cannot decide the DIRECTORY: it outlives the directory, so a
  # hand-deletion plus a stray `git init` at the same path with the same branch
  # name still reads healthy and still answers $branch (measured on git 2.43).
  # That one stays a refusal — every tree field below would describe a stranger's
  # tree and file it under this workspace.
  wd_common=$(_ws_common_dir "$workdir"); main_common=$(_ws_common_dir "$main")
  [[ -n "$main_common" && "$wd_common" == "$main_common" ]] \
    || { echo "manifest: $workdir is not a worktree of $main" >&2; return 1; }

  # `--quiet` turns git's own two answers into two exit codes, which is what lets
  # "that ref does not exist" be a field and "I cannot read that repository" stay
  # a refusal. Measured on git 2.43: rc 1 for an absent ref in a readable repo,
  # rc 128 for a repo git cannot read at all (and without --quiet, 128 for both).
  # `tip` is recorded as JSON null when absent, never as "" or a substitute oid: a
  # renamed branch leaves the registry's name resolving to nothing, and ws-reap
  # refuses that as `branch-missing`. The tip stays the tip of the branch this
  # record NAMES — filing the renamed branch's tip under `branch` would be the
  # forgery this rung exists to prevent.
  tip=$(git -C "$main" rev-parse --verify --quiet "refs/heads/$branch" 2>/dev/null); rc=$?
  case "$rc" in
    0) : ;;
    1) tip="" ;;
    *) echo "manifest: could not ask $main for refs/heads/$branch" >&2; return 1 ;;
  esac
  # Measured against whatever is checked out, which is what `worktreeHead` above
  # makes legible: on a drifted worktree this counts that branch's uncommitted
  # work, and it is still the honest answer to "what is uncommitted here".
  dirty=$(git -C "$workdir" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null) \
    || { echo "manifest: could not read the tree at $workdir" >&2; return 1; }
  dirty=$(printf '%s' "$dirty" | grep -c . || true)
  ignored=$(_ws_ignored_digest "$workdir") \
    || { echo "manifest: could not read the ignored set at $workdir" >&2; return 1; }
  # $main answered rev-parse a moment ago — rc 0 or a clean "no such ref", both
  # of which are answers — so its stash list is readable; the count is the only
  # field whose repository has already been proven healthy.
  #
  # Scoped to the `branch` field, NOT to `worktreeHead`: it is the count of
  # entries whose subject names that branch, and pairing it with any other name
  # would make the record two things at once. So on a drifted worktree this can
  # read 0 while `worktreeHead`'s branch holds stashes — which is safe in the one
  # direction that matters, because `ws-reap` refuses drift (`registry-branch-drift`,
  # `detached-head`, `branch-missing`) before it ever consults a stash count, and
  # recomputes the count itself when it does. `worktreeHead` beside it is what
  # tells a reader which question the number answered.
  stashes=$(_ws_stash_count "$main" "$branch")
  # Pre-merge fix round, finding 5: `null`, not `0` — the seventh instance of
  # the measurement-forgery class in this plan (deviation 10, "a number is a
  # measurement"). The whole-directory-gone case already refuses earlier (the
  # `[[ -d "$workdir" ]]` guard above `_ws_archive_manifest`, and the
  # `git -C "$workdir" status` read a few lines up, both before this point);
  # this is the narrower window — `du` failing on a workdir that DOES exist
  # and IS otherwise readable. `registry.ts`'s `manifestBytes` already treats
  # anything but a finite JSON number as unmeasured (Task 19), so writing the
  # honest value here is the whole fix: a fabricated 0 would have argued
  # against a cleanup that could free real disk.
  bytes=$(_ws_gc_bytes "$workdir"); [[ "$bytes" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || bytes=null
  pr=$(_reg_get "$id" prnumber); [[ "$pr" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || pr=null
  transcript=$(_transcript_path "$id") || transcript=""
  printf '{"id":%s,"branch":%s,"worktreeHead":%s,"base":%s,"tip":%s,"dirty":%s,"ignoredDigest":%s,"stashes":%s,"worktreeBytes":%s,"pr":%s,"transcript":%s}\n' \
    "$(_json_str "$id")" "$(_json_str "$branch")" "$(_json_str "$wthead")" "$(_json_str "$base")" \
    "$( [[ -n "$tip" ]] && _json_str "$tip" || echo null)" \
    "$dirty" "$(_json_str "$ignored")" "$stashes" "$bytes" "$pr" "$(_json_str "$transcript")"
}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Add `cmd_ws_restore` and `cmd_ws_attic`**

Insert after `_ws_archive_manifest`:

```bash
cmd_ws_restore() {   # ccd ws-restore --session <id> — undo an archive entirely
  # No confirmation: it only creates. The one thing it must not do is leave the
  # session unsupervised — `ccd ensure` does NOT re-supervise (ccd:1427-1434), so
  # boot persistence would be silently lost.
  [[ $# -eq 2 && $1 == --session ]] || die "usage: ccd ws-restore --session <id>"
  local id=$2
  [[ $id =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || die "bad session id"
  [[ -f "$REG/$id.uuid" ]]       || die "no such session: $id"
  [[ -f "$REG/$id.archived" ]]   || die "not archived: $id"
  local workdir; workdir=$(_reg_get "$id" workdir)
  [[ -d "$workdir" ]] || die "worktree is gone: $workdir — see: ccd ws-attic --session $id"
  rm -f "$REG/$id.archived" "$REG/$id.archivedreason" "$REG/$id.archivemanifest"
  _spawn "$id" resume
  _reg_set "$id" started 1
  _ws_supervise "$id"
  echo "restored $id — $workdir"
}

_attic_project() {   # id -> the project owning its attic refs
  # Registry first, tombstone second: after a reap the registry is gone, and
  # the attic is exactly what the user still needs to reach.
  local id="$1" p
  p=$(_reg_get "$id" project); [[ -n "$p" ]] && { printf '%s\n' "$p"; return 0; }
  p=$(sed -n 's/.*"project"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' "$REG/.reaped/$id.json" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
  [[ -n "$p" ]] && { printf '%s\n' "$p"; return 0; }
  return 1
}

cmd_ws_attic() {   # ccd ws-attic --session <id>   |   ccd ws-attic --drop <id>
  # --drop is terminal-only: only ['ws-attic','--session'] is whitelisted, so
  # the PWA cannot reach it. Attic refs are never garbage-collected on a timer.
  [[ $# -eq 2 ]] || die "usage: ccd ws-attic --session <id> | ccd ws-attic --drop <id>"
  local mode=$1 id=$2
  [[ $id =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || die "bad session id"
  local project; project=$(_attic_project "$id") || die "no such session: $id"
  local main="$PROJECTS_ROOT/$project"
  case "$mode" in
    --session)
      git -C "$main" for-each-ref --format='%(refname) %(objectname)' "refs/ccrc/attic/$id/" 2>/dev/null
      ;;
    --drop)
      local n=0 ref
      while IFS= read -r ref; do
        [[ -n "$ref" ]] || continue
        git -C "$main" update-ref -d "$ref" && n=$(( n + 1 ))
      done < <(git -C "$main" for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' "refs/ccrc/attic/$id/" 2>/dev/null)
      echo "dropped $n attic ref$( (( n == 1 )) || echo s ) for $id"
      ;;
    *) die "usage: ccd ws-attic --session <id> | ccd ws-attic --drop <id>" ;;
  esac
}
```

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `_json_str`, `_ws_gc_bytes`, `$REG/<id>.base`/`.branch`/`.workdir`.
- Produces:
  - `ccd pr-state --session <id>` / `--project <project>` → **JSONL**, one
    object per workspace session, exit 0 always
  - success object keys: `id, project, repo, branch, base, baseShort, tip,
    ahead, dirty, commits[{sha,subject,body}], template, rows[], phase,
    number, checkedAt, reason`. **`tip`, `ahead` and `dirty` are nullable and
    null means UNMEASURED** (deviations 10 and 11): the branch the registry
    names did not resolve, or the worktree was not corroborated as this
    workspace's / its tree would not read. Never `""`, never `0`.
  - failure objects, both on **stdout at exit 0**: the WHOLE-REPO
    `{"phase":"unknown","reason":<token>}` (no id — `_gh_repo_slug` failing,
    `_gh_pr_list` failing, and a gh body that is not a list of rows), and the
    PER-SESSION `{"id":…,"phase":"unknown","reason":"error"}` (incomplete
    registry; `$main` unreadable). **Neither persists anything.**
  - registry writes: `<id>.prphase`, `<id>.prnumber`, `<id>.prcheckedat`
  - `_pr_py <mode> …` — the single embedded python helper (mode `state` here;
    Task 5 adds `pick`)
  - `_gh_repo_slug <main-checkout>` → `OWNER/NAME`
  - `_gh_pr_list <repo> [head-branch]` → rows JSON, or the failure object +
    non-zero. The optional second parameter is a NAMED head filter, never a
    forwarded `"$@"`; `pr-state` passes none and its argv is unchanged
    (deviation 12).

**Context.** `--state all` is mandatory: `--state closed` is a *superset* that
includes MERGED, so filtering on it conflates merged with abandoned in both
directions. `mergeable`/`mergeStateStatus` are **never read** — they return the
literal string `"UNKNOWN"` on merged PRs. `mergeCommit.oid` is never an
identity: two PRs can share one. `--head` matches on `headRefName` **across
fork owners**, so `isCrossRepository === false` plus a base match plus proof 0
(`headRefOid` locally reachable from our tip, emitted here as `ours`) is what
binds a PR to a workspace. A 100-PR window keeps an old merged PR matchable for
months over a 144-slug namespace that `ws-reap` recycles, which is the other
reason the binding is not the branch name.

- [ ] **Step 1: Teach the harness to build a repo `_gh_repo_slug` can resolve**

**Do this first: without it Tasks 3, 4, 5, 6 and Task 12's agreement test are
unrunnable, not merely awkward.** `makeCcdHarness`'s `makeRepo`
(`ccdWsHelpers.ts:72-84`) sets `remote.origin.url` to a **local bare path**,
`$HOME/origins/<name>.git`. `_gh_repo_slug` (Step 6 below) requires
`OWNER/NAME` after stripping the GitHub prefixes, so against that layout it
returns **rc 1** — measured. Every consequence is a whole test file:
`cmd_pr_state` would answer `{"phase":"unknown","reason":"no-remote"}` for
every fixture, `cmd_pr_open` would die `no origin remote for demo` before the
`--repo o/r` assertion it is supposed to make, and `_ws_reap_eval`'s Phase C
would refuse `no-remote` before reaching the proof ladder at all.

So the fixture has to look like GitHub to `git config` and like a local bare
repo to the network. Three keys do that:

| key | value | why |
|---|---|---|
| `remote.origin.url` | `https://github.com/o/r` | what `_gh_repo_slug` reads |
| `url.<bare>.insteadOf` | `https://github.com/o/r` | what keeps **fetch and push** local |
| `remote.origin.pushurl` | `$HOME/origins/<name>.git` | states the push target outright, so `git remote -v` shows it and a later change to the rewrite cannot silently redirect a push |

`insteadOf` is the load-bearing one, and it is **not** optional: `cmd_ws_add`
runs `git -C "$main" fetch origin --quiet` (`ccd:183`) and `_ws_reap_eval`
Phase C runs `timeout 60 git -C "$main" fetch --quiet origin` before it will
prove anything, so without the rewrite every one of those calls leaves the box
for the real `github.com/o/r` — slow, flaky, and a test suite on the network.
With it the rewrite happens inside git while `git config --get
remote.origin.url` still returns the https string, which is exactly the split
we need. It also keeps Task 5's `refuses when the fetch fails` test honest:
deleting `$HOME/origins/demo.git` makes fetch fail *locally and immediately*
(measured: rc 128 in 9 ms), rather than passing for the unrelated reason that
`github.com/o/r` 404s.

**Measured, in a throwaway HOME, before this step was written** — do not
re-derive it from first principles, and do not drop `pushurl` on the grounds
that it is redundant:

| variant | `remote -v` fetch | `remote -v` push | `git push origin main` |
|---|---|---|---|
| all three keys | local bare | local bare | lands in the bare repo, rc 0 |
| `insteadOf` only | local bare | local bare | lands in the bare repo, rc 0 |
| `pushurl` only | **`https://github.com/o/r`** | local bare | lands in the bare repo, rc 0 |

So `pushurl` is belt, not brace: `insteadOf` alone would already route the push
locally. It is set anyway because "which repo does a push in this fixture
actually reach" is a question the harness should answer without the reader
having to know how url rewriting composes. What the same run also confirmed
end to end against the real `ccd`: `_gh_repo_slug` → `o/r` (rc 0),
`cmd_ws_add demo` succeeds and records `base=origin/main`,
`git push -u origin ws/quiet-basin` lands in `$HOME/origins/demo.git` and sets
the upstream, `push --force-with-lease` after an amend succeeds, and the fetch
is 14 ms — i.e. local.

`ccd-ws-gc.test.ts`, counted on `20d8829` — and none of them wants a
GitHub-looking origin.

`sh` is **not** part of this lift. `makeCcdHarness`'s `sh` passes `cwd: home`

`makeGhRepo` has to call `makeRepo`'s body, and inside an object literal it

into a named local **inside `makeCcdHarness`** beside `git` (it closes over

```ts
  /** A real git repo with one commit and an origin, so worktree/base logic is
   *  exercised for real rather than mocked. */
  const makeRepoAt = (name: string): string => {
    const origin = path.join(home, 'origins', `${name}.git`);
    const main = path.join(home, 'projects', name);
    execFileSync('git', ['init', '--bare', '-b', 'main', origin]);
    execFileSync('git', ['init', '-b', 'main', main]);
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(main, 'README.md'), 'hi\n');
    git(main, 'add', 'README.md');
    git(main, 'commit', '-m', 'init');
    git(main, 'remote', 'add', 'origin', origin);
    git(main, 'push', '-u', 'origin', 'main');
    git(main, 'remote', 'set-head', 'origin', '-a');
    return main;
  };
```

and in the returned object, `makeRepo:` becomes a reference to it, with the new
builder beside it:

```ts
    makeRepo: makeRepoAt,
    /** A repo that reads as GitHub and behaves as a local bare repo.
     *
     *  `_gh_repo_slug` reads `remote.origin.url` and requires OWNER/NAME, so a
     *  bare local path (what `makeRepo` sets) makes it return non-zero and
     *  every PR verb answer `no-remote`. Three keys:
     *    - `url`      -> the https string `_gh_repo_slug` parses
     *    - `insteadOf`-> rewrites fetch AND push back to the local bare repo.
     *      Without it `cmd_ws_add`'s `git fetch origin` (ccd:269) and
     *      `_ws_reap_eval`'s mandatory fetch would both leave the box for the
     *      real github.com. `git config --get remote.origin.url` is NOT
     *      affected by insteadOf, which is the whole point.
     *    - `pushurl`  -> the same bare repo, said out loud. Measured: insteadOf
     *      alone already routes the push locally, so this is not what makes
     *      pr-open's "the branch really landed in $HOME/origins/demo.git" work
     *      — it is here so `git remote -v` names the push target without the
     *      reader having to reason about rewrite precedence.
     *  Configured AFTER the initial push/set-head, so the repo is built with
     *  a plain local origin exactly as makeRepo builds it. */
    makeGhRepo: (name, slug = 'o/r') => {
      const main = makeRepoAt(name);
      const origin = path.join(home, 'origins', `${name}.git`);
      git(main, 'config', 'remote.origin.url', `https://github.com/${slug}`);
      git(main, 'config', `url.${origin}.insteadOf`, `https://github.com/${slug}`);
      git(main, 'config', 'remote.origin.pushurl', origin);
      return main;
    },
```

The `url.<path>.insteadOf` key name is legal with a path as the subsection:
git splits a three-level key at the FIRST and LAST dot, so
`url./tmp/x/origins/demo.git.insteadOf` parses as section `url`, subsection
`/tmp/x/origins/demo.git`, variable `insteadOf` — confirmed by reading it back
with `git config -l`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the shared gh harness**

Create `infra/ccrc/server/test/ccdPrHelpers.ts`:

```ts
// The isolated-HOME bash harness for every PR/reap ccd test, modelled on
// ccdWsHelpers.ts. `gh` is a SHELL FUNCTION, so nothing here can reach the
// network or the host's real `gho_` tokens; `timeout` is shadowed too, because
// ccd wraps every gh call in it and the stub must not be bypassed.
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { makeCcdHarness, type CcdHarness } from './ccdWsHelpers.js';

/** gh prints $HOME/gh-rows.json, exits with $HOME/gh-rc (default 0), echoes
 *  $HOME/gh-err to stderr, and appends its argv to $HOME/gh-calls so the exact
 *  flags are assertable. `timeout N cmd…` drops N and runs cmd, so a stubbed
 *  rc of 124 reproduces a real timeout exactly — and it LOGS its own argv
 *  first, because the wrapper is the only bound on a blocking DNS hang and a
 *  stub that silently swallowed it would let ccd drop `timeout` with the whole
 *  suite still green. */
export const GH_STUB = `
gh() {
  printf '%s\\n' "$*" >> "$HOME/gh-calls"
  [[ -f "$HOME/gh-err" ]]       && cat "$HOME/gh-err" >&2
  [[ -f "$HOME/gh-rows.json" ]] && cat "$HOME/gh-rows.json"
  local rc=0; [[ -f "$HOME/gh-rc" ]] && rc=$(cat "$HOME/gh-rc")
  return "$rc"
};
timeout() { printf 'timeout %s\\n' "$*" >> "$HOME/gh-calls"; shift; "$@"; };
`;

export interface PrHarness extends CcdHarness {
  /** What the stubbed `gh pr list` returns. */
  ghRows(rows: unknown[]): void;
  /** Make the stubbed gh fail: rc plus the stderr it prints. 124 = timeout. */
  ghFail(rc: number, stderr: string): void;
  ghCalls(): string[];
  /** Every argv the POISONED gh on PATH saw — i.e. every call that escaped
   *  GH_STUB. Must be empty in any test that includes the stub. */
  ghPoison(): string[];
  /** Run a snippet, returning the failure instead of throwing. */
  run(snippet: string): { code: number; stdout: string; stderr: string };
}

export function makePrHarness(prefix: string): PrHarness {
  const h = makeCcdHarness(prefix);
  const at = (n: string): string => path.join(h.home, n);

  // The gh stub above is a shell FUNCTION, and bash resolves functions before
  // PATH — so it wins whenever a snippet includes GH_STUB. This is what answers
  // when a snippet does not. It is deliberately structural rather than a rule to
  // remember: /usr/bin/gh exists on this box and ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml holds a
  // real `gho_` token with repo WRITE scope, so ONE test written without the
  // stub is a live call against the real github.com/o/r — or worse, a write. The
  // isolated HOME does not close it (GH_TOKEN/GH_HOST/GH_CONFIG_DIR are inherited
  // from the parent env, and an unauthenticated call still leaves the box). HOME
  // is isolated by construction in the harness rather than by discipline at each
  // call site; so is this.
  const bin = path.join(h.home, '.local', 'bin');
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(bin, 'gh'),
    '#!/bin/sh\nprintf \'%s\\n\' "$*" >> "$HOME/gh-poison"\n'
    + 'echo "ccd tests must never reach the real gh" >&2\nexit 97\n', { mode: 0o755 });
  const withBin = (env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = {}): NodeJS.ProcessEnv =>
    ({ ...env, PATH: `${bin}:${env['PATH'] ?? process.env['PATH'] ?? ''}` });
  const sh = (snippet: string, env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = {}): string => h.sh(snippet, withBin(env));
  const lines = (n: string): string[] => (fs.existsSync(at(n))
    ? fs.readFileSync(at(n), 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean) : []);

  return {
    ...h,
    sh,
    ghRows: (rows) => { fs.writeFileSync(at('gh-rows.json'), JSON.stringify(rows)); },
    ghFail: (rc, stderr) => {
      fs.writeFileSync(at('gh-rc'), String(rc));
      fs.writeFileSync(at('gh-err'), stderr);
    },
    ghCalls: () => lines('gh-calls'),
    ghPoison: () => lines('gh-poison'),
    run: (snippet) => {
      try { return { code: 0, stdout: sh(snippet), stderr: '' }; }
      catch (e) {
        const err = e as { status?: number; stdout?: string; stderr?: string };
        return { code: err.status ?? 1, stdout: String(err.stdout ?? ''), stderr: String(err.stderr ?? '') };
      }
    },
  };
}

/** `_cfg_dir` (ccd:1116-1123) as a lookup. Which wrapper `_ws_least_loaded`
 *  happened to pick is what decides where Claude Code keeps that session's
 *  transcript, so every assertion about a transcript path reads the registry's
 *  `wrapper` field and comes through here — hardcoding `.claude` is right for
 *  exactly one of the four wrappers and silently wrong for the other three. */
export const CFG_DIR: Record<string, string> = {
  claude: '.claude', claude2: '.claude-personal',
  'claude-corp': '.claude-corp', gpt: '.claude-gpt',
};

/** A gh row for a PR on `head`, merged into `base` by `mergeOid`, whose head
 *  commit is `headOid`. Every field the merge predicate reads is explicit — a
 *  fixture that omits one would pass for the wrong reason. */
export const mergedRow = (over: Record<string, unknown> = {}): Record<string, unknown> => ({
  number: 42, state: 'MERGED', headRefName: 'ws/quiet-basin', headRefOid: 'deadbee',
  baseRefName: 'main', isCrossRepository: false, mergedAt: '2026-07-20T10:00:00Z',
  mergeCommit: { oid: '7a68ca0' }, url: 'https://github.com/o/r/pull/42',
  title: 'the work', isDraft: false, statusCheckRollup: null, ...over,
});
```

```ts
 *  a real oid the binding check can be pointed at.

 *  `makeGhRepo`, never `makeRepo`: `_gh_repo_slug` reads `remote.origin.url`
 *  and `makeRepo`'s is a local bare PATH, so every assertion below would read
 *  `{"phase":"unknown","reason":"no-remote"}` instead of the phase it names. */
const workspaceWithCommit = (project: string, slug: string): { wt: string; main: string; tip: string } => {
  const main = h.makeGhRepo(project);
  h.sh(`${WS_ADD} CCD_WS_SLUG=${slug} cmd_ws_add ${project}`);

  h.git(wt, 'add', 'f.txt');
  h.git(wt, 'commit', '-m', 'the work');
  return { wt, main, tip: h.git(wt, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD') };
};
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Add the gh helpers to `ccd`**

Insert after `_ws_ignored_digest` (added in Task 2):

```bash
_gh_pr_list() {   # repo [head-branch] -> rows JSON on stdout; on failure prints
                  # the answer object instead and returns non-zero. NEVER
                  # partially prints.
  # The head filter is a NAMED second parameter and the flag is built here — it
  # is never a forwarded "$@". pflag is last-wins, so a passthrough on the one
  # gh call two verbs share would let a caller override --repo or --state.
  # pr-open needs the filter because it asks a question about ONE branch; both
  # readers get the same fields, the same 100-PR window and the same failure
  # classification, which is the point of there being one reader.
  local repo="$1" head="${2:-}" errf out rc err
  local -a filter=()
  [[ -n "$head" ]] && filter=(--head "$head")
  errf=$(mktemp)
  out=$(timeout "$PR_GH_TIMEOUT" gh pr list --repo "$repo" "${filter[@]}" --state all --limit 100 \
          --json "$PR_JSON_FIELDS" 2>"$errf"); rc=$?
  err=$(cat "$errf" 2>/dev/null); rm -f "$errf"
  if (( rc == 124 )); then printf '{"phase":"unknown","reason":"timeout"}\n'; return 1; fi
  if (( rc != 0 )); then
    # `gh auth status` is NOT probed first: it is another network call on the
    # unhappy path. The stderr we already have is the cheaper signal.
    case "$err" in
      *"gh auth login"*|*"not logged in"*|*"HTTP 401"*) printf '{"phase":"unknown","reason":"unauthenticated"}\n' ;;
      *"rate limit"*|*"HTTP 403"*)                      printf '{"phase":"unknown","reason":"rate-limit"}\n' ;;
      *"dial tcp"*|*"no such host"*|*"proxyconnect"*)   printf '{"phase":"unknown","reason":"offline"}\n' ;;
      *)                                                printf '{"phase":"unknown","reason":"error"}\n' ;;
    esac
    return 1
  fi
  printf '%s\n' "$out"
}
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Add the one embedded python helper**

Insert after `_gh_pr_list`:

```bash
_pr_py() {   # mode [args…]; stdin = the gh rows JSON. The ONE embedded helper.
  # Embedded rather than a sibling file on purpose: ~/.local/bin/ccd is a COPY,
  # so a second file is a second deployment step and a new failure mode in
  # which `ccd caps` advertises a verb whose helper is missing.
  #
  # The program arrives on fd 3, NOT on stdin: `python3 - <<'PY'` reads the
  # program FROM stdin, so the heredoc and the piped rows are the same channel
  # and python consumes the whole of it as source — `sys.stdin.read()` then
  # returns '' at EOF, `rows_in()` answers [], and every PR in the fixture
  # vanishes into `phase:"none"` at exit 0. Measured both forms side by side:
  # `python3 - "$@" <<PY` gives stdin='', `python3 /dev/fd/3 "$@" 3<<PY` gives
  # the rows, with sys.argv identical. The rows cannot move to argv instead —
  # spec §7 is that no GitHub-sourced string is ever placed in an argv.
  python3 /dev/fd/3 "$@" 3<<'PY'
import json, os, re, subprocess, sys, time

mode = sys.argv[1]
# `headRefOid` and `mergeCommit.oid` are GitHub-SOURCED, and `is_ours` puts the
# first of them in a git argv. Spec §7: no GitHub-sourced string is ever placed
# in a prompt, an argv, or a shell — so this is the boundary, not a formality.
# Both ends are anchored and the floor is 7, and both are pinned: a row saying
# `headRefOid: "main"` otherwise resolves as a REVISION and binds (main really
# is an ancestor of our tip), and `{1,40}` would let a three-character hex ref
# like `abc` do the same. `is_merged` reads `mergeCommit.oid` through it as a
# SHAPE check only — a merge commit is never an identity, two PRs can share one.
OID = re.compile(r'^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$')

def rows_in():
    """The rows, or None for A BODY WE COULD NOT READ — which is NOT `[]`.

    `[]` is an affirmative answer: this repository has no pull request for you,
    which is `phase:"none"`, which is the one answer meaning "ready to open a
    PR" — and which CLEARS the persisted number. Collapsing an unintelligible
    body into it therefore turns "I could not understand GitHub" into "GitHub
    says the merge you had is gone". `gh` exiting 0 is not the same as `gh`
    having answered: an empty stdout, a JSON object, a proxy's HTML error page
    and a truncated array all arrive here at rc 0. Empty counts as unreadable
    too — `gh pr list --json` prints `[]` for a repo with no PRs, never
    nothing, and an empty stdin is exactly what deviation 8's program-on-stdin
    defect produced."""
    raw = sys.stdin.read().strip()
    if not raw:
        return None
    try:
        v = json.loads(raw)
    except Exception:
        return None
    return v if isinstance(v, list) else None

def git(main, *args):
    return subprocess.run(['git', '-C', main, *args], capture_output=True, text=True)

def is_ours(main, tip, oid):
    """Proof 0 — the PR's head commit exists locally AND, where we have a tip to
    reach from, is reachable from it. This is what a recycled slug and a
    stranger's fork both fail.

    The cat-file rung survives mutation and is kept deliberately: `merge-base
    --is-ancestor` on an object this repository does not have exits 128 and so
    already answers False. Kept because 128 is git's *"I could not do this"*
    and 1 is its *"no"*, and this function must not start reading a fatal as an
    answer if the ancestry call is ever changed. (`OID`'s `{7,40}` survives too:
    `{1,40}` accepts the same strings any real headRefOid is — it bounds a
    GitHub-sourced string rather than deciding anything, and the cat-file rung
    is what actually rejects a value.)

    `tip is None` is the registry's branch not resolving in $main — a hand
    rename or a hand delete, which deviation 7 measured and calls ORDINARY.
    There is then no anchor to reach FROM, and answering False demotes a bound
    MERGED row to `no-commits` and clears the persisted number: a LOCAL fact
    erasing GitHub's answer about a PR. So the ancestry rung is SKIPPED rather
    than failed, and what remains is still three of four conjuncts plus "this
    repository can still see that commit". The recycled slug — the case the
    ancestry rung exists for — cannot be in this state: ws-add creates the
    branch, so a recycled name always resolves and always gets the full proof.
    The wire says which rung answered: `tip` is null beside `ours`."""
    if not isinstance(oid, str) or not OID.match(oid):
        return False
    if git(main, 'cat-file', '-e', oid + '^{commit}').returncode != 0:
        return False
    if tip is None:
        return True
    return git(main, 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', '--', oid, tip).returncode == 0

def annotate(rows, main, tip, branch, base_short):
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        if not isinstance(r, dict):
            continue
        r['ours'] = is_ours(main, tip, r.get('headRefOid'))
        out.append(r)
    return out

def bound(r, branch, base_short):
    """The workspace<->PR binding. Branch name alone is not it."""
    return (r.get('isCrossRepository') is False
            and r.get('baseRefName') == base_short
            and r.get('headRefName') == branch
            and r.get('ours') is True)

def is_merged(r, branch, base_short):
    # The trailing `bound(...)` conjunct survives mutation: every caller today
    # passes a row `pick` already filtered by `bound`. It stays so the predicate
    # is true of ANY row rather than only of a pre-filtered one — Task 5's
    # `pick` mode calls it too, and "merged" is the answer that fires the
    # archive trigger, which is not a fact to infer from the caller's habits.
    oid = (r.get('mergeCommit') or {}).get('oid')
    return (r.get('state') == 'MERGED'
            and isinstance(r.get('mergedAt'), str)
            and isinstance(oid, str) and OID.match(oid) is not None
            and bound(r, branch, base_short))

def pick(rows, branch, base_short):
    """Highest number AFTER the binding check, never before."""
    cands = [r for r in rows if bound(r, branch, base_short)]
    cands.sort(key=lambda r: r.get('number') if isinstance(r.get('number'), int) else 0)
    return cands[-1] if cands else None

if mode == 'state':
    (id_, project, main, repo, branch, base, base_short, tip, ahead, dirty, template, reg) = sys.argv[2:14]
    # An argv can only carry a string, so "" is how the shell says UNMEASURED
    # for all three. None here and JSON null on the wire, never 0 and never "":
    # a number is a measurement, and none of these was measured. Deviation 7's
    # `tip: null` rule for the archive manifest, applied to the same fact.
    tip = tip or None
    ahead = int(ahead) if ahead != '' else None
    dirty = int(dirty) if dirty != '' else None
    raw_rows = rows_in()
    if raw_rows is None:
        # THE ID-LESS SHAPE, on purpose: the body is one gh call's answer for the
        # whole repository, so it is unreadable for every session of it at once —
        # which is what the id-less object means and what the sweep's per-project
        # backoff keys off. Nothing is persisted: the last good phase, number and
        # checkedAt all stay, which is what makes "last checked 6m ago" the honest
        # reading rather than a fresh-looking lie.
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({'phase': 'unknown', 'reason': 'error'}) + '\n')
        sys.exit(0)
    rows = annotate(raw_rows, main, tip, branch, base_short)
    chosen = pick(rows, branch, base_short)
    # `reason` accompanies `phase` and stays None for every phase but one, so
    # that prstate.ts's phaseFor can be pinned equal to this on BOTH fields.
    reason = None
    if chosen is None:
        # `ahead is None` is UNMEASURED, and `None == 0` is False in python, so an
        # unresolvable ref falls through to `none` — "no PR bound to this
        # workspace", which is what was actually observed — instead of
        # `no-commits`, which asserts that the branch is level with base.
        phase, number = ('no-commits' if ahead == 0 else 'none'), None
    elif is_merged(chosen, branch, base_short):
        phase, number = 'merged', chosen.get('number')
    elif chosen.get('state') == 'MERGED':
        # gh says MERGED but a conjunct failed. Never claim merged on a partial
        # match: the archive trigger and the cleanup offer both hang off it.
        # `merge-unproven`, NOT `error`: the gh read succeeded, and calling this
        # `error` puts "GitHub could not be read" on a phone about a read that
        # worked. phaseFor answers the same token for the same row.
        phase, number, reason = 'unknown', chosen.get('number'), 'merge-unproven'
    elif chosen.get('state') == 'CLOSED':
        phase, number = 'closed', chosen.get('number')
    elif chosen.get('isDraft') is True:
        phase, number = 'draft', chosen.get('number')
    else:
        phase, number = 'open', chosen.get('number')

    commits = []
    if tip and base:
        # `--` AFTER the revisions, per Global Constraints. SURVIVES mutation by
        # construction, exactly as the `rev-list` one does: `$base` comes from
        # the registry and always yields a `..`-bearing operand, so git can only
        # read it as a range and no fixture can distinguish the two forms. The
        # rule exists because git's own disambiguation is positional, and
        # `git diff --quiet -- A B` silently treats both shas as PATHSPECS
        # (verified: exit 0, where the same call with `--` last exits 1).
        r = git(main, 'log', '--format=%H%x1f%s%x1f%b%x1e', base + '..refs/heads/' + branch, '--')
        if r.returncode == 0:
            for rec in r.stdout.split('\x1e'):
                rec = rec.strip('\n')
                if not rec:
                    continue
                parts = (rec.split('\x1f') + ['', '', ''])[:3]
                commits.append({'sha': parts[0], 'subject': parts[1], 'body': parts[2].strip()})

    checked_at = int(time.time() * 1000)
    def put(field, value):
        with open(os.path.join(reg, id_ + '.' + field), 'w') as f:
            f.write(str(value))

    def clear(field):
        try:
            os.remove(os.path.join(reg, id_ + '.' + field))
        except FileNotFoundError:
            pass

    put('prphase', phase)
    # phase and number are ONE answer, so a writer that persists half of it
    # lies. A PR that is deleted, force-pushed out of reachability, or whose
    # slug ws-reap has recycled leaves {phase:'none', number:42} on disk if the
    # number is merely left alone: fleet.ts hands that pair straight to the
    # wire, so the cap renders `#42` under a phase whose own copy is "no pull
    # request yet", and ws-archive reads the same field and files
    # `archivedreason merged:#42` for a PR that no longer binds to this
    # workspace. REMOVED rather than blanked, so the field is absent exactly as
    # it is for a workspace that never had a PR.
    #
    # NO FAILED READ REACHES THIS LINE, and it takes two guards to say that, not
    # one. `_gh_pr_list` returns before `_pr_py` is called for every read that
    # failed by EXIT CODE. An rc-0 read whose body is not a list of rows does
    # reach `_pr_py` — and `rows_in` answering None returns above, before any
    # `put`/`clear` runs. The comment here used to claim the first guard alone
    # made this unreachable; it did not, and a `gh` that exited 0 with an empty
    # or unparseable stdout cleared a persisted `merged:#42`.
    if number is None:
        clear('prnumber')
    else:
        put('prnumber', number)
    put('prcheckedat', checked_at)

    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        'id': id_, 'project': project, 'repo': repo, 'branch': branch, 'base': base,
        'baseShort': base_short, 'tip': tip, 'ahead': ahead, 'dirty': dirty,
        'commits': commits, 'template': template or None, 'rows': rows,
        'phase': phase, 'number': number, 'checkedAt': checked_at, 'reason': reason,
    }) + '\n')
PY
}
```

```bash
_pr_state_one() {   # id main repo rows -> one JSON line
  local id="$1" main="$2" repo="$3" rows="$4"
  local project branch base baseShort tip ahead workdir dirty tmpl
  project=$(_reg_get "$id" project); branch=$(_reg_get "$id" branch)
  base=$(_reg_get "$id" base);       workdir=$(_reg_get "$id" workdir)
  # CARRIES THE ID. A per-session failure and a whole-repo failure are
  # different events: the server backs a PROJECT off on the id-less shape,
  # which three sites emit — `_gh_repo_slug`, `_gh_pr_list`, and `_pr_py`
  # mode `state` for an unparseable rc-0 body — and each of those really is
  # one gh answer for the whole repo, so every session of it is equally
  # unreadable. An id-less object HERE, by contrast, would let one
  # registry-incomplete workspace mark its seven siblings `unknown` and
  # silence the whole project's lane. §6's "Partial sweep" row promises
  # per-session honesty; this is where that is kept.
  [[ -n "$branch" ]] || { printf '{"id":%s,"phase":"unknown","reason":"error"}\n' "$(_json_str "$id")"; return 0; }
  [[ -n "$base" ]] || base="origin/HEAD"
  baseShort="${base#origin/}"
  # `--quiet` turns git's own two answers into two exit codes, and the same
  # three-way case `_ws_archive_manifest` walks (ccd:990-995) is walked here for
  # the same reason. Measured on git 2.43: rc 1 for an absent ref in a readable
  # repository, rc 128 when the repository cannot be read at all — and WITHOUT
  # `--quiet`, 128 for both, which collapses "the branch was renamed" into "I
  # cannot see this repository". `tip=""` here means the FIRST of those and is
  # emitted as JSON null; the second is not a fact about a PR at all, so it is
  # this session's failure object and persists nothing.
  #
  # The `tip=""` arm is an EQUIVALENT mutant, disclosed rather than pinned: the
  # command substitution already assigned "" when rev-parse printed nothing, so
  # deleting the assignment changes no value. It is written out because the arm
  # is where a reader learns that rc 1 is a FIELD and not a failure, and an empty
  # arm is indistinguishable from an unhandled one.
  local rc
  tip=$(git -C "$main" rev-parse --verify --quiet "refs/heads/$branch" 2>/dev/null); rc=$?
  case "$rc" in
    0) : ;;
    1) tip="" ;;
    *) printf '{"id":%s,"phase":"unknown","reason":"error"}\n' "$(_json_str "$id")"; return 0 ;;
  esac
  # "" is UNMEASURED, not zero. `ahead=0` is the claim "this branch is level with
  # base", which is what `no-commits` is built from, and a ref that does not
  # resolve has not been measured against anything. _pr_py reads "" as null.
  ahead=""
  if [[ -n "$tip" ]] && git -C "$main" rev-parse --verify --quiet "$base" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # `--` after the revisions per Global Constraints, and it SURVIVES mutation
    # by construction: `$base` comes from the registry and always yields a
    # `..`-bearing operand, which git can only read as a range, so no fixture can
    # distinguish the two forms. Followed anyway — git's disambiguation is
    # positional, and the rule is cheaper than re-deciding it per call site.
    ahead=$(git -C "$main" rev-list --count "$base..refs/heads/$branch" -- 2>/dev/null)
    # The GUARD and its FALLBACK VALUE both survive mutation, and for the same
    # reason: both revisions were verified a line ago, so rev-list has no way to
    # fail here today and nothing can observe which value the guard would have
    # written. Kept because `int(ahead)` in _pr_py raises on a non-numeric string
    # and this session's whole line then disappears from the sweep's output; `""`
    # rather than `0` because an unwritten count is UNMEASURED, which is what the
    # rest of this function now says, and `0` would say "level with base".
    [[ "$ahead" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || ahead=""
  fi
  # THE ONE READ IN THIS VERB THAT IS ABOUT A DIRECTORY. ccrc asks $main;
  # $workdir is otherwise only ever a path git is asked ABOUT — but "what is
  # uncommitted here" is a question about that directory's contents, so it is
  # `-C "$workdir"` and therefore has to be ENTITLED first: git's own record AND
  # the directory itself must both say $main, the pair `cmd_ws_rm` requires
  # before it touches anything and `_ws_archive_manifest` walks for the identical
  # read. Neither rung alone is enough — the record outlives the directory, so a
  # hand-deletion plus a stray `git init` still answers $branch while its tree
  # belongs to a stranger. Measured: without the common-dir rung the squatter's
  # two untracked files were counted and reported as this workspace's.
  #
  # UNENTITLED OR UNREADABLE IS `null`, NOT A REFUSAL AND NEVER 0. `dirty` is an
  # advisory — the PR state is entirely knowable when gh answered and the
  # worktree did not — and this verb answers for every workspace of a project
  # from one gh call, so refusing here would cost the siblings their state too.
  # `ws-archive` refuses on these same facts because it writes a record that
  # authorises deletions; this one only reports. What is NOT allowed is `0`: the
  # shipped one-liner piped into `grep -c` and threw git's status away, so a
  # deleted worktree answered `"dirty": 0` — an affirmative "nothing is
  # uncommitted here" about a directory that is not there. That is deviation 6's
  # silent-empty-stream defect, one task later in the same file. `registered` and
  # the status are read from `$?` on their own lines: `local x=$(cmd)` returns
  # local's status, not the command's.
  #
  # Two of the three rungs survive mutation and are kept rather than pinned,
  # because each is redundant only GIVEN the others and the rule names all three:
  #   - `registered != 0` — a path whose common dir equals `$main`'s is inside
  #     `$main`'s repository, and `git status` from anywhere in a worktree
  #     reports that worktree, so the count is the same with or without this
  #     rung today. It is the rung the plan's rule names FIRST, and it is the one
  #     that stops answering if `_ws_common_dir` is ever loosened.
  #   - `-z "$main_common"` — an unreadable `$main` makes both sides empty and
  #     therefore equal, which is the fail-OPEN this guard exists to stop; it is
  #     unreachable only because the tip read above already returned on rc 128.
  # The `wd_common != main_common` rung is the one that catches the squatter, and
  # it is pinned.
  local wthead registered wd_common main_common porcelain prc
  dirty=""
  wthead=$(_ws_wt_branch "$main" "$workdir"); registered=$?
  wd_common=$(_ws_common_dir "$workdir"); main_common=$(_ws_common_dir "$main")
  if (( registered != 0 )) || [[ -z "$main_common" || "$wd_common" != "$main_common" ]]; then
    echo "pr-state: $workdir is not a corroborated worktree of $main — dirty unknown for $id" >&2
  else
    porcelain=$(git -C "$workdir" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null); prc=$?
    if (( prc == 0 )); then dirty=$(printf '%s' "$porcelain" | grep -c . || true)
    else echo "pr-state: could not read the tree at $workdir — dirty unknown for $id" >&2; fi
  fi
  tmpl=""
  [[ -f "$main/.github/pull_request_template.md" ]] && tmpl=$(cat "$main/.github/pull_request_template.md")
  printf '%s' "$rows" | _pr_py state "$id" "$project" "$main" "$repo" "$branch" "$base" \
    "$baseShort" "$tip" "$ahead" "$dirty" "$tmpl" "$REG"
}

cmd_pr_state() {   # ccd pr-state --session <id> | ccd pr-state --project <project>
  # ONE gh call per repo, whichever form. Read-only apart from the three
  # registry fields it persists so a ccrc restart degrades to honest stale.
  [[ $# -eq 2 ]] || die "usage: ccd pr-state --session <id> | ccd pr-state --project <project>"
  local mode=$1 arg=$2
  case "$mode" in
    --session) [[ $arg =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || die "bad session id" ;;
    --project) [[ $arg =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || die "bad project" ;;
    *)         die "usage: ccd pr-state --session <id> | ccd pr-state --project <project>" ;;
  esac

  local -a ids=()
  if [[ $mode == --session ]]; then
    [[ -f "$REG/$arg.uuid" ]] || die "no such session: $arg"
    [[ -n "$(_reg_get "$arg" workspace)" ]] || die "not a workspace: $arg"
    ids=("$arg")
  else
    local f id
    for f in "$REG"/*.workspace; do
      # An empty registry leaves the glob unexpanded. Survives mutation because
      # the `.uuid` test below then looks for a file literally named `*.uuid`
      # and fails too — an accident of two guards, not one guard doing two jobs.
      [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
      id=$(basename "$f" .workspace)
      # The same regex `--session` applies to its argv, applied to what the
      # directory listing handed back — every `$REG/$id.*` path below is built
      # from it. The plan's rule is "before any path is built from an id", with
      # no exception for ids ccd wrote itself; a filename cannot hold a `/` so
      # nothing traversable is reachable and every read here is read-only, which
      # makes this the rule rather than a hole being closed.
      [[ "$id" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || continue
      [[ -f "$REG/$id.uuid" ]] || continue
      [[ "$(_reg_get "$id" project)" == "$arg" ]] || continue
      ids+=("$id")
    done
  fi
  (( ${#ids[@]} )) || return 0

  local project main repo rows
  project=$(_reg_get "${ids[0]}" project)
  # A registry VALUE, and `$main` is built from it. `--session` validated the id
  # it was handed and nothing validated this. `die`, not an answer object,
  # because a project name ccd cannot build a path from is a registry-IDENTITY
  # error — the class this verb already dies on (`no such session`, `not a
  # workspace`) — and it costs the repo's one gh call per sweep to proceed.
  [[ "$project" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || die "bad project in registry for ${ids[0]}"
  main="$PROJECTS_ROOT/$project"
  repo=$(_gh_repo_slug "$main") || { printf '{"phase":"unknown","reason":"no-remote"}\n'; return 0; }
  # The answer object _gh_pr_list printed IS the output on failure: one repo
  # failing marks that repo's sessions unknown and touches no other project.
  rows=$(_gh_pr_list "$repo") || { printf '%s\n' "$rows"; return 0; }

  local id
  for id in "${ids[@]}"; do _pr_state_one "$id" "$main" "$repo" "$rows"; done
}
```
