- [ ] **Step 4: Add the guard evaluator to `ccd`**

Insert after `cmd_pr_open`:

```bash
# ── reap guards ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Evaluated by ws-audit to PRODUCE a verdict, and again by ws-reap to RE-PROVE
# it at the instant of deletion. One implementation, two evaluations at two
# times: the audit's verdict is never trusted, it is recomputed.

# THE secret-shaped name list, and now it has TWO consumers, so it is a list
# rather than a `case` — `_ws_sensitive_match` walks it for one name, and
# `_WS_SENSITIVE_FIND` is the same list as a `find` predicate for the scan
# INSIDE a collapsed ignored directory. Two hand-maintained copies of a §7
# guard's definition is exactly the drift this design cannot afford, so the
# predicate is DERIVED here, once, at source time.
#
# Small, non-rotting and permanent. `.ccrc/` deliberately does NOT match: it is
# listed and destroyed like any other ignored directory, because ccd itself put
# it in info/exclude and exempting it would be a blind spot ccd manufactured.
#
# `.env*` AND `*.env`, because dotenv has two spellings and only the first was
# here for a round: `production.env`, `prod.env` and `My Project.env` all read
# as ordinary rubbish queued for deletion in the one guard §7 forbids
# overriding, while four places claimed the case was closed by the `-z` read. It
# was not; `-z` fixed the QUOTING of `deploy key.pem` and `prod db.sqlite`,
# whose suffixes were already listed, and `My Project.env` had no arm to match
# quoted or unquoted. `env.sample` and `environment` are the negatives that keep
# this a suffix and not a substring.
_WS_SENSITIVE_GLOBS=( '.env*' '*.env' '*.pem' '*.key' '*.p12' 'id_[dre]*' '*.kdbx'
                      'credentials*' '*.sqlite*' '*.db' '*.dump' '*.sql' 'secrets*' )
_WS_SENSITIVE_FIND=()
for _wsg in "${_WS_SENSITIVE_GLOBS[@]}"; do
  (( ${#_WS_SENSITIVE_FIND[@]} )) && _WS_SENSITIVE_FIND+=( -o )
  _WS_SENSITIVE_FIND+=( -name "$_wsg" )
done
unset _wsg

_ws_sensitive_match() {   # path -> 0 when it is secret-shaped
  # `[[ $b == $g ]]` with the pattern UNQUOTED is glob matching, i.e. the same
  # operation each `case` arm used to be — including `id_[dre]*`'s bracket
  # expression. `pins the two matchers to one list` walks a table of positives
  # and negatives through this function AND through the find predicate and
  # requires the same answer from both.
  local b="${1%/}" g; b="${b##*/}"
  for g in "${_WS_SENSITIVE_GLOBS[@]}"; do
    [[ "$b" == $g ]] && return 0
  done
  return 1
}

# F3 REFINEMENT (pre-merge fix round; the human partner ruled directly:
# apply it). The inside-of-ignored scan enumerates every entry under a
# collapsed directory, and three of the globs above — `credentials*`,
# `secrets*`, `*.pem` — reach one directory into a dependency or build tree
# and catch its ORDINARY contents there: a TypeScript declaration file, a
# generated JS bundle and its sourcemap, a template. Measured over 15 real
# projects: 338 inside-hits, 7 of 15 projects refused on the FIRST tap, and
# essentially all of it was exactly this shape — `credentials.d.ts`,
# `cacert.pem`, 33 x `.env.example`, `secretsmanager.generated.js`,
# `secrets-manager.js.map`. A secret-shaped name that ALSO ends in a source,
# compiled or template extension is NOISE, not a secret. Measured effect:
# 32 hits, 4 of 15 projects — and the survivors still include the real
# `.env`, `.env.local`,
# `infrastructure/dist/config/{production,staging,dev}.env` and
# `dev-data/app.db`, exactly the content this guard exists for.
#
# EXCLUDED IS NOT INVISIBLE — the other half of the ruling. Every name this
# drops is still COUNTED (`REAP_SENSITIVE_FILTERED`, `sensitiveFiltered` on
# the wire), so a wrong filter is something anyone can notice from the
# audit's own output rather than a silent hole. This is a §7 no-override
# guard, so the list is narrow and enumerated rather than inferred from a
# pattern: on any doubt a name stays sensitive.
_WS_SENSITIVE_NOISE_EXT=( ts tsx js jsx mjs cjs map py pyc pyi go rs java rb php cs c h cpp swift kt
                          example sample template dist )

_ws_sensitive_noise() {   # path -> 0 when a secret-shaped name is vendored/template NOISE
  local b="${1%/}" ext; b="${b##*/}"
  for ext in "${_WS_SENSITIVE_NOISE_EXT[@]}"; do
    [[ "$b" == *".$ext" ]] && return 0
  done
  return 1
}

REAP_SCAN_SECONDS=30      # the whole-workspace bound on the inside-of-ignored scan

_ws_sensitive_inside() {   # absdir relpath deadline -> 0 with hits in _WS_INSIDE_HITS, 1 = the scan did not complete
  # THE §0 GUARD, ONE DIRECTORY DOWN. `--ignored=matching` collapses a wholly
  # ignored directory to a SINGLE entry, so `build/.env` holding a live key was
  # handed to `_ws_sensitive_match` as `build/`, matched nothing, and was
  # deleted under a sheet reading "not in git · 1 entry, 39 B — build/".
  # Measured end to end before this existed: verdict `reapable`, a token issued,
  # `sensitive: []`, and `build/.env` gone afterwards. Moving one secret one
  # directory deeper defeated the only guard §7 refuses to give an override.
  #
  # `find`, NOT `git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard`, and the
  # difference is not a preference — measured on git 2.43 with a nested
  # repository inside an ignored `build/`:
  #     git ls-files …  ->  build/nested/          (one entry, and that is all)
  #     find …          ->  build/nested/.env      (the file)
  # git collapses a nested repository exactly the way `--ignored=matching`
  # collapses an ignored directory, so it reproduces this very blindness one
  # level deeper — over content `rm -rf` destroys all the same. The question
  # here is "what will be deleted", which is a filesystem question.
  #
  # ALL TYPES, not `-type f`: `_ws_sensitive_match` matches DIRECTORY names too
  # (git hands it `secrets/` as a top-level entry and the `%/` strip is there
  # for exactly that), so restricting the scan to regular files would answer a
  # different question inside than outside.
  #
  # BOUNDED, and the bound is a DEADLINE for the whole workspace rather than a
  # per-entry timeout, so a workspace with 226 ignored entries cannot cost 226
  # timeouts. Measured on this box against the tree `--ignored=matching` was
  # chosen for (custom-tools: 226 collapsed entries, 355,392 entries beneath
  # them): 3.4 s with one `find` per entry, 1.2 s as a single walk. The
  # performance reason for `--ignored=matching` still holds for the DISPLAY —
  # nothing here is printed, counted or sized, only matched — and sensitivity
  # cannot be sampled. Expiry is a read that did not complete, which is a
  # refusal, and the remedy travels in the message.
  #
  # ANY DIAGNOSTIC IS ALSO A READ THAT DID NOT COMPLETE, the same rule and the
  # same polarity as the `git status` beside it: a `chmod 000` subdirectory
  # makes find print `Permission denied` and carry on, and the entries it could
  # not reach are then simply absent — which is the state that says "no secrets
  # here" about files nobody enumerated.
  # `${1%/}` — git names a collapsed directory `build/`, with the trailing
  # slash, and a doubled separator makes `${f#"$abs"/}` match nothing, so every
  # hit came back as `build/` + the ABSOLUTE path. Measured.
  # TWO MUTATION SURVIVORS, disclosed and measured, and they are the same
  # reason: nothing can spend the budget in a fixture. `left=$(( deadline -
  # SECONDS ))` can be replaced by a constant, and `(( left > 0 ))` by `(( 1 ))`,
  # with the whole suite green (44 files / 712 tests, exit 0, each measured on
  # its own) — because reaching either needs a scan that really takes 30 s, and
  # the largest ignored tree on this box takes 3.4 s. What IS pinned is the
  # `rc == 124` arm (`refuses, with the remedy, when the scan runs out of its
  # budget`, which fails `timeout` for `find` alone), so the EXPIRY behaviour
  # has a fixture and only the clock that produces it does not. They stay
  # because a per-entry timeout is the thing they exist to prevent: without the
  # subtraction each entry gets a fresh 30 s and 226 entries cost 226 of them.
  local abs="${1%/}" rel="${2%/}" ent="$2" deadline="$3" outf errf err rc left f
  _WS_INSIDE_HITS=()
  left=$(( deadline - SECONDS ))
  (( left > 0 )) || {
    REAP_IGNREASON="the scan of the ignored directories did not finish within ${REAP_SCAN_SECONDS}s (stopped at $ent): remove or move the largest ignored directory and reap again"
    return 1
  }
  # TWO MORE MUTATION SURVIVORS, disclosed and measured, and they are the same
  # pair `_ws_collect_ignored` discloses for the same reason: an empty temp-file
  # name is itself a failing redirect, so `>""` never runs the scan and the
  # `(( rc == 0 ))` rung below refuses anyway. Both stay because each states the
  # case it is about, and because the fall-through only holds while that later
  # line keeps its `rm`. The four `rm -f "$outf"` here ARE pinned individually,
  # by `removes the inside-scan's scratch files too`, which walks all four exits
  # — with any one deleted a fixture for a DIFFERENT failure still cleans up.
  outf=$(mktemp) || return 1
  errf=$(mktemp) || { rm -f "$outf"; return 1; }
  timeout "$left" find "$abs" -mindepth 1 \( "${_WS_SENSITIVE_FIND[@]}" \) -print0 \
    >"$outf" 2>"$errf"; rc=$?
  err=$(cat "$errf" 2>/dev/null); rm -f "$errf"
  if (( rc == 124 )); then
    rm -f "$outf"
    REAP_IGNREASON="the scan of the ignored directories did not finish within ${REAP_SCAN_SECONDS}s (stopped at $ent): remove or move the largest ignored directory and reap again"
    return 1
  fi
  (( rc == 0 )) || { rm -f "$outf"; REAP_IGNREASON="could not walk the ignored directory $ent"; return 1; }
  [[ -z "$err" ]] || { rm -f "$outf"; REAP_IGNREASON="could not read all of the ignored directory $ent ($err)"; return 1; }
  # `${f#"$abs"/}` with the prefix QUOTED: an unquoted one is a GLOB, and an
  # ignored directory is free to be called `build[1]`.
  while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    [[ -n "$f" ]] || continue
    _WS_INSIDE_HITS+=( "$rel/${f#"$abs"/}" )
  done <"$outf"
  rm -f "$outf"
}

_ws_collect_ignored() {   # workdir — fills REAP_IGNORED (`sensitive\tbytes\tpath`) / REAP_SENSITIVE / REAP_IGNDIGEST
  # NON-ZERO when the ignored set could not be READ, and both of its reads are
  # checked. Neither failure can be allowed to look like "there is nothing
  # ignored here", because that is the answer that authorises the delete:
  #
  #   - The DIGEST half forges the token. A failure and an empty set hash
  #     identically (Task 2, deviation 6), so a discarded status puts "" into
  #     REAP_IGNDIGEST on the audit side AND on the reap side, the fingerprints
  #     match, and D2's consent check passes. Measured with only
  #     `status --ignored=matching` failing: both sides produce
  #     `igndigest='' … token=17af9144…`, an exact match, from a read that never
  #     happened. The digest is now built from the RECORDS this function
  #     produces rather than from a second `git status` (see the tail), so this
  #     read is the only one that can fail and its status is checked here.
  #   - The ENUMERATION half is worse, because it needs no token at all: an empty
  #     REAP_SENSITIVE means `sensitive-ignored` cannot fire, and the resume path
  #     (Task 6 Step 4) reads that array directly. Same measurement:
  #     `sensitive=()` for a worktree holding a gitignored `secrets/creds.env`.
  #
  # The read is therefore ONE `git status` whose status is checked, and the loop
  # filters `!! ` itself rather than piping through grep — a pipeline's exit code
  # would be grep's, and grep exits 1 on a legitimately empty ignored set. It is
  # also the ONLY `git status` here now: `_ws_ignored_digest` survives for the
  # ARCHIVE manifest, which records what it cannot describe rather than refusing.
  #
  # AND THE EXIT CODE IS NOT THE WHOLE ANSWER. A PARTIALLY unreadable tree makes
  # git warn and exit 0: measured on git 2.43, `chmod 000` on a subdirectory
  # gives rc 0, no line for anything inside it, and `warning: could not open
  # directory 'sub/'` on stderr — which `2>/dev/null` throws away. The entries
  # git could not reach are then simply absent, so a gitignored `secrets/` under
  # that directory leaves REAP_SENSITIVE empty and `sensitive-ignored`, a guard
  # §7 forbids overriding, cannot fire over files nobody ever enumerated. So
  # stderr is captured and ANY diagnostic is a read that did not complete.
  # Deliberately not a match on git's wording: git translates its warnings and
  # ccd pins no locale, so a text test would pass silently on a box with LANG
  # set — the failure mode this exists to remove.
  #
  # AND THE READ IS `-z`, WHICH IS A CORRECTNESS REQUIREMENT, NOT A STYLE.
  # Without it git C-QUOTES any path holding a space, a non-ASCII byte, a quote,
  # a backslash or a control character: measured on git 2.43, `!! .env` bare
  # beside `!! "deploy key.pem"` and `!! "s\303\251crets/"`. `_ws_sensitive_match`
  # is then handed a string whose first and last characters are `"`, so every
  # SUFFIX pattern dies on the trailing quote and every PREFIX pattern on the
  # leading one — measured end to end, a gitignored private key named
  # `deploy key.pem` produced verdict=reapable, sensitive:false and a TOKEN,
  # against the one guard §7 says has no override (`prod db.sqlite`,
  # `ssh key.pem`, same shape). This comment used to name `My Project.env` in
  # that list and was WRONG to: its suffix had no arm in `_ws_sensitive_match`
  # at all, so it was un-matched quoted and un-matched unquoted, and no amount of
  # `-z` was going to close it. That one is closed where it lives, by the `*.env`
  # arm. The quoted string is also what the size
  # read was given, and it names nothing on disk, so `ignoredBytes`
  # under-reported precisely the entries that matter — and the human, whose
  # reading of a filename this whole design rests on, was shown
  # `"s\303\251crets/"`.
  #
  # MUTATION SURVIVOR, disclosed: `-c core.quotePath=false` is a stated NO-OP
  # here and cannot be pinned. Measured on git 2.43 in both directions: with
  # `-z` the output is verbatim whether that config is false, true or unset, and
  # WITHOUT `-z` the config unquotes the non-ASCII byte and still quotes the
  # space — so it fixes nothing on its own and changes nothing beside `-z`. It
  # is passed so the line says what it is for; `-z` is what does the work, and
  # `reads the path git C-QUOTES` is what kills its removal.
  #
  # `-z` needs a FILE rather than `$(…)`: command substitution drops NUL bytes,
  # so the separator would vanish and every entry run together.
  #
  # What `-z` gives it also takes back, and the record shape is the answer: git
  # is no longer escaping a TAB or a NEWLINE inside a path either, so
  # `path\tbytes\tsensitive` read left to right shifts its fields on
  # `a<TAB>b.log` and `cmd_ws_audit` prints `"bytes":b.log`, which is not JSON.
  # Hence `sensitive\tbytes\tpath`: the two fixed-shape fields first — one of
  # `0|1`, one of `[0-9]+`, neither able to contain a tab — and the free-form
  # one last, so the path keeps whatever bytes it has.
  #
  # `du -sb` rather than `_ws_gc_bytes`, which answers `-` for anything that is
  # not a DIRECTORY (its own contract, and right for the workspace totals it was
  # written for): every ignored FILE was therefore recorded as 0 bytes, so a
  # 400 MB `dump.sql` was listed as free. `$wd` is absolute, so no `--` guard is
  # needed against a leading dash — but `head -n1` IS needed, because du echoes
  # the path back beside the size and a path with a newline in it makes that two
  # lines (measured: `cut -f1` alone returned `1\nd.log`, which fails the
  # numeric test and silently became 0).
  #
  # THREE MORE MUTATION SURVIVORS, disclosed with the reason each is one, and
  # two of them are the same reason — an empty temp-file name is itself a
  # failing redirect, so the read never runs and the NEXT guard refuses:
  #   - `outf=$(mktemp) || return 1` — removable with the suite green: `>""` is
  #     an invalid redirect, git never runs, and `(( rc == 0 ))` refuses.
  #   - the `|| { rm -f "$outf"; return 1; }` on the `errf` line — removable for
  #     the same reason PLUS one more: `2>""` fails the read, so control reaches
  #     `(( rc == 0 )) || { rm -f "$outf"; …` one line later, which unlinks the
  #     same file. Measured, not assumed: a test was written for it and the
  #     mutant was re-swept and still SURVIVED. The OTHER THREE `rm -f "$outf"`
  #     — the exit-code one, the stderr one and the one after the loop — are
  #     each pinned individually by `removes its scratch file on EVERY path that
  #     refuses`, which walks all four exits, because with any single one
  #     deleted a fixture for a DIFFERENT failure still cleans up and one case
  #     pins nothing.
  #     Both stay for the reason `_gh_repo_slug`'s first two guards stay: each
  #     states the case it is about rather than relying on a later line, and the
  #     fall-through only holds while that later line keeps its `rm`.
  #   - `[[ -n "$p" ]] || continue` — git never emits a bare `!! `, so `p` cannot
  #     be empty after the prefix strip and no fixture can make it so. Kept
  #     because the loop's other two lines both dereference `$p` into a
  #     filesystem path, and an empty one would size `$wd/` — the whole
  #     workspace — as an "ignored entry".
  local wd="$1" entry p b sens deadline outf errf err rc ih
  REAP_IGNORED=(); REAP_SENSITIVE=(); REAP_IGNDIGEST=""; REAP_IGNREASON=""
  REAP_SENSITIVE_FILTERED=0
  deadline=$(( SECONDS + REAP_SCAN_SECONDS ))
  outf=$(mktemp) || return 1
  errf=$(mktemp) || { rm -f "$outf"; return 1; }
  git -C "$wd" -c core.quotePath=false status --porcelain --ignored=matching -z \
    >"$outf" 2>"$errf"; rc=$?
  err=$(cat "$errf" 2>/dev/null); rm -f "$errf"
  (( rc == 0 )) || { rm -f "$outf"; return 1; }
  [[ -z "$err" ]] || { rm -f "$outf"; return 1; }
  while IFS= read -r -d '' entry; do
    case "$entry" in '!! '*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
    p="${entry#!! }"
    [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
    b=$(du -sb "$wd/$p" 2>/dev/null | head -n1 | cut -f1); [[ "$b" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || b=0
    sens=0
    if _ws_sensitive_match "$p"; then
      # NOISE is counted, not silenced: `_ws_sensitive_noise` is the F3
      # refinement (see its own comment) and every name it drops still moves
      # `REAP_SENSITIVE_FILTERED`, so "excluded" never means "invisible".
      if _ws_sensitive_noise "$p"; then
        REAP_SENSITIVE_FILTERED=$(( REAP_SENSITIVE_FILTERED + 1 ))
      else
        sens=1; REAP_SENSITIVE+=("$p")
      fi
    fi
    # AND THE ENTRY IS OPENED WHEN IT IS A DIRECTORY. A hit anywhere inside
    # makes the ENTRY sensitive — the entry is what the sheet lists and what
    # `rm -rf` destroys — while REAP_SENSITIVE records the PATH THAT WAS FOUND,
    # because "move `build/.env` somewhere else" is a remedy and "build/ is
    # sensitive" is not. The sensitivity of the entry and the paths reported are
    # therefore two different facts and both are kept.
    if [[ -d "$wd/$p" ]]; then
      _ws_sensitive_inside "$wd/$p" "$p" "$deadline" || { rm -f "$outf"; return 1; }
      # Same per-hit noise filter as the top-level match just above, applied
      # to each path the inside-scan found individually — one collapsed
      # directory can hold both a generated `.js.map` (noise) and a real
      # `.env` (not), and the entry must read sensitive on the second alone.
      for ih in "${_WS_INSIDE_HITS[@]}"; do
        if _ws_sensitive_noise "$ih"; then
          REAP_SENSITIVE_FILTERED=$(( REAP_SENSITIVE_FILTERED + 1 ))
        else
          sens=1; REAP_SENSITIVE+=("$ih")
        fi
      done
    fi
    REAP_IGNORED+=("$sens"$'\t'"$b"$'\t'"$p")
  done <"$outf"
  rm -f "$outf"
  # THE DIGEST IS OVER THE RECORDS, not over the paths — which is a change of
  # WHAT the token promises, and it was made because the old promise was empty.
  # `_ws_ignored_digest` hashes `status --ignored=matching`'s lines, i.e. the
  # SET OF PATHS, so measured: growing an ignored `build/out.o` from 9 bytes to
  # 400,000 left the token IDENTICAL and the reap deleted 400,215 bytes where
  # the sheet said 9; adding a whole file inside an already-listed ignored
  # directory did the same; so did dropping a nested git repository with its own
  # commits into one (27,141 bytes, reaped silently). The records already carry
  # `sensitive\tbytes\tpath`, so hashing THEM makes the size and the
  # inside-the-directory sensitivity above both move the token, and the consent
  # check refuses `state-changed` for each.
  #
  # `sort -z`, because a digest is over a SET and git's enumeration order is not
  # promised; NUL-separated, because a path may hold a TAB or a NEWLINE and the
  # records are built to survive that. The empty case hashes the empty input
  # rather than one blank line, so "nothing ignored" and "one entry called
  # nothing" cannot collide.
  #
  # A FAILED HASH IS STILL NOT AN EMPTY ONE (deviation 6): the shape check is
  # what keeps `sha256sum` failing from putting "" into the field on BOTH sides,
  # where the fingerprints then match and D2's consent check passes over a
  # measurement nobody made.
  #   MUTATION SURVIVOR, disclosed: the `printf ''` that feeds an EMPTY set can
  #   be written `printf '\n'` with the suite green, and always will be. The
  #   comment above reasons about "nothing ignored" colliding with "one entry
  #   called nothing", but that second state is unconstructible — the collector's
  #   `[[ -n "$p" ]] || continue` refuses an empty path and every record carries
  #   `sensitive\tbytes\t` before it. Unpinnable by construction, like the
  #   sensitive-digest `sort` two blocks down. (Gate finding N3.) `_ws_ignored_digest` keeps its own copy of that
  # rung because the ARCHIVE manifest still calls it, and archive records what
  # reap refuses over.
  # MUTATION SURVIVOR, disclosed: the `sort -z` can be deleted with the whole
  # suite green, because git enumerates the ignored set in a stable order for a
  # given tree and both sides of the consent check call this same function, so
  # no fixture can make the two orders differ. It stays because a digest is over
  # a SET, and git's order is not promised — the day it changes for a reason
  # (a config, a version, a filesystem readdir order) the token would move under
  # a workspace nobody touched, which is `state-changed` for no reason at all.
  # The same argument the sensitive digest's `sort` carries at ccd's Phase D1.
  if (( ${#REAP_IGNORED[@]} )); then
    REAP_IGNDIGEST=$(printf '%s\0' "${REAP_IGNORED[@]}" | sort -z | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)
  else
    REAP_IGNDIGEST=$(printf '' | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)
  fi
  [[ "$REAP_IGNDIGEST" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || { REAP_IGNDIGEST=""; return 1; }
}

_ws_merge_proof() {   # main M tip -> 0, with the passing rung in _WS_PROOF
  local main="$1" M="$2" tip="$3" Pm mb a b cout
  _WS_PROOF=""
  # ancestor — a true merge commit contains our tip.
  git -C "$main" merge-base --is-ancestor -- "$tip" "$M" 2>/dev/null && { _WS_PROOF=ancestor; return 0; }
  # tree — a squash whose base did not move. `--` AFTER the revisions is a
  # CORRECTNESS requirement: `diff --quiet -- A B` makes the shas pathspecs and
  # exits 0 for any pair (verified).
  git -C "$main" diff --quiet "$M" "$tip" -- 2>/dev/null && { _WS_PROOF=tree; return 0; }
  # patch-id — a squash whose base DID move, i.e. the majority case on a busy
  # repo. Whole-branch diff, NOT git cherry: cherry compares per-commit
  # patch-ids and reports + for every commit of a multi-commit squash.
  #
  # TWO MUTATION SURVIVORS, disclosed: `[[ -n "$Pm" ]]` and `[[ -n "$mb" ]]` are
  # each removable with the suite green, and they are removable because the
  # `-n "$a"` below is the backstop that IS pinned. `Pm` is empty only for a
  # merge commit with no parent (a root commit as `M`), and `mb` only for
  # histories with no common ancestor; in both cases the `git diff` that follows
  # gets an empty revision operand, fails, and leaves `a` empty — which
  # `never proves patch-id from two EMPTY patch-ids` refuses. They stay because
  # each names the case it is about, and because a diff against `""` is a git
  # invocation nobody should be relying on the shape of.
  Pm=$(git -C "$main" rev-parse --verify "${M}^1" 2>/dev/null) || Pm=""
  if [[ -n "$Pm" ]]; then
    mb=$(git -C "$main" merge-base -- "$tip" "$Pm" 2>/dev/null) || mb=""
    if [[ -n "$mb" ]]; then
      a=$(git -C "$main" diff --binary "$mb" "$tip" -- 2>/dev/null | git -C "$main" patch-id --stable | cut -d' ' -f1)
      b=$(git -C "$main" diff --binary "$Pm" "$M"   -- 2>/dev/null | git -C "$main" patch-id --stable | cut -d' ' -f1)
      [[ -n "$a" && "$a" == "$b" ]] && { _WS_PROOF=patch-id; return 0; }
    fi
  fi
  # cherry — the rebase-merge rung. Requires cherry to SUCCEED: swallowing its
  # exit code and testing an empty string would pass every broken invocation.
  if cout=$(git -C "$main" cherry "$M" "$tip" 2>/dev/null); then
    grep -q '^+' <<< "$cout" || { _WS_PROOF=cherry; return 0; }
  fi
  return 1
}

_ws_fingerprint() {   # id branch tip headOid mergeOid proof dirty igndigest sensdigest stashes wthead baseOid clipsDigest
  # THIRTEEN facts, and the thirteenth is the clips. `~/.cc-clips/<id>` is
  # `rm -rf`'d at (h) — 3.8 MB full-resolution screenshots per the spec — and
  # until this argument existed the fingerprint could not see it at all:
  # measured, pasting two clips between the sheet rendering and the tap left the
  # token IDENTICAL (`0e38d4d1…7ccd` before and after) and the reap deleted
  # them. A change to WHAT GETS DELETED that no human consented to in any form
  # is the one thing D2 exists to refuse, so the manifest is now both on the
  # wire (`cmd_ws_audit`'s `clips`) and in the token.
  printf '%s\n' "id=$1" "branch=$2" "tip=$3" "headRefOid=$4" "mergeCommit=$5" "proof=$6" \
    "dirtyCount=$7" "ignoredDigest=$8" "sensitiveDigest=$9" "stashCount=${10}" \
    "worktreeHead=${11}" "baseOid=${12}" "clipsDigest=${13}" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1
}

_ws_reap_reset() {
  REAP_VERDICT=""; REAP_DETAIL=""; REAP_PROOF=""; REAP_TOKEN=""
  REAP_TIP=""; REAP_HEADOID=""; REAP_MERGE=""; REAP_BASEOID=""; REAP_WTHEAD=""
  REAP_DIRTY=0; REAP_STASHES=0; REAP_IGNDIGEST=""; REAP_SENSDIGEST=""; REAP_IGNREASON=""
  REAP_CLIPDIGEST=""
  REAP_PRNUM=""; REAP_PRURL=""; REAP_FETCHED=0
  REAP_IGNORED=(); REAP_SENSITIVE=(); REAP_SENSITIVE_FILTERED=0; _WS_INSIDE_HITS=()
}

# MUTATION SURVIVOR, disclosed: the `return 1` is removable with the suite
# green, because every call site in `_ws_reap_eval` is `… ; return 1` and none
# of them reads this function's status. It stays so that a site CAN be written
# `_reap_refuse … || return` — and so that the function's contract is "this
# refuses", not "this assigns two variables".
_reap_refuse() { REAP_VERDICT="$1"; REAP_DETAIL="$2"; return 1; }

_ws_reap_eval() {   # id -> 0 when reapable, else REAP_VERDICT names the refusal
  _ws_reap_reset
  local id="$1" ws project workdir branch base baseShort main wthead common mainreal
  local st up ahead repo rows row registered errf err rc stashall dirt

  # ── Phase A: identity ────────────────────────────────────────────
  [[ -f "$REG/$id.uuid" ]] || { _reap_refuse no-such-session "no registry entry for $id"; return 1; }
  ws=$(_reg_get "$id" workspace)
  [[ -n "$ws" ]] || { _reap_refuse not-a-workspace "$id is a main checkout"; return 1; }
  [[ -f "$REG/$id.archived" ]] \
    || { _reap_refuse not-archived "archive first — that is the staging"; return 1; }
  # Registry FIRST, git's record second — and "second" is a veto, not a
  # fallback. This used to read "the reverse of ws-rm, which reads only the
  # worktree" — no longer true: ws-rm reads its branch from git's worktree
  # record too (_ws_wt_branch, ccd:706-717), which survives the directory being
  # hand-deleted, so the specific mechanism that made ws/swift-harbor an orphan
  # invisible to ccd ls, the PWA and ws-gc alike is fixed there. Reap still
  # reads the registry first, for its own reasons: it needs `base` and `project`
  # too, and it must be able to REFUSE for want of a name
  # (incomplete-registry) rather than proceed with a partial one. What it does
  # NOT do is trust that name — the same _ws_wt_branch has to corroborate it
  # below, and after that the two are equal by construction, so which one the
  # rest of this function operates on is no longer a question anyone can get
  # wrong.
  project=$(_reg_get "$id" project); workdir=$(_reg_get "$id" workdir); branch=$(_reg_get "$id" branch)
  base=$(_reg_get "$id" base); [[ -n "$base" ]] || base="origin/HEAD"
  baseShort="${base#origin/}"
  [[ -n "$project" && -n "$workdir" && -n "$branch" ]] \
    || { _reap_refuse incomplete-registry "project='$project' workdir='$workdir' branch='$branch'"; return 1; }
  main="$PROJECTS_ROOT/$project"
  if [[ ! -d "$workdir" ]]; then
    # A missing worktree is a refusal when the USER removed it and a resume
    # when WE did. The breadcrumb is what tells the two apart.
    [[ -f "$REG/$id.reaping" ]] \
      || { _reap_refuse worktree-missing "$workdir is gone"; return 1; }
  fi

  if [[ -d "$workdir" ]]; then
    # THE branch question, asked of $main and of nothing else. `_ws_wt_branch`
    # (ccd:706-717) reads `git -C "$main" worktree list --porcelain`, so the
    # answer is $main's own registration for this path; it cannot leave $main, it
    # survives the directory being gone, and it follows a rename whether ccd or
    # the user did it. NOT `git -C "$workdir" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`, which
    # the spec's A6/A7 spell and an earlier draft of this plan used: that answers
    # from whatever repository owns that DIRECTORY, and after a hand-deletion and
    # a stray `git init` that need not be $main at all. Measured on git 2.43: a
    # stranger `git init`ed at the workdir with one commit on `attacker/main`
    # makes the directory read answer `attacker/main` while $main's record still
    # says `ws/quiet-basin`. Reap does not delete the name it reads here — it
    # deletes the registry's, by CAS, in _ws_reap_tail — but the verdict it
    # reaches and the names it prints would both have been decided by a
    # stranger's HEAD, and the file now has ONE rule instead of two: git's
    # worktree record is the authority, in ws-rm and here alike.
    #
    # TWO statements, deliberately, exactly as cmd_ws_rm writes it (ccd:733-734):
    # `local x=$(cmd)` returns LOCAL's status, so a one-line form would read $?
    # from the declaration and `registered` would be 0 for every path, registered
    # or not — turning the no-record rung below into dead code. `wthead` is
    # declared with the other locals at the top of this function for that reason.
    wthead=$(_ws_wt_branch "$main" "$workdir"); registered=$?
    # The three rungs cmd_ws_rm walks (ccd:783, :793, :805), in refusal form,
    # outermost first.
    #
    # Rung 3 — exit 1: $main holds NO registration for this path. Nothing here is
    # $main's to remove and no name is corroborated, which is the reading that
    # deletes nothing. It gets its own token rather than being folded into
    # `foreign-worktree`: a hand-deleted or hand-pruned admin directory is not
    # "a different repository", and telling someone their worktree belongs to
    # another repo when it belongs to none would be false. Measured on git 2.43:
    # `rm -rf $main/.git/worktrees/<slug>` leaves the directory and the branch
    # both intact while every read of the directory fails `not a git repository`
    # — the state the old `rev-parse` form reported as `detached-head`, about a
    # HEAD it had not managed to read.
    (( registered == 0 )) \
      || { _reap_refuse no-worktree-record "$main has no worktree record for $workdir"; return 1; }
    # Rung 2 — registered, and the record says detached. `_ws_wt_branch` reports
    # this as empty-with-exit-0, which is why emptiness alone cannot stand in for
    # both rungs. Unlike the old form this can no longer fire because a read
    # failed: it fires only when git positively recorded a detached HEAD.
    [[ -n "$wthead" ]] \
      || { _reap_refuse detached-head "$main records $workdir on a detached HEAD"; return 1; }
    # Rung 1 — registered, on a branch, and it has to be the branch the registry
    # names. Both sides of this comparison are now RECORDS — ccrc's registry and
    # git's registration — which is what the token is named for. ws-rm can let
    # git win and merely note the divergence (ccd:787-788) because it deletes
    # whatever git had checked out there; reap cannot, because the registry's
    # name is what its stash count, its upstream check, its tip, its PR bind and
    # its CAS delete are all built from. So a disagreement here is never
    # resolved, it is refused, and both names are printed as §6 requires.
    [[ "$wthead" == "$branch" ]] \
      || { _reap_refuse registry-branch-drift "the registry says $branch, git's worktree record for $workdir says $wthead"; return 1; }
    # STILL REQUIRED — and now for a different reason, which is why it is worth
    # saying out loud rather than leaving in place by inertia. It used to sit
    # immediately after the branch read in order to CONTAIN a name that might
    # have come from another repository; with `_ws_wt_branch` no name can, so
    # containment is no longer its job and the ordering above no longer turns on
    # it. What is left is the DIRECTORY, and that is not the weaker reason — it
    # is ccd's own (ccd:737-752). Everything below this line reads or destroys
    # `$workdir`: Phase B asks it for `status --porcelain` and for its ignored
    # set, so a stranger's clean tree would certify OUR workspace as safe to
    # delete; and `_ws_reap_tail` hands the same path to `git worktree remove`,
    # which in ws-rm killed the session and disabled the unit BEFORE git got
    # round to refusing. `registered` cannot decide it either — the record
    # outlives the directory, and measured on git 2.43 a `git init` at that path
    # leaves the record reading healthy with no `prunable` marker, because the
    # record's gitdir file now points at the stranger's own `.git`. Hence: both
    # sides must say $main, and this must run BEFORE Phase B rather than merely
    # somewhere after the branch read.
    #
    # `_ws_common_dir` (ccd:687-692), never a `cd` inside a command substitution.
    # An earlier draft of this plan wrote the cd form; `ccrc/ws-rm-fix` deleted
    # exactly that pattern from cmd_ws_add and cmd_ws_rm and documented why at
    # _ws_common_dir, so writing it back here would reintroduce a bug main has
    # already fixed. The reason, restated because it decides an irreversible
    # refusal: ccd does not control the stdout of a captured `cd`. Plain
    # `--git-common-dir` prints a bare `.git` from a repo's own checkout, so the
    # cd form is load-bearing rather than cosmetic — and bash's own cd prints the
    # directory it landed on when a relative operand hits CDPATH, while a `cd`
    # exported as a shell function (bash imports those from the environment)
    # prints whatever it likes. `2>/dev/null` catches neither. Both sides then
    # compare multi-line garbage: two wrong answers that happen to match wave a
    # squatter through, two that differ refuse a healthy workspace.
    # Empty is NO ANSWER, never a match — the helper's own contract — so both
    # sides are required non-empty before the comparison means anything.
    #
    # MUTATION SURVIVOR, disclosed: replacing the FIRST call with the banned
    # `cd "$workdir" && git rev-parse --git-common-dir` form leaves the suite
    # green, and the reason is worth knowing rather than papering over. `$workdir`
    # is absolute, so CDPATH cannot fire on it, and from a LINKED worktree
    # `--git-common-dir` already answers absolutely — so on this side the two
    # forms agree. The form is banned for the OTHER side: from a repository's own
    # checkout plain `--git-common-dir` prints a bare `.git`, and `$main` is
    # exactly that. `_ws_common_dir` (ccd:687-692) is where that is pinned, and
    # it is called here rather than reimplemented so there is one answer to
    # break.
    common=$(_ws_common_dir "$workdir") || common=""
    mainreal=$(_ws_common_dir "$main")  || mainreal=""
    [[ -n "$common" && -n "$mainreal" && "$common" == "$mainreal" ]] \
      || { _reap_refuse foreign-worktree "$workdir belongs to ${common:-no repository}, not ${mainreal:-no repository}"; return 1; }
    # Still called WTHEAD, still fingerprinted as `worktreeHead=`, still on the
    # wire as `headMatchesRegistry`, all deliberately unrenamed: `worktree list
    # --porcelain` reports each worktree's HEAD (git reads it out of
    # `$GIT_DIR/worktrees/<slug>/HEAD`), so the VALUE is the same fact it always
    # was. Only the repository the question is put to changed. One thing about
    # the value did change and is worth knowing while reading the fingerprint: a
    # detached worktree now yields "" where `rev-parse` yielded the literal
    # `HEAD` — unobservable, because rung 2 refuses before this line.
    #
    # MUTATION SURVIVOR, disclosed: writing `REAP_WTHEAD="$branch"` here leaves
    # the suite green, and always will — rung 1 above refuses unless
    # `wthead == branch`, so on this line the two are equal BY CONSTRUCTION. It
    # is written from `wthead` because the field means "what git's record says",
    # and the day that rung moves or softens, the fingerprint must follow git
    # rather than quietly follow the registry.
    REAP_WTHEAD="$wthead"

    # ── Phase B: nothing local is lost ─────────────────────────────
    # TWO statements, and the pipeline's status is not the read's. `status
    # --porcelain | grep -c .` counts ZERO lines for a tree nobody could read, so
    # the one-line form passes the `dirty-tree` guard on an unreadable worktree —
    # the same defect the archive manifest shipped and deviation 6 closed there
    # (`_ws_gc_dirty` states the rule for the file: a status we could not read is
    # not a clean one). An index.lock contention or a permission change mid-flight
    # is enough, and this guard is one §5.3 forbids overriding.
    #
    # And the exit code is only HALF of "could not read", which is why stderr is
    # captured rather than discarded. A PARTIALLY unreadable tree exits 0:
    # measured on git 2.43, `chmod 000` on an untracked subdirectory holding
    # uncommitted work gives rc 0, EMPTY stdout, and `warning: could not open
    # directory 'sub/'` on stderr. The count is then 0, `dirty-tree` passes, and
    # the audit hands out a token certifying a clean tree over work it never
    # saw. Same rule as the ignored set in `_ws_collect_ignored`, and for the
    # same reason: these two are the guards §5.3/§7 allow no override for, so
    # "some of the tree" is not an answer either of them may act on. The test is
    # for the DIAGNOSTIC and not its wording — git translates warnings and ccd
    # pins no locale.
    #
    # SAID OUT LOUD, because the polarity is chosen and not free: ANY diagnostic
    # refuses, so one benign `warning:` — a stale index extension, a
    # `core.fsmonitor` complaint, an advice line a future git decides to print —
    # makes this workspace un-reapable, permanently, with no override anywhere.
    # That is the correct direction (the alternative is a wording allowlist that
    # a translated warning walks straight through), and the cost is that the
    # remedy is to fix the warning, not to press through it. `ws-archive`, which
    # runs unattended, is deliberately NOT built this way — it records what it
    # cannot describe rather than refusing forever.
    #
    # `dirt` and `REAP_DIRTY` are two names because they are two types: the raw
    # status text is not the count, and one variable holding both in turn is how
    # a later reader ends up printing porcelain into a sentence that says
    # "file(s)".
    # MUTATION SURVIVOR, disclosed: this line's `|| { _reap_refuse … }` is
    # removable with the suite green, for the same reason as the two in
    # `_ws_collect_ignored` — an empty `errf` makes `2>""` a failing redirect, the
    # status read never runs, and the `(( rc == 0 ))` two lines down refuses with
    # the same token. Unlike those two there is no file to leak here, so nothing
    # observable is left to pin. It states the case rather than relying on a
    # later line to catch it.
    errf=$(mktemp) || { _reap_refuse tree-unreadable "could not read the tree at $workdir"; return 1; }
    dirt=$(git -C "$workdir" status --porcelain 2>"$errf"); rc=$?
    err=$(cat "$errf" 2>/dev/null); rm -f "$errf"
    (( rc == 0 )) && [[ -z "$err" ]] \
      || { _reap_refuse tree-unreadable "could not read the tree at $workdir"; return 1; }
    REAP_DIRTY=$(printf '%s' "$dirt" | grep -c . || true)
    (( REAP_DIRTY == 0 )) \
      || { _reap_refuse dirty-tree "$REAP_DIRTY uncommitted or untracked file(s)"; return 1; }
    _ws_collect_ignored "$workdir" \
      || { _reap_refuse tree-unreadable "could not read the ignored set at $workdir${REAP_IGNREASON:+ — $REAP_IGNREASON}"; return 1; }
    (( ${#REAP_SENSITIVE[@]} == 0 )) \
      || { _reap_refuse sensitive-ignored "${REAP_SENSITIVE[*]}"; return 1; }
  fi

  # THE STASH READ THAT CANNOT FAIL SILENTLY — corroborated here rather than
  # widened in `_ws_stash_count`, whose `2>/dev/null … || true` is Task 2's
  # deliberate contract and which Task 4 consumes.
  #
  # Every failure of that helper is a 0, and a 0 is what authorises the delete.
  # Neither of the two techniques already in this file can see it: measured on
  # git 2.43, with `.git/logs/refs/stash` unreadable OR deleted while
  # `refs/stash` still resolves, `git stash list` returns rc 0, EMPTY stdout and
  # EMPTY stderr — so the exit code says fine and Phase B's stderr rule has
  # nothing to test. The failure is deterministic, so ws-reap recomputes the
  # same 0 and the `--expect` consent check matches. That is deviation 6's
  # digest forgery in the `stashCount` field: a deletion authorised over stashes
  # nobody counted.
  #
  # What CAN see it is the ref, and the invariant is ONE-WAY — not the
  # biconditional this comment used to claim. Measured across push/pop/drop/clear
  # on git 2.43, one half IS a law git keeps: at least one entry ⇒ `refs/stash`
  # resolves, because git creates the ref on the first push and deletes it when
  # the last entry goes. The CONVERSE is not, and the converse is what this guard
  # rests on: `git reflog expire --all --expire=now --expire-unreachable=now` — a
  # documented maintenance command that does not mention refs/stash — empties the
  # stash reflog and LEAVES THE REF, so it resolves (rc 0) beside a `git stash
  # list` that returns rc 0 and zero entries. Measured on git 2.43.
  # (`git gc --prune=now` does not reach it, nor does gc with
  # `gc.reflogExpire=now` — git protects refs/stash from gc by default, measured
  # too. The trigger is narrow. It is not impossible.)
  #
  # So the guard has a FALSE-POSITIVE STATE and it is DISCLOSED rather than
  # engineered away: from here the two are indistinguishable, and the only safe
  # reading of "I cannot tell" is to refuse. What that costs is said out loud —
  # a repository in that state answers `stash-unreadable` PERMANENTLY, for every
  # workspace in it, with no override, and since this runs before the `exists`
  # branch it blocks the `reap-interrupted` resume path too. Which is why the
  # REMEDY travels in the refusal detail rather than in this comment: the
  # operator the message reaches is the only one who can act, and neither
  # 'git stash clear' nor 'git update-ref -d refs/stash' is something they will
  # guess. Both measured against the reflog-expire fixture, in the test that
  # names it.
  #
  # What the guard must NOT do is read "refs/stash exists" as "this branch has
  # stashes". A stash on another branch is a legitimate, reapable state (also
  # measured: a stash pushed from $main's own checkout leaves this branch's
  # count at an honest 0), and refusing it would make every workspace in a repo
  # whose main holds one stash permanently un-reapable, with no override. So the
  # corroboration is on the WHOLE list and the branch-scoped count stays
  # `_ws_stash_count`'s.
  if git -C "$main" rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/stash >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    stashall=$(git -C "$main" stash list 2>/dev/null | grep -c .)
    (( stashall > 0 )) \
      || { _reap_refuse stash-unreadable "refs/stash resolves in $main but the stash list read back empty — either its reflog cannot be read, or maintenance ('git reflog expire --all') emptied it and left the ref: if this repository truly holds no stashes, 'git stash clear' (or 'git update-ref -d refs/stash') clears the stale ref"; return 1; }
  fi
  REAP_STASHES=$(_ws_stash_count "$main" "$branch")
  (( REAP_STASHES == 0 )) \
    || { _reap_refuse stashes-present "$REAP_STASHES stash entr$( (( REAP_STASHES == 1 )) && echo y || echo ies) on $branch"; return 1; }
  up=$(git -C "$main" rev-parse --verify --quiet "$branch@{upstream}" 2>/dev/null) \
    || { _reap_refuse no-upstream "$branch was never pushed"; return 1; }
  ahead=$(git -C "$main" rev-list --count "$up..refs/heads/$branch" 2>/dev/null)
  [[ "$ahead" == 0 ]] \
    || { _reap_refuse unpushed-commits "$ahead commit(s) are not on the remote"; return 1; }

  # ── Phase C: the work is genuinely in main ─────────────────────
  REAP_TIP=$(git -C "$main" rev-parse --verify "refs/heads/$branch" 2>/dev/null) \
    || { _reap_refuse branch-missing "refs/heads/$branch does not resolve"; return 1; }
  repo=$(_gh_repo_slug "$main") || { _reap_refuse no-remote "no origin remote for $project"; return 1; }
  rows=$(_gh_pr_list "$repo")   || { _reap_refuse gh-unreadable "$rows"; return 1; }
  row=$(printf '%s' "$rows" | _pr_py pick "$main" "$branch" "$baseShort" "$REAP_TIP")
  case "$row" in
    '')                   _reap_refuse no-bound-pr "no merged PR binds to $branch"; return 1 ;;
    '!pr-head-not-ours')  _reap_refuse pr-head-not-ours "the PR head commit is not reachable from $branch"; return 1 ;;
    '!'*)                 _reap_refuse "${row#!}" "the bound PR is not merged"; return 1 ;;
  esac
  IFS=$'\t' read -r REAP_PRNUM REAP_PRURL REAP_MERGE REAP_HEADOID <<< "$row"
  # §7's argv boundary, restated on THIS side of the split — because the split
  # is what can move a value out of the field that was anchored and into one
  # that was not. `_pr_py pick` checks `mergeCommit.oid` and `headRefOid`
  # against `OID` (ccd:292) inside python, but `url` and `number` are
  # GitHub-sourced and unanchored, and all four come back joined with tabs. So a
  # PR whose `url` holds a TAB shifts every later field: measured with
  # `url: "https://x/\tinjected"`, the string `injected` became REAP_MERGE and
  # reached `git cat-file -e "injected^{commit}"`, `git merge-base --is-ancestor
  # -- "$tip" "injected"` and `git diff --stat "injected" …`. It failed closed
  # there, but by luck rather than by construction, and one anchored test is
  # what turns the one into the other. Same regex as python's, deliberately:
  # a floor of 7 because a 3-character hex string like `abc` can be a real ref,
  # and both ends anchored because `headRefOid: "main"` otherwise resolves as a
  # REVISION and binds.
  #
  # ALL SIX PIECES ARE PINNED — the two anchors on each oid, the floor and the
  # ceiling — and the route that reaches them is a fixture that shadows
  # `_pr_py pick` and hands this line one crafted row at a time. That is not a
  # contrivance; it is the case the line is FOR. While the two ends are one
  # producer, python's `OID` screens both oids before they are joined and the
  # tab-shift above always leaves a literal TAB in the tail field, so the
  # character class alone answers everything and NOTHING beneath it is
  # observable. Measured, and the reason this comment is a correction: the
  # previous one claimed "the character class and the anchors are what is
  # pinned" and disclosed the floor as the sole survivor. Re-swept, EIGHT
  # mutants of this one line survived — dropping either conjunct, dropping
  # either `^`, dropping either `$`, `{1,40}`, and `{7,}`. With `^` gone,
  # `origin/deadbeef1` matches on its nine-hex tail and reaches
  # `git cat-file -e "origin/deadbeef1^{commit}"`, `merge-base --is-ancestor`
  # and `diff --stat`: the exact "resolves as a REVISION and binds" case the
  # two lines above say the anchors exist to stop. bash's `=~` searches unless
  # anchored, which is why each anchor needs its own fixture rather than
  # inheriting one from its neighbour.
  [[ "$REAP_MERGE" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$ && "$REAP_HEADOID" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$ ]] \
    || { _reap_refuse pr-fields-malformed "gh named mergeCommit='$REAP_MERGE' headRefOid='$REAP_HEADOID'"; return 1; }

  # Mergedness is NEVER proven against an unfetched ref. Six repos on this box
  # have never been fetched; one is 24 days stale.
  timeout 60 git -C "$main" fetch --quiet origin \
    || { _reap_refuse fetch-failed "could not fetch origin — nothing is claimed about your commits"; return 1; }
  REAP_FETCHED=$(date +%s)
  git -C "$main" cat-file -e "${REAP_MERGE}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null \
    || { _reap_refuse merge-commit-missing "$REAP_MERGE is not in the object store after a fetch"; return 1; }
  # A REFUSAL, not a default. This was the last fingerprint input that answered
  # a failed read with `""`: measured, with only this read failing the verdict
  # stayed `reapable` and a token was issued over a field nobody measured — and
  # because the failure is deterministic, ws-reap recomputes the same `""` and
  # the `--expect` consent check matches. Same class as the ignored digest
  # (deviation 6) and the stash count above. `$base` is the registry's, so this
  # fires for a workspace whose base ref was deleted or renamed under it, which
  # is a state to reconcile rather than one to delete over.
  REAP_BASEOID=$(git -C "$main" rev-parse --verify "$base" 2>/dev/null) \
    || { _reap_refuse base-missing "$base does not resolve in $main"; return 1; }
  if _ws_merge_proof "$main" "$REAP_MERGE" "$REAP_TIP"; then
    REAP_PROOF="$_WS_PROOF"
  else
    _reap_refuse tree-differs "$(git -C "$main" diff --stat "$REAP_MERGE" "$REAP_TIP" -- | head -5; git -C "$main" log --oneline "$REAP_MERGE".."$REAP_TIP" | head -5)"
    return 1
  fi

  # ── Phase D1: the session ──────────────────────────────────────
  st=$(_ws_status "$id") || { _reap_refuse status-unknown "cannot read the wrapper status file"; return 1; }
  [[ "$st" != busy ]] || { _reap_refuse session-busy "the session is working — a model turn, a Bash tool command, or a status this ccd does not recognise"; return 1; }

  # MUTATION SURVIVOR, disclosed and unpinnable BY CONSTRUCTION: the `sort` can
  # be deleted with the suite green, because every state that reaches this line
  # has an EMPTY sensitive set — a non-empty one refuses `sensitive-ignored`
  # above, with no override — so the digest is the constant sha256 of one blank
  # line. It stays because the field is a set digest and a set has no order,
  # and because the ordering `_ws_collect_ignored` produces is git's, which is
  # not promised. The only way to pin it would be a state this design forbids.
  REAP_SENSDIGEST=$(printf '%s\n' "${REAP_SENSITIVE[@]-}" | sort | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)
  # The clips manifest is `_ws_clip_manifest`'s, the same producer the TOMBSTONE
  # records at (a), so the record of what was deleted and the consent to delete
  # it cannot describe different files. Hashed rather than carried, because the
  # fingerprint is a line-per-fact document and a manifest holds newlines.
  REAP_CLIPDIGEST=$(_ws_clip_manifest "$id" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)
  REAP_TOKEN=$(_ws_fingerprint "$id" "$branch" "$REAP_TIP" "$REAP_HEADOID" "$REAP_MERGE" "$REAP_PROOF" \
                 "$REAP_DIRTY" "$REAP_IGNDIGEST" "$REAP_SENSDIGEST" "$REAP_STASHES" "$REAP_WTHEAD" \
                 "$REAP_BASEOID" "$REAP_CLIPDIGEST")
  REAP_VERDICT=reapable
  return 0
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Add `cmd_ws_audit`**

Insert after `_ws_reap_eval`:

```bash
cmd_ws_audit() {   # ccd ws-audit --session <id> — read-only; the token's source
  [[ $# -eq 2 && $1 == --session ]] || die "usage: ccd ws-audit --session <id>"
  local id=$2
  [[ $id =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || die "bad session id"

  # `_json_str`'s status, checked ONCE and up front — the same probe, for the
  # same reason, as `_ws_manifest` (ccd:1109). Nineteen `_json_str` substitutions
  # below sit inside printf ARGUMENT LISTS, where a failure is a swallowed status
  # and an empty argument, i.e. `"path":,` — a document that authorises deletions
  # and does not parse, at exit 0. Bytes can no longer fail the encode (see
  # `_json_str`), so what is left is python3 not being runnable at all, and the
  # only honest answer to that is to print NOTHING and exit non-zero. Before
  # `_ws_reap_eval`, so a refusal costs no gh call and no fetch.
  _json_str probe >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || die "python3 unavailable — cannot quote the audit record safely"

  _ws_reap_eval "$id" || true      # a refusal is an ANSWER, not an error
  local project workdir branch base repo transcript reaping
  project=$(_reg_get "$id" project); workdir=$(_reg_get "$id" workdir)
  branch=$(_reg_get "$id" branch);   base=$(_reg_get "$id" base)
  repo=$(_gh_repo_slug "$PROJECTS_ROOT/$project" 2>/dev/null) || repo=""
  transcript=$(_transcript_path "$id") || transcript=""
  reaping=$(_reg_get "$id" reaping)

  # Sensitive-first, then bytes descending. Counts and total bytes are NEVER
  # truncated — the whole judgement this design rests on is the human reading
  # a filename, and a truncated list makes it structurally unavailable.
  #
  # NUL-terminated end to end, and the record is `sensitive\tbytes\tpath`
  # (`_ws_collect_ignored`): the read that fills it is `-z`, so a path may
  # legitimately contain a TAB or a NEWLINE. `printf '%s\n' | sort` splits such
  # a path across two records and an `IFS=$'\t' read -r p b s` on a
  # path-first record shifts every field — measured, `a<TAB>b.log` printed
  # `"bytes":b.log`, which is not JSON. So: `sort -z`, `read -d ''`, and the
  # two fixed-shape fields peeled off the FRONT with `${…%%}`/`${…#}` rather
  # than by word-splitting, which would collapse a run of tabs.
  local ign_json="[" first=1 total=0 count=0 rec rest p b s
  if (( ${#REAP_IGNORED[@]} )); then
    while IFS= read -r -d '' rec; do
      s="${rec%%$'\t'*}"; rest="${rec#*$'\t'}"
      b="${rest%%$'\t'*}"; p="${rest#*$'\t'}"
      # MUTATION SURVIVOR, disclosed: `[[ -n "$p" ]] || continue` is removable
      # with the suite green, and always will be — REAP_IGNORED's records are
      # built by _ws_collect_ignored, whose own `[[ -n "$p" ]]` (disclosed
      # there) already refuses an empty path, and `read -d ''` cannot produce
      # an empty record from `printf '%s\0'` over a non-empty array. Same
      # reasoning as the `$dl` sibling below; kept as defence in depth against
      # a future producer. (Gate finding N8.)
      [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
      (( first )) || ign_json+=","; first=0
      ign_json+="{\"path\":$(_json_str "$p"),\"bytes\":$b,\"sensitive\":$( ((s)) && echo true || echo false)}"
      total=$(( total + b )); count=$(( count + 1 ))
    done < <(printf '%s\0' "${REAP_IGNORED[@]}" | sort -z -t$'\t' -k1,1nr -k2,2nr)
  fi
  ign_json+="]"

  local sens_json="[" sfirst=1 sp
  for sp in "${REAP_SENSITIVE[@]-}"; do
    [[ -n "$sp" ]] || continue
    (( sfirst )) || sens_json+=","; sfirst=0
    sens_json+="$(_json_str "$sp")"
  done
  sens_json+="]"

  # `-z` HERE TOO, for the reason the ignored list has it: this array is read by
  # the same human, in the same document, before the same irreversible action,
  # and without `-z` git C-QUOTES the same five classes of byte — measured, a
  # dirty `déjà vu.txt` rendered `"?? \"d\\303\\251j\\303\\240 vu.txt\""` beside
  # an `ignored` array already carrying raw paths. No guard reads this array
  # (`dirty-tree` refuses on `REAP_DIRTY`, a count from `_ws_reap_eval`'s own
  # read), so nothing here decides anything; the whole judgement this design
  # rests on is a human reading a filename, and `\303\251` is not one.
  #
  # A pipe rather than a temp file: process substitution is a PIPE, so the NULs
  # survive it — it is `$(…)` that drops them, which is why the collector needs
  # a file and this does not. And `-c core.quotePath=false` is deliberately NOT
  # repeated here: `_ws_collect_ignored` records it as a measured NO-OP beside
  # `-z`, and a second copy would be a second line no fixture can pin.
  #
  # A RENAME OR COPY IS TWO RECORDS, `XY <to>NUL<from>NUL`, where the non-`-z`
  # form printed one `R  <from> -> <to>` line — so the second is consumed here
  # and rejoined into that line. Unpaired it would join the list as an entry
  # with no status letters: a bare filename, in exactly the list a human is
  # asked to read. The letter is in the X column: measured on git 2.43, a
  # worktree-only rename is not detected at all (` D` plus `??`) and only an
  # INDEX rename produces the two-path form. `C` is not dead weight beside `R`:
  # it needs `status.renames=copies` AND a modified source (git's copy detection
  # only looks at sources that changed in the same diff, and status has no
  # `--find-copies-harder`), and both halves are in a fixture.
  #
  # MUTATION SURVIVOR, disclosed and measured: `[[ -n "$dl" ]] || continue` is
  # removable with the suite green. Under `-z` git's output ends in a NUL and
  # never contains two in a row, so `read -d ''` cannot produce an empty record
  # — it hits EOF and ends the loop instead. Kept for the reason the identical
  # line in `_ws_collect_ignored` is kept: the next statement indexes `$dl`
  # positionally, and an empty record would put `""` into the one list this
  # design asks a human to read filenames out of.
  local dirty_json="[" dfirst=1 dl dsrc
  if [[ -d "$workdir" ]]; then
    while IFS= read -r -d '' dl; do
      [[ -n "$dl" ]] || continue
      case "$dl" in
        [RC]*) IFS= read -r -d '' dsrc && dl="${dl:0:3}$dsrc -> ${dl:3}" ;;
      esac
      (( dfirst )) || dirty_json+=","; dfirst=0
      dirty_json+="$(_json_str "$dl")"
    done < <(git -C "$workdir" status --porcelain -z 2>/dev/null)
  fi
  dirty_json+="]"

  local exists=false headmatch=false ahead=0 bytes=0
  [[ -d "$workdir" ]] && exists=true
  [[ -n "$REAP_WTHEAD" && "$REAP_WTHEAD" == "$branch" ]] && headmatch=true
  if [[ -n "$branch" ]] && git -C "$PROJECTS_ROOT/$project" rev-parse --verify --quiet "$base" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ahead=$(git -C "$PROJECTS_ROOT/$project" rev-list --count "$base..refs/heads/$branch" 2>/dev/null)
    [[ "$ahead" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || ahead=0
  fi
  # Pre-merge fix round, finding F: `null`, never a fabricated `0` — the same
  # rule `_ws_archive_manifest` (ccd:1190) already carries, applied here where
  # `_ws_gc_bytes`'s own fix (ccd:3201) actually closes the gap. This is the
  # figure `ReapSheet.tsx`'s primary Remove button prints beside "Remove
  # <slug> ·" — the one confirm the whole design exists to protect — so a
  # `du` that could not fully measure the tree must say so rather than hand
  # the sheet a plausible-looking lie. `WsAudit.worktreeBytes` is `number |
  # null` on the wire for exactly this reason (shared/api.ts).
  bytes=$(_ws_gc_bytes "$workdir"); [[ "$bytes" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || bytes=null

  printf '{"id":%s,"branch":%s,"base":%s,"workdir":%s,"project":%s,"repo":%s,' \
    "$(_json_str "$id")" "$(_json_str "$branch")" "$(_json_str "$base")" \
    "$(_json_str "$workdir")" "$(_json_str "$project")" "$(_json_str "$repo")"
  printf '"exists":%s,"headMatchesRegistry":%s,"reaping":%s,' \
    "$exists" "$headmatch" "$( [[ -n "$reaping" ]] && _json_str "$reaping" || echo null)"
  printf '"dirty":%s,"ignored":%s,"ignoredCount":%s,"ignoredBytes":%s,"sensitive":%s,"sensitiveFiltered":%s,' \
    "$dirty_json" "$ign_json" "$count" "$total" "$sens_json" "${REAP_SENSITIVE_FILTERED:-0}"
  # `clips` on the wire, because the sheet cannot ask a human to consent to a
  # deletion it does not list. `_ws_clip_manifest` is the same producer the
  # tombstone and the fingerprint use, and it is called HERE rather than read
  # from a variable so the field is present on every verdict — a refusal is the
  # answer a human reads too.
  printf '"clips":%s,"stashes":%s,"worktreeBytes":%s,"commitsAheadOfBase":%s,' \
    "$(_ws_clip_manifest "$id")" "$REAP_STASHES" "$bytes" "$ahead"
  printf '"pr":{"number":%s,"url":%s,"mergeCommit":%s,"headRefOid":%s},' \
    "$( [[ "$REAP_PRNUM" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && echo "$REAP_PRNUM" || echo null)" \
    "$(_json_str "$REAP_PRURL")" "$(_json_str "$REAP_MERGE")" "$(_json_str "$REAP_HEADOID")"
  printf '"merge":{"proof":%s,"fetchedAt":%s},"transcript":%s,' \
    "$( [[ -n "$REAP_PROOF" ]] && _json_str "$REAP_PROOF" || echo null)" \
    "$REAP_FETCHED" "$(_json_str "$transcript")"
  # Three verdicts, not two, and the third one is why: `reapable` MEANS a token.
  #
  # `token` is present ONLY when the verdict is reapable AND the tree was
  # actually read. The second half is not a belt-and-braces restatement of the
  # first: with the worktree gone and a `reaping` breadcrumb explaining why,
  # `_ws_reap_eval` skips the whole of Phase B on purpose — that is the RESUME
  # of a killed reap, and refusing it would strand the workspace half-deleted
  # forever — so it reaches `reapable` with `REAP_DIRTY=0`, `REAP_IGNDIGEST=""`,
  # `REAP_SENSITIVE=()` and `REAP_WTHEAD=""` straight out of `_ws_reap_reset`.
  # Those are the reset defaults, not measurements, and `dirty-tree` and
  # `sensitive-ignored` — the two guards §7 forbids overriding — were never
  # evaluated at all. A fingerprint over them is deviation 6's digest forgery
  # with more fields: ws-reap recomputes the same unmeasured values and the
  # consent check matches, so the token would certify a tree nobody ever looked
  # at. The audit therefore reports the state (`exists:false`, `reaping`) and
  # hands out nothing to confirm against; resuming a killed reap is ws-reap's
  # own path, not a token-carrying delete.
  #
  # AND IT MUST NOT SAY `reapable` WHILE DOING SO. Withholding the token from a
  # verdict that still read `reapable` produced a wire shape the sheet
  # mis-renders: `wsaudit.ts` gives `reapable` an EMPTY sentence, `ReapSheet`
  # renders the primary Remove button on `verdict === 'reapable'`, and that
  # button's `confirm()` early-returns when `token === undefined` — a button
  # that silently does nothing, under no explanation at all. Two different
  # states must not share a verdict: this one is `reap-interrupted`, the
  # worktree is already gone, ccrc's own breadcrumb says ccrc removed it, and
  # what is left is a RESUME (`ws-reap --resume`, Task 6), which is not a
  # token-carrying delete and never asks for a confirmation the human cannot
  # give. `_ws_reap_eval` is deliberately untouched: its `reapable` is what the
  # resume path itself depends on.
  if [[ "$REAP_VERDICT" == reapable && "$exists" == true ]]; then
    printf '"verdict":"reapable","detail":"","token":%s}\n' "$(_json_str "$REAP_TOKEN")"
  elif [[ "$REAP_VERDICT" == reapable ]]; then
    printf '"verdict":"reap-interrupted","detail":%s}\n' \
      "$(_json_str "a previous removal stopped after the ${reaping:-worktree} step and left no worktree to inspect")"
  else
    printf '"verdict":%s,"detail":%s}\n' "$(_json_str "$REAP_VERDICT")" "$(_json_str "$REAP_DETAIL")"
  fi
}
```

### Task 6: `ccd ws-reap` — the only destructive verb

**Files:**
- Modify: `infra/<server-host>-portability/ccd` — `cmd_ws_reap` and its tail
  helpers after `cmd_ws_audit`; `cmd_caps`; dispatcher
- Test: **Create** `infra/ccrc/server/test/ccd-ws-reap.test.ts`
  (uses `makeGhRepo` — Task 3 Step 1 — and `CFG_DIR` from `ccdPrHelpers.ts`)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `_ws_reap_eval`, `_ws_reap_reset`, `_ws_collect_ignored`, `_ws_status`
  (the resume path re-proves Phase D1 itself) and every global they set.
- Produces: `ccd ws-reap --expect <64hex> --session <id>` →
  `{"reaped":…,"branch":…,"pr":42,"proof":"patch-id","tombstone":…,"attic":17,"bytes":…}`
  on success, `{"refused":"<token>","detail":…,"paths":[…]}` **on stdout with
  exit 0** on refusal. Writes `$HOME/.cc-sessions/.reaped/<id>.json` and
  `refs/ccrc/attic/<id>/<sha>` refs.

**Context.** REFUSE FIRST, TEAR DOWN SECOND — ccd's own doctrine (ccd:334). A
refusal is an answer, not an error. `--expect` is load-bearing: the whitelist
pins `['ws-reap','--expect']`, so an unconfirmed reap cannot cross the wire at
all, and the token is a fingerprint of the world state a human was shown — any
drift refuses `state-changed`. It is an anti-staleness device, not an
authentication one: forging it requires knowing the exact current state, and if
that state satisfies every independently re-checked guard the reap was
legitimate anyway.

**With one exception, and it is stated here rather than discovered later: the
RESUME path does not compare `--expect` at all.** The argv still requires a
shape-valid 64-hex string, so the verb cannot be spelled without one, but
nothing on that path compares it — because there is nothing to compare it to.
The token is `_ws_reap_eval`'s, built from thirteen facts Phase B and Phase C
measured, and on a resume the worktree is usually already gone: Phase B has no
tree left to read, and Phase C would need a `gh` read an outage could withhold
for ever, which is the wedge §5.6 exists to end. `cmd_ws_audit` says the same
thing from the other side by refusing to ISSUE a token for `reap-interrupted`,
and a token nobody can obtain cannot be the boundary. What stands in its place
is the TOMBSTONE — which exists only because a token-carrying reap was
authorised, and whose `tip` is re-validated against the live ref per phase —
plus a full re-proof of Phase B and Phase D1, the two whose facts can still
change in the gap. What is accepted is that a second human holding any 64-hex
string can FINISH a cleanup a first human authorised, never start one.

`git branch -D` appears nowhere. `git branch -d` is not relied on in either
direction: it refuses on a squash merge even when the work is byte-identically
in main, and it *succeeds* when the branch merely equals its upstream. Since
mergedness is proven independently and the attic already holds every sha, the
branch is deleted with a compare-and-swap that aborts if the ref moved.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

Create `infra/ccrc/server/test/ccd-ws-reap.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { CCD, WS_ADD, ghContainedEnv } from './ccdWsHelpers.js';
import { CFG_DIR, GH_STUB, makePrHarness, mergedRow, type PrHarness } from './ccdPrHelpers.js';

let h: PrHarness;
beforeEach(() => { h = makePrHarness('ccrc-ccd-audit-'); });
afterEach(() => { h.cleanup(); });

const ARCH = `_ws_unsupervise() { :; }; _ws_supervise() { :; }; _spawn() { :; };
  tmux() { return 1; }; _alive() { return 1; };`;

interface Built { main: string; wt: string; tip: string; merge: string }

/**
 * A GENUINE SQUASH MERGE WITH A MOVED BASE — the case the whole ladder exists
 * for, and the first thing the definition of done names. main gains an
 * unrelated commit after the branch is cut, then the branch's three commits
 * land on main as one squashed commit. `ancestor` says no; `tree` says no
 * (the base moved); `patch-id` is what passes.
 *
 * `makeGhRepo` is mandatory here: Phase C refuses `no-remote` before the
 * ladder is ever reached against `makeRepo`'s local-path origin, and its
 * `insteadOf` rewrite is what keeps `_ws_reap_eval`'s mandatory
 * `git fetch origin` off the network.
 *
 * `ignore` writes a `.gitignore` INTO THE MERGED WORK — into the branch's
 * commits and into main's squash of them, so both sides carry it and the
 * patch-ids still match. It is a parameter rather than three lines in each
 * caller because the obvious alternative is wrong in a way that hides itself:
 * committing `.gitignore` to the branch AFTER the squash landed adds a commit
 * that is genuinely not in the merge, so the ladder refuses `tree-differs`
 * before any question about ignored content is reached. Measured: the
 * `LISTS non-sensitive ignored content` case failed outright that way, and
 * `changes the token when ANY fingerprinted fact moves` PASSED — vacuously,
 * comparing a 64-hex token against the `undefined` a refusal hands out.
 */
function squashMovedBase(ignore: string[] = []): Built {
  const main = h.makeGhRepo('demo');
  h.sh(`${WS_ADD} CCD_WS_SLUG=quiet-basin cmd_ws_add demo`);
  const wt = path.join(h.home, 'worktrees', 'demo', 'quiet-basin');
  for (const n of ['1', '2', '3']) {
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(wt, `f${n}.txt`), `work ${n}\n`);
    h.git(wt, 'add', `f${n}.txt`);
    h.git(wt, 'commit', '-m', `work ${n}`);
  }
  if (ignore.length) {
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(wt, '.gitignore'), `${ignore.join('\n')}\n`);
    h.git(wt, 'add', '.gitignore');
    h.git(wt, 'commit', '-m', 'ignore');
  }
  const tip = h.git(wt, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD');
  // main moves underneath, THEN the squash lands on top of that.
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(main, 'other.txt'), 'someone else\n');
  h.git(main, 'add', 'other.txt');
  h.git(main, 'commit', '-m', 'unrelated');
  for (const n of ['1', '2', '3']) fs.writeFileSync(path.join(main, `f${n}.txt`), `work ${n}\n`);
  if (ignore.length) fs.writeFileSync(path.join(main, '.gitignore'), `${ignore.join('\n')}\n`);
  h.git(main, 'add', '-A');
  h.git(main, 'commit', '-m', 'squash of the work (#42)');
  const merge = h.git(main, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD');
  h.git(main, 'push', 'origin', 'main');
  h.git(wt, 'push', '-u', 'origin', 'ws/quiet-basin');
  h.ghRows([mergedRow({ headRefOid: tip, mergeCommit: { oid: merge } })]);
  h.sh(`${ARCH} cmd_ws_archive --session demo-quiet-basin`);
  return { main, wt, tip, merge };
}

/**
 * A REBASE MERGE — the fourth rung, and the one no other fixture reaches.
 * main gains an unrelated commit, then the branch's three commits are REPLAYED
 * onto it (`cherry-pick`, i.e. exactly what "Rebase and merge" does) and main
 * ends on the replayed copies. `ancestor` says no (our shas were rewritten);
 * `tree` says no (main carries `other.txt`, our tip does not); `patch-id` says
 * no (`M^1..M` is one commit's worth of diff against our three); `cherry` is
 * what passes, because every one of our commits has a patch-id equivalent in
 * `M`'s history.
 */
function rebaseMerged(): Built {
  const main = h.makeGhRepo('demo');
  h.sh(`${WS_ADD} CCD_WS_SLUG=quiet-basin cmd_ws_add demo`);
  const wt = path.join(h.home, 'worktrees', 'demo', 'quiet-basin');
  for (const n of ['1', '2', '3']) {
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(wt, `f${n}.txt`), `work ${n}\n`);
    h.git(wt, 'add', `f${n}.txt`); h.git(wt, 'commit', '-m', `work ${n}`);
  }
  const tip = h.git(wt, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD');
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(main, 'other.txt'), 'someone else\n');
  h.git(main, 'add', 'other.txt'); h.git(main, 'commit', '-m', 'unrelated');
  // The replay. Same patches, new shas, on a base our tip does not descend
  // from — which is precisely when `cherry` is the only rung left.
  h.git(main, 'cherry-pick', `${tip}~2`, `${tip}~1`, tip);
  const merge = h.git(main, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD');
  h.git(main, 'push', 'origin', 'main');
  h.git(wt, 'push', '-u', 'origin', 'ws/quiet-basin');
  h.ghRows([mergedRow({ headRefOid: tip, mergeCommit: { oid: merge } })]);
  h.sh(`${ARCH} cmd_ws_archive --session demo-quiet-basin`);
  return { main, wt, tip, merge };
}

/** `pre` is sourced BEFORE the verb, which is the only way to fail one specific
 *  git read: every stub in this file shadows a function or a command rather than
 *  patching ccd. */
const audit = (pre = '', id = 'demo-quiet-basin'): Record<string, any> =>
  JSON.parse(h.sh(`${GH_STUB} ${ARCH} ${pre} cmd_ws_audit --session ${id}`));

/**
 * Read EVERY refusal through this. `ws-audit` is read-only, so a verdict that
 * is not `reapable` must leave the worktree on disk — the definition of done
 * names that explicitly ("every negative case asserts the worktree still
 * exists afterwards") and a checklist item is not an executable assertion.
 * It also asserts `token` is absent, because a refusal that still handed out a
 * token would let the very next reap through.
 *
 * The two identity cases that delete the worktree THEMSELVES
 * (`worktree-missing` and the breadcrumb case) call `audit()` directly and say
 * so inline; every other `it` that expects a REFUSAL goes through here — which
 * is why the session id is a parameter: `no-such-session` and
 * `not-a-workspace` are refusals about a DIFFERENT id or a stripped registry,
 * and reaching for `audit()` to say so is exactly how the two of them lost the
 * worktree assertion.
 */
const refusal = (wt: string, pre = '', id = 'demo-quiet-basin'): Record<string, any> => {
  const a = audit(pre, id);
  expect(a.verdict, `expected a refusal, got ${a.verdict}`).not.toBe('reapable');
  expect(a.token, 'a refusal must not hand out a reap token').toBeUndefined();
  expect(fs.existsSync(wt), 'a read-only audit must never remove the worktree').toBe(true);
  return a;
};

describe('the proof ladder', () => {
  it('proves a MULTI-COMMIT SQUASH WITH A MOVED BASE via patch-id', () => {
    // Tree-equality alone holds only when the base did not move between
    // branch point and merge. On a busy repo that is the minority case, and a
    // tree-only design false-refuses almost every real squash — which is
    // exactly what pushes people onto a one-tap unguarded delete.
    squashMovedBase();
    const a = audit();
    expect(a.verdict).toBe('reapable');
    expect(a.merge.proof).toBe('patch-id');
    expect(a.token).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
  });

  it('proves a squash whose base did NOT move via tree equality', () => {
    const main = h.makeGhRepo('demo');
    h.sh(`${WS_ADD} CCD_WS_SLUG=quiet-basin cmd_ws_add demo`);
    const wt = path.join(h.home, 'worktrees', 'demo', 'quiet-basin');
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(wt, 'f.txt'), 'work\n');
    h.git(wt, 'add', 'f.txt'); h.git(wt, 'commit', '-m', 'work');
    const tip = h.git(wt, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD');
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(main, 'f.txt'), 'work\n');
    h.git(main, 'add', '-A'); h.git(main, 'commit', '-m', 'squash');
    const merge = h.git(main, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD');
    h.git(main, 'push', 'origin', 'main'); h.git(wt, 'push', '-u', 'origin', 'ws/quiet-basin');
    h.ghRows([mergedRow({ headRefOid: tip, mergeCommit: { oid: merge } })]);
    h.sh(`${ARCH} cmd_ws_archive --session demo-quiet-basin`);
    expect(audit().merge.proof).toBe('tree');
  });

  it('proves a TRUE merge via ancestor', () => {
    const main = h.makeGhRepo('demo');
    h.sh(`${WS_ADD} CCD_WS_SLUG=quiet-basin cmd_ws_add demo`);
    const wt = path.join(h.home, 'worktrees', 'demo', 'quiet-basin');
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(wt, 'f.txt'), 'work\n');
    h.git(wt, 'add', 'f.txt'); h.git(wt, 'commit', '-m', 'work');
    const tip = h.git(wt, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD');
    h.git(main, 'merge', '--no-ff', '-m', 'Merge PR #42', 'ws/quiet-basin');
    const merge = h.git(main, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD');
    h.git(main, 'push', 'origin', 'main'); h.git(wt, 'push', '-u', 'origin', 'ws/quiet-basin');
    h.ghRows([mergedRow({ headRefOid: tip, mergeCommit: { oid: merge } })]);
    h.sh(`${ARCH} cmd_ws_archive --session demo-quiet-basin`);
    expect(audit().merge.proof).toBe('ancestor');
  });

  it('proves a REBASE MERGE via cherry — the rung nothing else reaches', () => {
    // The fourth rung, and the DoD names it. Every earlier rung must fail
    // here: our shas were rewritten (not an ancestor), main carries
    // `other.txt` that our tip does not (tree differs), and `M^1..M` is one
    // replayed commit against our three (patch-ids differ). If this comes back
    // `ancestor`, the fixture fast-forwarded instead of replaying — read the
    // fixture, do not relax the assertion.
    rebaseMerged();
    const a = audit();
    expect(a.verdict).toBe('reapable');
    expect(a.merge.proof).toBe('cherry');
    expect(a.token).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
  });

  it('REFUSES the control case: squash plus one genuinely unmerged commit', () => {
    // The entire point. All four rungs must reject this, and the sheet must
    // say so rather than offer an override, because there is none.
    const { wt } = squashMovedBase();
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(wt, 'later.txt'), 'not in the merge\n');
    h.git(wt, 'add', 'later.txt');
    h.git(wt, 'commit', '-m', 'a real follow-up');
    h.git(wt, 'push', 'origin', 'ws/quiet-basin');
    const a = refusal(wt);
    expect(a.verdict).toBe('tree-differs');
    expect(a.detail).toContain('later.txt');
  });

  it('never proves patch-id from two EMPTY patch-ids', () => {
    // `[[ -n "$a" && "$a" == "$b" ]]` — the `-n` half, which a whole-diff
    // mutation sweep found deletable with the suite still green. It is
    // reachable, not defensive: `a` is empty exactly when the tip's tree equals
    // its merge base with `M^1`, and `b` is empty exactly when `M` is an empty
    // commit. Both at once and the mutant `[[ "$a" == "$b" ]]` certifies the
    // branch merged because git computed NOTHING about either side.
    //
    // `_ws_merge_proof` is called directly: this is a shape no `squashMovedBase`
    // variant produces, and the ladder is a pure function of three revisions.
    const main = h.makeRepo('demo');
    h.git(main, 'checkout', '-q', '-b', 'side');
    h.git(main, 'commit', '-q', '--allow-empty', '-m', 'empty on the side');
    const tip = h.git(main, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD');
    h.git(main, 'checkout', '-q', 'main');
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(main, 'other.txt'), 'moved\n');
    h.git(main, 'add', 'other.txt'); h.git(main, 'commit', '-m', 'unrelated');
    h.git(main, 'commit', '--allow-empty', '-m', 'empty squash');
    const merge = h.git(main, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD');
    // BOTH halves empty — measured here, because if either stops being empty
    // the fixture stops being about this guard at all.
    const patchId = (from: string, to: string): string => h.sh(
      `git -C "${main}" diff --binary "${from}" "${to}" -- | git -C "${main}" patch-id --stable | cut -d' ' -f1`);
    expect(patchId(h.git(main, 'merge-base', tip, `${merge}^1`), tip)).toBe('');
    expect(patchId(`${merge}^1`, merge)).toBe('');
    // The earlier rungs must both say no, or this proves nothing either.
    expect(h.sh(`git -C "${main}" merge-base --is-ancestor -- "${tip}" "${merge}"; echo "rc=$?"`)).toBe('rc=1');
    expect(h.sh(`git -C "${main}" diff --quiet "${merge}" "${tip}" --; echo "rc=$?"`)).toBe('rc=1');
    // `cherry` is what answers instead, and the assertion is on WHICH rung:
    // with the guard deleted this reports `patch-id`.
    expect(h.sh(`_ws_merge_proof "${main}" "${merge}" "${tip}"; echo "rc=$? proof=$_WS_PROOF"`))
      .toBe('rc=0 proof=cherry');

    // And the OTHER end of the helper, which no fixture that reaches a rung can
    // observe: a call that proves nothing must return 1 with `_WS_PROOF` still
    // EMPTY. Both the reset at the top and the final `return 1` survived a
    // whole-diff sweep for want of exactly this — a caller that read a stale
    // `_WS_PROOF` after a refusal would record the previous workspace's proof.
    h.git(main, 'checkout', '-q', '-b', 'stray');
```
